components.description: Casa Bi-Directional Module, the original 85 MHz card. Carries no RF connectors at all; every port lands on the paired rear 6+12 I/O card. The faceplate is a blank plate with a model band, two tapering stripe groups and three status LEDs, shared with the BDM2 and BDM2m.
components.name: bdm

provenance.depth-known-wrong: THE 380.0 IS NOT MERELY UNMEASURED, IT IS IMPOSSIBLE, and this contract now says so in a field a tool can read - size-confidence: {d: known-wrong}. THE CONSTRAINT. Front and rear cards MEET AT A MIDPLANE, which the owner photographed: working/photos/casa/c40g-empty-midplane.png shows the emptied cage with the card guides and the midplane at the back of it, and the opening where the rear I/O card reaches through to the front card. So a front card and its rear partner have to share the chassis depth - 386.0 on the C100G, 388.45 on the C40G. Two cards at 380.0 need 760, which is not a wide error bar, it is twice the box. WHAT THE SHAPE IS, from the owner: "the front card is mostly rectangular, but the I/O card is kind of L SHAPED where the top part of the top connector PASSES THROUGH THE MIDPLANE and plugs into the front card, and the other one is plugged into the midplane. So they ultimately kind of meet in the middle." So the rear card is a body against the midplane PLUS A TONGUE at the top reaching forward through it. NOTE WHAT THAT DOES AND DOES NOT ALLOW, because the obvious rule is wrong. front + rear CAN exceed the chassis depth, by about the tongue length, because the tongue overlaps the front card at a height where the front card is not - they interleave rather than tile. The constraint is therefore an inequality with slack, not an equality. What it cannot absorb is a 374 mm overlap where a tongue is tens of millimetres. ONE PHOTOGRAPH IS USABLE AND IT IS NOT THIS CARD-FAMILY-WIDE. bdm2m-solder-side.jpeg has the faceplate FULLY IN FRAME, so its 345.5 long axis anchors the scale at 5.00 px/mm; the card measures 1336 px from the faceplate to the top of its midplane connectors. Raw that is 267 mm. The shot is NOT orthographic - the PCB reads 4.66 percent wider at the connector end than at the faceplate end, which is perspective, not a taper - so correcting to the mean scale gives about 261, and taking the card top at the outermost connector edge instead pushes it to about 282. CALL IT 270 PLUS OR MINUS 12 AND DO NOT ROUND THAT AWAY. REJECTED, and the rejection is the useful part: bdm2m-top-plan.jpeg and both qam-io-card plan shots have the faceplate CLIPPED BY THE FRAME, so the 345.5 anchor is truncated and every number off them is understated by an unknown amount. Measured anyway, the top-plan gives 227 mm for the same card the solder side gives 270 - a 19 percent disagreement that is entirely the broken anchor. They are not second opinions and must not be averaged in. NOTHING IS REPLACED. 270 plus or minus 12 is one reading of one card from one photograph that fails gate 1, and stamping it on twelve cards would be the family-number pattern doing harm instead of good - these cards share a FACEPLATE, which is established, not a depth, which is not. What is established is that 380.0 cannot be true. WANTED, in order of how much each unlocks: a tape on any one front card (fixes it outright); a tape on any one rear I/O card; an unclipped side-on photograph of a rear card showing where the tongue begins, which would give the midplane position and both halves at once.
provenance.faceplate-hardware-photo: THE OWNER SUPPLIED AN ISOMETRIC OF THE C100G FRONT and it corrects the SHAPE of two things on this faceplate. working/photos/casa/ - c100g-front-isometric.png and the crop crop-ejectors.png, read at high zoom. WHAT IT SETTLES: - The captive screw is not a flat slotted head. It is a substantial BLACK KNURLED KNOB standing well proud, with a dark top face and a light metallic band. `knurl` is added for that reason - it is a shape fact and costs no dimension. The drawn 2D head is still a slotted circle and is NOT redrawn; the figures draw it that way and this photograph cannot give a true elevation of it. - The EJECTOR LEVER is the most prominent thing on the whole face: a large CURVED BLACK lever, not the rounded strip this skin draws, with a thin vertical linkage rod running down the card from the knob to it. - RELATIVE PROMINENCE, which is the one quantitative thing a perspective view CAN give: lever stands proud of knob stands proud of lamp. This contract already orders them that way - 4.2, 1.6, 0.3 - so the photograph CONFIRMS the ordering rather than correcting it. Only the absolute magnitudes are understated, and it gives no absolute magnitude. WHAT IT DOES NOT SETTLE, and why nothing else moved. It is a three-quarter view: every forward projection is foreshortened by an unknown factor, nothing of known size is in frame, and the one feature that looks measurable - the knob ellipse - needs a diameter nobody has. So it fails gate 1 outright, exactly as the Cisco perspective figures did. THE LEVER SILHOUETTE IS DELIBERATELY NOT REDRAWN: the true elevation outline of a curved lever is precisely what a three-quarter crop cannot give, and drawing sixteen faceplates from it would replace a sourced schematic strip with an invented curve. The 4.2 stays, marked `borrowed`. WANTED, and it closes both at once: ONE STRAIGHT-ON PHOTOGRAPH OF A SINGLE CARD, with a rule or any part of known size in frame. That would give the lever its silhouette AND its projection, and it is the cheapest open question on this family. THIS ENTRY IS ONE READING OF ONE PHOTOGRAPH restated across the thirteen front-slot cards that share this faceplate. The photograph shows DS 8X96, US 16X4 and SMM 8X10G specifically; the rest inherit it because the family shares a plate, which the DS/US positions provenance already establishes to the millimetre. It is NOT thirteen observations. The REAR cards - the 6+12 I/O family, rfd, rfu-16x8, ups-32x4, lc-sw-bdm and the two SMM Switch BDMs - are NOT in this photograph and are deliberately left alone.
provenance.identity: drawing - Table A-10 of the C100G install guide, "BDM 6+12 (BDM with 6+12 IO)". This is the 85 MHz card, the one the docsis-classic configuration ships, and it is what casa/bdm@1 now means. Before the split casa/bdm@1 meant the BDM2m and this variant was reachable only through that configuration's skins override
provenance.layout: drawing - Figure 1-14 of the Casa C100G Hardware Installation Guide (rev 07/08/2022). Three LEDs in a single column with STATUS, ALARM and ACTIVE printed to their right, between two mirrored stripe groups. The BDM, BDM2 and BDM2m are one faceplate; the model band is the only visible difference, which is exactly why they were once one component
provenance.led-column-x: NOT ACTED ON, and this is the gap. The same figure puts the lamp column centre at 0.25221 of the plate width and the label text starting at 0.4336, which anchored to 30.47 would be cx 7.68 and text x 13.21 against the 6.30 and 10.64 drawn here. The vertical fix above is trustworthy because it is anchored to the 345.5 height, which is a dimension the contract already holds; there is no equally trusted width, and the figure's outline aspect is 10 percent off, so an x-fraction off this drawing is the softer number of the two. Left alone deliberately rather than moved on a figure that is known to be wrong about the axis it would be scaled by
provenance.leds: drawing-measured - Figure 1-20 of the C40G Hardware Installation Guide (rev 07/07/2022), "BDM module, SMM Switch BDM A, B, and LC Switch BDM", which draws the BDM, BDM2 and BDM2m side by side. All three plates measure 113 x 1417 px and give IDENTICAL feature fractions, which is what confirms the three share one faceplate. THE FIGURE IS SCHEMATIC IN OUTLINE - its 12.54 aspect is 10 percent off the real 30.47 / 345.5 = 11.34 - SO ONLY PROPORTIONS ARE TAKEN FROM IT, anchored to the 345.5 height this contract already holds. Lamp centres read y 804.5, 822.5 and 837.5 within a plate spanning y 70 to 1486; the figure's own pitch wobbles between 18.0 and 15.0 px, which is a drawing slip of a pixel and a half, so the pitch is the group's span divided evenly: 16.5 px = 0.011644 of the height = 4.02 mm, putting the centres at 196.16, 200.18 and 204.20. THIS REPLACES A 6.6 mm PITCH THAT WAS NEVER MEASURED - it was chosen so the lamps would read as separate indicators, and it pushed the cluster up against the upper stripe group, leaving 1.66 mm of grey above it and 4.44 mm below. The figure puts the cluster in clean grey between the two groups; at 4.02 the margins are 5.42 above and 5.84 below, against the figure's own 6.10 and 5.60. THE 3.0 DIAMETER IS UNCHANGED AND IS STILL NOT MEASURED: the figure's lamp is 12 px tall and 14 px wide, and because the plate outline is anisotropic those scale to 2.93 mm off the height and 3.78 mm off the width. A lamp is round, so neither is the answer, and 3.0 sits between them, so it is carried forward unchanged and UNMEASURED. This contract cannot open a gap for that - gaps are device-level in the schema - so the uncertainty is stated here, alongside the same admission the size entry makes: a caliper on the hardware closes both at once
provenance.ports: drawing - the BDM faceplate has NO connectors. This is not an omission; the architecture puts all RF on the paired rear I/O card
provenance.power: Table A-10 reads "Approximately 300W per BDM", under a title scoping it to the BDM WITH its 6+12 I/O, and the BDM2/BDM2m data sheet's "Total Power 300 W" sits in a table headed "BDM2/2 m with 6+12 IO Card". So the figure is the pair's, and `power-draw-scope: module-with-paired-io` says so in DATA rather than in this sentence. A BDM position is two modelled modules - this card in a front bay and casa/io-6p12 in the paired rear bay - and no document divides the 300 W between them, so a chassis sum must not add the rear module as well. Both vendor statements say "approximately"
provenance.relief: THE C100G/C40G CARD FAMILY RELIEF. This entry is written in full HERE and every other Casa card points at it; the short entries in those files say so and name this one, so nobody reads eleven files and mistakes one decision for eleven agreeing readings. WHAT IS ON A CASA CARD FACE, and this part IS sourced: two captive slotted screws on the centreline and an ejector latch strip at one edge, drawn in Figures 1-11, 1-12, 1-14, 1-15 and 1-16 of both guides and named in the text - "remove using the integrated thumbscrews", "screw down its captive screws", and the latch strip the rear-card entries already call an ejector latch. Where a card has lamps, the figure names them (STATUS / ALARM / ACTIVE, or per-port pairs). So which nodes stand off the plate, and what each one IS, comes off the figures. HOW FAR NONE OF THEM STAND IS PUBLISHED. Neither guide, neither datasheet set and no appendix table carries a Z dimension for any card feature; searched both guides for "thumbscrew", "captive", "latch", "ejector", "LED" and Appendix A. Every card figure also fails the orthographic gate - Figure 1-11 renders its plate 15 percent narrow - so no fraction off one would be worth taking even if depth were visible in an elevation, which it is not. SO THREE NUMBERS ARE USED, ONE PER KIND OF THING, AND NONE OF THE THREE IS A MEASUREMENT. Each is the library's single existing figure for that hardware, reused so the library carries ONE number per kind rather than nineteen: cyl 1.6  captive panel screw   = edgecore/agr-panel-screw@1 out 4.2  ejector latch         = edgecore/agr-psu-dc@1 dome 0.3 panel lamp            = common/led-dot@1 CORRECTED. An earlier version of this entry called the 4.2 "measured off real hardware" and tokened all three `borrowed`, which in this library means the ORIGIN was measured. Going and reading the three origin contracts shows none of them was: agr-panel-screw says "estimated - it stands proud but was not measured"; agr-psu-dc's only measured figure is the MODULE's 360.7 mm depth and its latch height is sourced nowhere; common/led-dot carries no depth provenance at all, only size: estimated. All three are now tokened `estimated` and each feature's `source` names the origin AND says it is not a measurement. Found by cisco-relief, which went to read the origins in order to cite them precisely - the check this contract should have run when it wrote the citation. THE REUSE IS STILL THE RIGHT DESIGN and nothing about it changes: one number per kind of hardware, the link recorded, and one caliper on any panel screw anywhere in the library fixing every screw in it. What went is only the claim that somebody had already held that caliper. They are ESTIMATES. Applying one estimate to a family is a deliberate choice and it is the honest one HERE, because these cards genuinely share a faceplate - the DQM/DCU positions entry already records that the BDM and the DS/US cards are ONE plate to the millimetre. What must not be read into it is corroboration: eleven cards carrying 4.2 is ONE estimate written eleven times. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: a caliper on any one C100G or C40G card. One measurement fixes the whole family, which is the other reason to keep the family on one number.
provenance.size: ESTIMATED, shared with casa/io-6p12 - the six faceplates in Fig 1-14 measure 196 x 2610 px against that card's 197 x 2613, so the whole family shares one envelope. The guide figures are schematic rather than to scale, so the absolute numbers come from Table A-1 arithmetic. Needs a caliper
provenance.variants: THREE PRODUCTS, ONE FACEPLATE, and they are now three components. casa/bdm@1 used to be all of them at once: it carried attrs model BDM2m while its own description said "BDM, BDM2 and BDM2m share it and differ only by label", and the plain BDM was reachable only as a skin override inside the docsis-classic configuration. A reader could not tell which product was in a slot, and no bay could offer a choice. They are split because the guides differentiate them on a real specification, not just a label: Table A-10 ("BDM 6+12 (BDM with 6+12 IO)") gives upstream "Up to 85 MHz with 1 OFDMA and 6 ATDMA channels", while Table A-11 ("BDM 6+12 (BDM_204MHZ and BDM2m_204MHZ with 6+12 IO2)") gives "Up to 204 MHz" - different upstream capability AND a different paired rear I/O card. The BDM2/BDM2m data sheet (BDM2_BDM2m_DS_RevA, 12-2024) separates the last two: "BDM2m provides identical capabilities as the BDM2 card but uses a different packet processor", the same distinction CommScope draws between the SMM300G and SMM300Gm

components.description: Casa Bi-Directional Module 2m (BDM2m_204MHZ), the high-split 204 MHz card with the newer packet processor. Carries no RF connectors at all; every port lands on the paired rear 6+12 IO2 card. Faceplate shared with the BDM and BDM2.

provenance.depth-known-wrong: THE 380.0 IS NOT MERELY UNMEASURED, IT IS IMPOSSIBLE, and this contract now says so in a field a tool can read - size-confidence: {d: known-wrong}. THE CONSTRAINT. Front and rear cards MEET AT A MIDPLANE, which the owner photographed: working/photos/casa/c40g-empty-midplane.png shows the emptied cage with the card guides and the midplane at the back of it, and the opening where the rear I/O card reaches through to the front card. So a front card and its rear partner have to share the chassis depth - 386.0 on the C100G, 388.45 on the C40G. Two cards at 380.0 need 760, which is not a wide error bar, it is twice the box. WHAT THE SHAPE IS, from the owner: "the front card is mostly rectangular, but the I/O card is kind of L SHAPED where the top part of the top connector PASSES THROUGH THE MIDPLANE and plugs into the front card, and the other one is plugged into the midplane. So they ultimately kind of meet in the middle." So the rear card is a body against the midplane PLUS A TONGUE at the top reaching forward through it. NOTE WHAT THAT DOES AND DOES NOT ALLOW, because the obvious rule is wrong. front + rear CAN exceed the chassis depth, by about the tongue length, because the tongue overlaps the front card at a height where the front card is not - they interleave rather than tile. The constraint is therefore an inequality with slack, not an equality. What it cannot absorb is a 374 mm overlap where a tongue is tens of millimetres. ONE PHOTOGRAPH IS USABLE AND IT IS NOT THIS CARD-FAMILY-WIDE. bdm2m-solder-side.jpeg has the faceplate FULLY IN FRAME, so its 345.5 long axis anchors the scale at 5.00 px/mm; the card measures 1336 px from the faceplate to the top of its midplane connectors. Raw that is 267 mm. The shot is NOT orthographic - the PCB reads 4.66 percent wider at the connector end than at the faceplate end, which is perspective, not a taper - so correcting to the mean scale gives about 261, and taking the card top at the outermost connector edge instead pushes it to about 282. CALL IT 270 PLUS OR MINUS 12 AND DO NOT ROUND THAT AWAY. REJECTED, and the rejection is the useful part: bdm2m-top-plan.jpeg and both qam-io-card plan shots have the faceplate CLIPPED BY THE FRAME, so the 345.5 anchor is truncated and every number off them is understated by an unknown amount. Measured anyway, the top-plan gives 227 mm for the same card the solder side gives 270 - a 19 percent disagreement that is entirely the broken anchor. They are not second opinions and must not be averaged in. NOTHING IS REPLACED. 270 plus or minus 12 is one reading of one card from one photograph that fails gate 1, and stamping it on twelve cards would be the family-number pattern doing harm instead of good - these cards share a FACEPLATE, which is established, not a depth, which is not. What is established is that 380.0 cannot be true. WANTED, in order of how much each unlocks: a tape on any one front card (fixes it outright); a tape on any one rear I/O card; an unclipped side-on photograph of a rear card showing where the tongue begins, which would give the midplane position and both halves at once.
provenance.faceplate-hardware-photo: THE OWNER SUPPLIED AN ISOMETRIC OF THE C100G FRONT and it corrects the SHAPE of two things on this faceplate. working/photos/casa/ - c100g-front-isometric.png and the crop crop-ejectors.png, read at high zoom. WHAT IT SETTLES: - The captive screw is not a flat slotted head. It is a substantial BLACK KNURLED KNOB standing well proud, with a dark top face and a light metallic band. `knurl` is added for that reason - it is a shape fact and costs no dimension. The drawn 2D head is still a slotted circle and is NOT redrawn; the figures draw it that way and this photograph cannot give a true elevation of it. - The EJECTOR LEVER is the most prominent thing on the whole face: a large CURVED BLACK lever, not the rounded strip this skin draws, with a thin vertical linkage rod running down the card from the knob to it. - RELATIVE PROMINENCE, which is the one quantitative thing a perspective view CAN give: lever stands proud of knob stands proud of lamp. This contract already orders them that way - 4.2, 1.6, 0.3 - so the photograph CONFIRMS the ordering rather than correcting it. Only the absolute magnitudes are understated, and it gives no absolute magnitude. WHAT IT DOES NOT SETTLE, and why nothing else moved. It is a three-quarter view: every forward projection is foreshortened by an unknown factor, nothing of known size is in frame, and the one feature that looks measurable - the knob ellipse - needs a diameter nobody has. So it fails gate 1 outright, exactly as the Cisco perspective figures did. THE LEVER SILHOUETTE IS DELIBERATELY NOT REDRAWN: the true elevation outline of a curved lever is precisely what a three-quarter crop cannot give, and drawing sixteen faceplates from it would replace a sourced schematic strip with an invented curve. The 4.2 stays, marked `borrowed`. WANTED, and it closes both at once: ONE STRAIGHT-ON PHOTOGRAPH OF A SINGLE CARD, with a rule or any part of known size in frame. That would give the lever its silhouette AND its projection, and it is the cheapest open question on this family. THIS ENTRY IS ONE READING OF ONE PHOTOGRAPH restated across the thirteen front-slot cards that share this faceplate. The photograph shows DS 8X96, US 16X4 and SMM 8X10G specifically; the rest inherit it because the family shares a plate, which the DS/US positions provenance already establishes to the millimetre. It is NOT thirteen observations. The REAR cards - the 6+12 I/O family, rfd, rfu-16x8, ups-32x4, lc-sw-bdm and the two SMM Switch BDMs - are NOT in this photograph and are deliberately left alone.
provenance.identity: drawing - Table A-11 of the C100G install guide plus the BDM2/BDM2m data sheet (12-2024), which says "BDM2m provides identical capabilities as the BDM2 card but uses a different packet processor". Ordering codes BDM2M-W (Wide Open) and BDM2M-N (No License). This is what casa/bdm@1 used to resolve to, so every bay default and configuration that meant a BDM2m now names this component instead
provenance.layout: drawing - Figure 1-14 of the Casa C100G Hardware Installation Guide (rev 07/08/2022). Three LEDs in a single column with STATUS, ALARM and ACTIVE printed to their right, between two mirrored stripe groups. The BDM, BDM2 and BDM2m are one faceplate; the model band is the only visible difference, which is exactly why they were once one component
provenance.led-column-x: NOT ACTED ON, and this is the gap. The same figure puts the lamp column centre at 0.25221 of the plate width and the label text starting at 0.4336, which anchored to 30.47 would be cx 7.68 and text x 13.21 against the 6.30 and 10.64 drawn here. The vertical fix above is trustworthy because it is anchored to the 345.5 height, which is a dimension the contract already holds; there is no equally trusted width, and the figure's outline aspect is 10 percent off, so an x-fraction off this drawing is the softer number of the two. Left alone deliberately rather than moved on a figure that is known to be wrong about the axis it would be scaled by
provenance.leds: drawing-measured - Figure 1-20 of the C40G Hardware Installation Guide (rev 07/07/2022), "BDM module, SMM Switch BDM A, B, and LC Switch BDM", which draws the BDM, BDM2 and BDM2m side by side. All three plates measure 113 x 1417 px and give IDENTICAL feature fractions, which is what confirms the three share one faceplate. THE FIGURE IS SCHEMATIC IN OUTLINE - its 12.54 aspect is 10 percent off the real 30.47 / 345.5 = 11.34 - SO ONLY PROPORTIONS ARE TAKEN FROM IT, anchored to the 345.5 height this contract already holds. Lamp centres read y 804.5, 822.5 and 837.5 within a plate spanning y 70 to 1486; the figure's own pitch wobbles between 18.0 and 15.0 px, which is a drawing slip of a pixel and a half, so the pitch is the group's span divided evenly: 16.5 px = 0.011644 of the height = 4.02 mm, putting the centres at 196.16, 200.18 and 204.20. THIS REPLACES A 6.6 mm PITCH THAT WAS NEVER MEASURED - it was chosen so the lamps would read as separate indicators, and it pushed the cluster up against the upper stripe group, leaving 1.66 mm of grey above it and 4.44 mm below. The figure puts the cluster in clean grey between the two groups; at 4.02 the margins are 5.42 above and 5.84 below, against the figure's own 6.10 and 5.60. THE 3.0 DIAMETER IS UNCHANGED AND IS STILL NOT MEASURED: the figure's lamp is 12 px tall and 14 px wide, and because the plate outline is anisotropic those scale to 2.93 mm off the height and 3.78 mm off the width. A lamp is round, so neither is the answer, and 3.0 sits between them, so it is carried forward unchanged and UNMEASURED. This contract cannot open a gap for that - gaps are device-level in the schema - so the uncertainty is stated here, alongside the same admission the size entry makes: a caliper on the hardware closes both at once
provenance.ports: drawing - the BDM faceplate has NO connectors. This is not an omission; the architecture puts all RF on the paired rear I/O card
provenance.power: Table A-11 reads "Approximately 300W per BDM2m_204MHZ", under a title scoping it to the BDM WITH its 6+12 I/O, and the BDM2/BDM2m data sheet's "Total Power 300 W" sits in a table headed "BDM2/2 m with 6+12 IO Card". So the figure is the pair's, and `power-draw-scope: module-with-paired-io` says so in DATA rather than in this sentence. A BDM position is two modelled modules - this card in a front bay and casa/io-6p12 in the paired rear bay - and no document divides the 300 W between them, so a chassis sum must not add the rear module as well. Both vendor statements say "approximately"
provenance.relief: the C100G/C40G card family treatment - two captive screws (cyl 1.6), the ejector latch strip (out 4.2) and the 3 status lamps (dome 0.3). THE FULL ARGUMENT IS IN casa/bdm@1 AND THIS IS A POINTER TO IT, not a second reading: the three magnitudes are one estimate per kind of hardware, taken from edgecore/agr-panel-screw@1, edgecore/agr-psu-dc@1 and common/led-dot@1 - NONE of which measured them, which is why all three are tokened `estimated` rather than `borrowed` - applied across the family because these cards share a faceplate. No Casa document states a depth for any of them. Eleven cards carrying 4.2 is ONE estimate written eleven times, not eleven readings that agreed.
provenance.size: ESTIMATED, shared with casa/io-6p12 - the six faceplates in Fig 1-14 measure 196 x 2610 px against that card's 197 x 2613, so the whole family shares one envelope. The guide figures are schematic rather than to scale, so the absolute numbers come from Table A-1 arithmetic. Needs a caliper
provenance.variants: THREE PRODUCTS, ONE FACEPLATE, and they are now three components. casa/bdm@1 used to be all of them at once: it carried attrs model BDM2m while its own description said "BDM, BDM2 and BDM2m share it and differ only by label", and the plain BDM was reachable only as a skin override inside the docsis-classic configuration. A reader could not tell which product was in a slot, and no bay could offer a choice. They are split because the guides differentiate them on a real specification, not just a label: Table A-10 ("BDM 6+12 (BDM with 6+12 IO)") gives upstream "Up to 85 MHz with 1 OFDMA and 6 ATDMA channels", while Table A-11 ("BDM 6+12 (BDM_204MHZ and BDM2m_204MHZ with 6+12 IO2)") gives "Up to 204 MHz" - different upstream capability AND a different paired rear I/O card. The BDM2/BDM2m data sheet (BDM2_BDM2m_DS_RevA, 12-2024) separates the last two: "BDM2m provides identical capabilities as the BDM2 card but uses a different packet processor", the same distinction CommScope draws between the SMM300G and SMM300Gm

components.description: Casa blank face plate for an unpopulated C100G or C40G card slot. A plain plate with two captive thumbscrews and nothing else. It is a functional part, not trim - it keeps the cooling airflow channelled through the chassis, and the guide is explicit that running a slot open makes components "excessively warm or even overheat". An empty bay in a real chassis has one of these in it.
components.name: blank-faceplate

provenance.fits: drawing - one part, both faces, because nothing in either guide distinguishes a front blank from a rear one. Front and rear slots share the 30.47 x 345.5 envelope, both guides use the same wording for both, and the C40G is the only place either guide places blanks by slot number - "Rear slots (non-redundant system) - Blank filler plates: 2, 3", which are rear slots. If the real part differs front to rear, this is the assumption to break first
provenance.part-number: NONE - and that is a finding, not an omission. Neither guide gives this part a number, an order code or a figure. It is referred to only by description - "blank face plates", "blank cover", "blank filler plates" - across four separate procedures. No number is invented here. Anyone holding the hardware can close this by reading the label
provenance.purpose: drawing - both hardware installation guides describe it and why it matters. C100G: "For any unpopulated chassis slots, the C100G CMTS comes equipped with blank face plates that you can easily remove using the integrated thumbscrews. The blank face plates are necessary to ensure system cooling by keeping the airflow properly channeled through the chassis. If these face plates are removed, the cooling airflow will escape prematurely, causing system components to become excessively warm or even overheat." The C40G carries the same paragraph. The line-card replacement procedure closes with "Otherwise, install a blank cover over the slot and screw down its captive screws to complete this procedure"
provenance.relief: the C100G/C40G card family treatment - two captive screws (cyl 1.6), the ejector latch strip (out 4.2). THE FULL ARGUMENT IS IN casa/bdm@1 AND THIS IS A POINTER TO IT, not a second reading: the magnitudes are one estimate per kind of hardware, taken from edgecore/agr-panel-screw@1 for a screw head, applied across the family because these cards share a faceplate. No Casa document states a depth for any of them. Eleven cards carrying 4.2 is ONE estimate written eleven times, not eleven readings that agreed. NOTE this card has NO LAMPS, so the family's dome figure is deliberately not cited here - citing a source for a number a file does not carry is how an inert wrong claim gets started. A blank has no latch and no lamp, so it takes the two screws and nothing else - which is the whole point of the part.
provenance.screws: drawing - two captive screws, at the family positions casa/bdm and casa/smm-8x10g use. The guides call them both "integrated thumbscrews" and "captive screws" and say a flat-tip screwdriver removes them, so they are drawn as the same slotted captive screw the cards carry
provenance.size: shared with the rest of the front-card family, taken from the chassis slot envelope (30.47 x 345.5). The depth is a guess at plate-plus-flange and is deliberately shallow - a blank has no body behind the face

components.description: The curved moulding on the C100G front bezel, between the casa systems mark and the model name. A closed lens-shaped outline, not a filled graphic.
components.name: brand-swoop

provenance.extent: drawing - 48.66 to 162.13 across and 4.62 to 24.08 down in his frame, mapped fractionally onto our 432.95 x 571 body
provenance.path: drawing - Jason's hand-built front SVG, `swoop`. Its nested transforms were not composed by hand; the path was SAMPLED at 160 points along its length through the browser CTM and decimated to 80, so the curve here is the measured curve rather than a redrawn approximation
provenance.relief: the 1.0 mm depth was compiling to a 258.3 x 40.5 RECTANGULAR PIT, which is not what a moulded groove is. `size.d` on anything that is not kind: module becomes data-depth, and the 3D viewer reads data-depth as a cavity to look into, taking its cross-section from the component's bounding box unless a `cavity` node says otherwise. So the whole band was a shallow tray. `relief.cavity: swoop` fixes it without touching a single number: the recess is now shape-punched from the swoop path's own art, which is the closed stroked outline the style entry above describes, so the groove has the shape of the groove. The depth is unchanged and still ESTIMATED - Jason's source is a 2D path and states no depth - and 1.0 mm is what this file has always carried. A groove is the right primitive here rather than a protrusion: the style entry settles it - "a moulded groove reads as an outline, a printed graphic would not".
provenance.style: drawing - his path is closed, fill none, stroked 0.72 in a 190.26-wide frame, which is 1.64 here. Drawn as an outline because that is what the source is - a moulded groove reads as an outline, a printed graphic would not

components.description: Casa C40G AC input panel - the bolted panel across the bottom of the REAR face on an AC chassis, where a DC chassis carries its two power entry modules. One continuous panel, not four module ends: it carries a rocker ON/OFF switch and an IEC C14 inlet for each of the four front-loaded PSUs, with vent mesh above and below.
components.name: c40g-ac-inlet-panel

provenance.NOT-PLACED: THIS COMPONENT IS BUILT BUT NOT PLACED ON THE C40G, and that is a format limitation rather than an oversight. It belongs on the rear face ONLY in the ac-power configuration, and there is no way to say that: a configuration can carry bays, skins, airflow, region-context and part-numbers, but not placements, so a bolted panel cannot be switched per configuration. Making it a BAY instead would overlap the two PEM bays that occupy the same band, which L13 rejects - and unlike a placement, a bay cannot use `for:` to declare the overlap legitimate, because L13 builds its owned-set from placements only. Marking it `optional:` would hide it everywhere, since build.sh emits no --with variants. So it is measured, recorded and ready for whoever adds config-scoped placements
provenance.inlets: composed from std/c13-inlet@1 rather than drawn - the IEC 60320 C14 appliance inlet at the standard 28.0 x 20.0 panel cutout. The figure draws the unmistakable C14 shroud, and the guide calls it an "AC power socket 115VAC or 240VAC auto-adjusting"
provenance.mirroring: the four groups run PSU1 to PSU4 LEFT to right here, which is the mirror of the front, where the guide says they are "labeled on the front of the chassis as PSU1, PSU2, PSU3 and PSU4 from right to left". Walking round a chassis flips left and right. Group centres are the front bay centres mirrored about the panel width, so an inlet lands behind its own PSU
provenance.relief: the four rockers and the seven screws, and nothing else. WHAT: Figure 1-11, "C40G PSU On/Off switch and AC power receptacle", draws a rocker switch and an IEC inlet per PSU with vent mesh above and below; Figures 1-2 and 1-3 draw the panel bolted on with screws at its corners, mid-edges and one captive screw at its centre. The four C14 inlets carry their own relief through std/c13-inlet@1 and are not re-declared here. HOW FAR: not stated anywhere in the C40G guides - searched "AC power", "receptacle", "On/Off", Appendix A. out 3.0 for a rocker bezel is the SAME number casa/pem carries for its breakers, and it is the same number for the same reason - one estimate for one class of panel-mounted rocker - NOT two independent readings that agreed. cyl 1.6 is edgecore/agr-panel-screw@1. The skin gained an id per corner screw so each cyl takes its own radius; as one group of six spread over 340 mm it would have been a single cylinder the width of the panel. THE VENT REFUSAL IS LIFTED. The first pass declined `vent` on vent-top and vent-bottom because the skin drew the CELLS light on a grey panel, the inverse of what `vent` punches, and recorded that the answer was to fix the drawing WITH A SOURCE. The owner's working/photos/casa/c40g-rear-ac.png is that source: the bottom band of an AC chassis carries fields of fine perforation that are unmistakably DARK HOLES on light grey metal, above and below the inlet row and between the groups. The cells are now drawn dark and the vent is declared. THE PHOTOGRAPH ALSO CONFIRMS THE ARRANGEMENT this contract derived from Figure 1-11: a small black rocker switch immediately to the LEFT of each IEC inlet, four groups across. That was read off a figure and is now corroborated by hardware. ONE FIDELITY POINT, RECORDED RATHER THAN FIXED: the real perforation is ROUND holes on a staggered lattice; this skin draws a rectangular grid of rounded cells. That simplification predates this pass, the photograph shows it is a simplification, and changing it is a drawing job rather than a relief one. NO DEPTH COMES OFF THE PHOTOGRAPH. It is a perspective shot with nothing of known size in frame; the 20.0 is this contract own estimate restated.
provenance.size: drawing, as FRACTIONS - Figure 1-2 renders at an aspect of 1.756 against the real 1.813, about 3 percent out, so it sits between Figure 1-1 (1.795, passes the gate) and Figure 1-10 (1.918, fails). Proportions only, anchored to the band already established from the DC rear: the panel occupies the same y 194 to 264.5 the two PEMs do, and the same x 37.5 to 386.7 card-region width. The depth is ESTIMATED
provenance.what-it-is: drawing - Figure 1-2, "C40G CMTS rear view (AC; non-redundant)", and Figure 1-3, its redundant twin. The bottom band of an AC chassis is ONE panel spanning the card-region width with screws at its corners and mid-edges and one captive screw at its centre - not four separate PSU rear faces. Figure 1-11 shows the same four switch-and-inlet groups in isolation and calls them "C40G PSU On/Off switch and AC power receptacle"
provenance.why-not-bays: the four PSUs are already modelled as FRONT bays (casa/c40g-psu-ac), because that is where they load and where the guide numbers them. Declaring the rear groups as bays too would count each PSU twice in any module total. This panel is therefore ONE part standing for the chassis-side AC entry, and it holds no power figure - the PSUs hold it

components.description: Casa C40G system fan module. A tall side-mounted assembly of eight fan units with the air filter built into its outboard face, occupying the full height of the card band. The chassis takes two: the right-hand slot carries the system fan module and is the air INTAKE, and the left-hand slot is a secondary fan module position that is empty unless the redundancy kit is fitted.
components.name: c40g-fan

provenance.air-filter: drawing - the filter is PART OF THIS MODULE, not a separate FRU. "Figure 1-9 shows the air filter side of the fan module." That is why no separate filter component is modelled for the fan position. The chassis carries a SECOND, unrelated filter - the one integrated into the snap-on front PSU cover - which is casa/c40g-psu-cover
provenance.body: the 380.0 is the size entry's own depth restated as a body so the tray draws as a solid. Same caveat as casa/fan: class `cooling` is not in the viewer's FRU class list, so it will not eject until that is reconciled with class `fan`
provenance.face: drawing - CORRECTED. This skin drew a perforated mesh across the whole front face, and NO C40G FIGURE SHOWS ONE THERE. Figure 1-1, "Casa C40G CMTS front view", and Figure 2-3, "Fan assembly removal", both draw the module's front as plain sheet metal carrying one long rounded pull handle, and the guide describes using it in those words - "grab the handle on the front of the fan tray and slowly pull the module out of the chassis". THE MESH WAS THE RIGHT FEATURE ON THE WRONG FACE: the perforation is Figure 1-9, "C40G fan module air filter side", which is the OUTBOARD face, and Figure 1-8's cross section shows why - the eight fans sit behind the filter, not behind the front plate, which is why the front is blank. Everything else in that column of Figure 1-1 - the yellow triangle, the FAN TRAY 2 / FAN TRAY 1 / AIR FILTER legends, "UNLOCK FAN TRAY", the rotating-blades label and the PSU boxes - is printed on the CHASSIS, which is how the device's front-furniture entry already reads it, so none of it belongs on the module. THE HANDLE RECTANGLE IS UNMEASURED and is left exactly as it was drawn. Figure 1-1 gives its width as about 0.19 of the module width against the 0.23 drawn here, but its top and bottom edges cannot be separated from the chassis in that figure - the strip and the chassis are the same grey above and below the bay - so there is no honest anchor for its length. Wanted: a front photograph of the fan strip, or a caliper
provenance.layout: drawing - Figure 1-1 of the C40G Hardware Installation Guide (rev 07/07/2022), "Casa C40G CMTS front view", which PASSES the orthographic gate: the drawn chassis measures 1364 x 760 px for an aspect of 1.795 against the real rack face of 482 / 265.9 = 1.813, agreeing to 1 percent, so it carries geometry at 2.858 px/mm scaled by the exactly known 265.9 height. Positions here are measured off it rather than taken as fractions
provenance.not-the-c100g-fan: CHECKED, and they are NOT the same part. casa/fan is the C100G assembly: three of them sit horizontally above the rear card band, each holds two fans, each draws 100 W, and the air goes front to rear. This one is a single tall side-mounted module holding eight fans at 400 W with the air going right to left. Same vendor, same era, different machine
provenance.power-draw-max-w: drawing - "The fan module has a power draw of approximately 400W." The word is the vendors: approximately. This is a whole-module figure for all eight fan units, and it is stated for THE system fan module in the singular - no document held here says what a second, redundancy-kit module adds
provenance.relief: one feature, and the rest is a refusal. The front face carries exactly one thing - "grab the handle on the front of the fan tray and slowly pull the module out of the chassis" - and Figures 1-1 and 2-3 both draw that one long rounded bar and nothing else, which is why the mesh was taken off this face. So there is one raised node to declare and `bar` is the right primitive for a grab handle. Its DIAMETER, 7.9, is the drawn rectangle's own short axis - the only self-consistent choice available - and its PROUDNESS is therefore also 7.9, which is a floor and not a measurement: a handle must clear enough for fingers. THE CROSS SECTION DOES NOT HELP, and this is worth recording because it is the figure anyone would reach for. Figure 1-8, "C40G fan module cross section", is not a section through the depth: it is the module with a side cover off, looking at the eight fan faces in two rows of four with the controller PCB and its fuses below. It shows the handle in profile at the right-hand edge, but the drawing's own aspect (1100 x 740 px, 1.49) matches neither 380/205 (1.85) nor any other pair of this module's dimensions, so it fails the orthographic gate and a fraction off it would be a number about the drawing. What it DOES establish is construction: eight fans, two rows, a PCB with fuses and a backplane connector, and a handle that genuinely protrudes. NOT MODELLED HERE: the perforated air-filter face. It is real and Figure 1-9 draws it, but it is the OUTBOARD side, and this component has only a front skin. A skins/body-right.svg carrying that mesh with a `vent` on it is the right way to add it and is left for whoever draws the six faces. WHAT WOULD SETTLE THE HANDLE: a front photograph of the fan strip, or a caliper - the same two things the face entry above already asks for.
provenance.size: drawing-measured - the strip runs x 386.7 to 422.7 and y 17 to 222 in body coordinates off Figure 1-1, so 36 x 205. The width is trimmed to 34.7 so the bay does not overlap the card bays, which end at x 387.5
provenance.what-it-is: drawing - "The C40G is equipped with a system fan module and air filter assembly on the right-hand side of the chassis. The fan assembly module (see Figure 1-7) has eight fans units to supply cooling air to the chassis, drawing cool air through the air filter and across the system modules from right to left with the air exiting the chassis on the left." Figure 1-7 labels the right strip "System fan module" and "Air filter" with "Air flow direction IN", and the left strip "Secondary fan module slot (optional with redundancy kit)" with "Air flow direction OUT"

features.source: the handle rect own drawn 7.9 short axis - the diameter is drawn. The proudness is a FLOOR

components.description: Casa C40G DC power entry module. Two sit side by side across the bottom of the rear face, each taking -40.5 to -60 VDC from a separate 20 A source and providing EMI filtering and redundant DC power to the chassis. The face carries a bolted terminal cover, four studs in a minus pair and a plus pair, two release levers and a disconnect-power warning.
components.name: c40g-pem

provenance.body: the box behind the face is the size entry's own ESTIMATED 200.0 depth restated as a body, not a second claim about the world. It is declared so the module draws as a solid filling its bay rather than as art painted on the rear plate. As with casa/pem, the 3D viewer additionally builds FRU groups only for data-class psu, fan and tab (library/demo2/relief.js), so a class power module will not eject until that list admits it - reported, not worked around
provenance.not-the-c100g-pem: CHECKED, and they do not match. casa/pem, the C100G part, is 207.0 x 91.6 for an aspect of 2.26; this face measures 158 x 70.5 for an aspect of 2.24. The aspects are nearly identical but the SIZE is not - the C40G part is a quarter narrower - so they are modelled separately rather than shared on the strength of a name and a silhouette. If a drawing later shows one part in both chassis, this is the assumption to break
provenance.power: NONE STATED. Neither C40G table gives a PEM figure, and a power ENTRY module is not a supply in the sense power-output-w means - it filters and distributes what the plant feeds it. The L27 warning is left standing as the record
provenance.relief: estimated, and the two halves of that word are different claims. WHAT stands proud is drawing - Figure 1-12, "C40G power entry module": a bolted terminal cover plate at the top left with a captive screw at its centre and two bolt sockets; below it a minus pair and a plus pair of studs, each carrying a hex nut over a star washer; two release levers to the right of them; and the yellow DISCONNECT POWER warning label. Those five kinds of thing, and which node each is, are read straight off that figure. HOW FAR each stands proud is stated NOWHERE. Searched both C40G guides for "power entry", "PEM", "terminal", "stud" and Appendix A; there is no Z dimension for this module in any of them, and Figure 1-12 is a flat elevation, so it cannot supply one either. Every mm below is ESTIMATED against the library's existing treatment of the same class of part, named so the next reader can overturn it in one place: 1.5 for the bolted cover plate is edgecore/agr-ground-plate@1; 1.6 for a panel screw head is edgecore/agr-panel-screw@1; 2.2 for a terminal nut is edgecore/agr-psu-dc@1, which did NOT measure it - its own measured figure is the module depth; 4.2 for a release lever is the same part's latch; 0.2 for a printed label is edgecore/agr-label-caution@1. NOT DONE ON PURPOSE: the two white-outlined terminal boxes are NOT raised. The figure draws them as outlines on the same grey as the plate, which is as consistent with printed boundaries as with a moulded body, and raising them would turn an ambiguity into an assertion. Note this is the opposite call from casa/pem, where the C100G blocks are drawn as filled black bodies - the two parts are treated differently because the two figures show different things, not by oversight. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: one oblique photograph of a C40G rear, or a caliper. THE FACE IS UNTOUCHED. 158.0 x 68.5 and every x/y in the skin are exactly as the size provenance above left them; this pass adds Z and nothing else
provenance.size: drawing-measured off Figure 1-4, "C40G CMTS rear view (DC; non-redundant)", scaled by the known 265.9 chassis height at 2.982 px/mm. The two PEM faces read x 44.8 to 195.7 and 212.8 to 377.7, so about 151 and 165 wide - the spread is edge noise on a figure at this scale - and 158.0 is carried for both. THE BAND WAS READ AS y 194 TO 264.5, SO 70.5 TALL, AND THAT TOP EDGE IS AN OVERREAD. 194 is impossible: the card slot immediately above ends at 194.82 in the same view, and two pieces of sheet metal cannot share 0.82 mm. The C40G's bays already said 196.0, leaving a 1.18 mm margin below the card cage, and the FRONT face shows a measured 1.48 mm margin in exactly that position between the card band and the brand band. So the height is 68.5 - the opening this module goes into - and the 2 mm was six pixels at 2.982 px/mm. FOUND BY asr9k-cards' BAY-VERSUS-OCCUPANT FIT CHECK, which is the only thing that could have: L13 fires on overlap, so a module too BIG for its bay is invisible to it. The bottom edge at 264.5 was agreed by every source throughout and is unchanged. The depth is ESTIMATED
provenance.what-it-is: drawing - "The C40G ships with two DC power entry modules (PEMs). The power entry modules receive -40.5 to -60 VDC (-48VDC nominal) power from separate 20A power supply sources. The two PEMs provide EMI filtering and redundant DC power to the chassis, as shown in Figure 1-12." It is a bay rather than a placement because the guide has both "Removing the DC power entry modules" and "Replacing the PEMs" procedures and it slides into an opening

components.description: Casa C40G AC power supply unit, 1100 W. Four sit in a row across the bottom front of the chassis behind the snap-on cover, numbered PSU1 to PSU4 from right to left. The front face carries two fans, a folding pull handle and a status LED; the ON/OFF switch and the AC inlet are on the module's other end, at the rear of the chassis.
components.name: c40g-psu-ac

provenance.body: the 300.0 is the size entry's own ESTIMATED depth restated as a body, not a second claim. Unlike the PEMs and the fans this one WILL eject: it is class psu, which is in the viewer's FRU class list
provenance.faceplate: drawing - Figure 1-10, "C40G AC power supply units", shows the four in place with the cover removed and enlarges one of them. Each face carries two fans, a folding pull handle across the LEFT fan, a status LED and a locking thumb screw on the right edge; the guide labels three of those in as many words ("Folding pull handle", "Locking thumb screw", "Status LED - ON / FAIL"). ARRANGEMENT CORRECTED against that enlargement. The skin had the two fans at 0.296 and 0.642 of the module width and the LED at 0.833 - out beyond the right fan, where the figure draws nothing. Measured on the enlarged face, whose box reads 374 x 157 px: the fans centre on 0.2674 and 0.7206 and the LED sits in the GAP BETWEEN THEM at 0.4987 across and 0.5833 down. Anchored to the 81.0 x 38.2 this contract holds, that is fan centres 21.66 and 58.37 and a lamp at 40.39, 22.28. The handle is translated with the left fan rather than re-drawn, the same treatment casa/c40g-pem gave its face, because it was never dimensioned on its own. X-fractions are safe to take from this figure even though it fails the orthographic gate, because the size entry below already anchors this part to a width measured elsewhere; a horizontal-centre reading of 0.4987 is in any case the one fraction an anisotropic drawing cannot get wrong. THE LAMP DIAMETER IS UNCHANGED AT 2.6 AND IS NOT MEASURED. The figure's lamp is 15 px across and 17 px down, which scale to 3.25 mm off the width and 4.16 off the height. A lamp is round, so the spread is the drawing being 12 percent out in aspect - 2.382 against this part's 2.121 - and not a diameter. Wanted: a caliper. NOT DRAWN, and named so it is not mistaken for absent: the figure gives each fan four corner screws, eight on the face. They are fasteners with no state and no stated position beyond that figure, so they are left out rather than placed from a drawing that cannot hold a dimension
provenance.power-output-w: 1100 W, and it is an OUTPUT because this module PROVIDES power. A psu states power-output-w and never a draw key - they are opposite signs of one unit and summing across both is the category error the vocabulary exists to prevent. The figure is the vendors nameplate rating, stated in the running text
provenance.relief: the kinds are the guide's own words; the depths are estimated. Figure 1-10 LABELS three things on this face - "Folding pull handle", "Locking thumb screw", "Status LED" - so which node is what is not a reading at all, it is a caption. What none of it gives is a Z dimension, and neither does Table A-1, the running text, or Figure 1-11 of the other end. Searched both C40G guides for "power supply", "PSU", "handle", "thumb". - handle: modelled FOLDED, because that is how Figure 1-10 draws it, lying across the left fan rather than swung out. bar 1.5 is the drawn stroke width - the wire diameter of the bail - so it is a number off the drawing rather than a guess. `uhandle` was the obvious primitive and is WRONG here: it takes its tube diameter from the node's SHORT axis, which on this path is the 12.2 mm bracket width, not the 1.5 mm wire, so it would have produced a 12 mm pipe. Recorded because the next person will reach for uhandle too. - thumbscrew: cyl 5.0 with knurl, which is common/fan-module@1's locking screw exactly - same part doing the same job, and the guide calls both a thumb screw. - status: dome 0.3, common/led-dot@1's lamp. Note the lamp DIAMETER stays 2.6 and stays unmeasured, for the reason the faceplate entry above gives; this pass adds Z only. THE FAN REFUSAL IS LIFTED AND THE ART IS REDRAWN. The first pass declined `vent` on fan-left/fan-right because this skin drew each fan as a LIGHT disc with dark guard wires over it - the inverse of what `vent` needs, which punches a node's DARK cells - so declaring it would have asserted that the surround was the hole. It recorded that the fix was "redrawing the fan as a dark aperture behind a light guard, which is an artwork change with no source behind it". THE OWNER'S PHOTOGRAPH IS THAT SOURCE: working/photos/casa/c40g-front.png, the chassis with the PSU cover off, shows each of the four PSUs with TWO circular openings that are genuinely dark and see-through, with the fan blades visible behind, and a light WIRE FINGER GUARD over each - concentric rings crossed by radial spokes. The art now draws that, and the vent is honest. IT ALSO CONFIRMS THE FOLDED HANDLE. The bail is a bright metal tube lying flat across the LEFT fan, exactly where Figure 1-10 draws it and where this contract put it. The tube is visibly more substantial than the 1.5 the drawn stroke width gave, but the photograph supplies no dimension and the number is unchanged. THE PHOTOGRAPH FAILS GATE 1 AND WAS TESTED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. Its metal extent measures 1149 x 591 px for an aspect of 1.944 against the real rack face at 1.813 - 7.2 percent out - so no absolute geometry comes off it and no fraction either. Shape, count and arrangement only, which is all that was needed. The four corner screws per fan that Figure 1-10 shows are still not drawn, for the reason already recorded above.
provenance.size: drawing, as FRACTIONS - Figure 1-10 FAILS the orthographic gate at an aspect of 1.918 against the real 1.813, nearly 6 percent out, where Figure 1-1 passes at 1.795. So only proportions are taken from it and they are anchored to the band Figure 1-1 does carry: the PSU row occupies the snap-on covers footprint, y 226.7 to 264.9 and x 44.0 to 386.6, and the four read as about 81.0 wide on an 87.2 pitch within it. The depth is ESTIMATED
provenance.the-other-end: drawing - Figure 1-11, "C40G PSU On/Off switch and AC power receptacle", shows a rocker switch and an IEC appliance inlet per PSU, with vent mesh above and below. That figure numbers PSU1 to PSU4 LEFT to right while Figure 1-10 numbers them right to left, and the two are consistent rather than in conflict: walking round the chassis flips left and right, so Figure 1-11 is the REAR face of the same four modules. The text settles which way round is which - "PSUs are labeled on the front of the chassis as PSU1, PSU2, PSU3 and PSU4 from right to left". Only the front face is drawn here; the rear face is not modelled, because these bays live on the front view
provenance.what-it-is: "The C40G supports up to four removable 1100W AC power supply units (PSUs). The PSUs operate concurrently in the chassis. In the event of a PSU failure, the remaining PSUs (up to two) provide the required power to maintain system operation." The warning beside it is worth keeping: "The C40G-20 cannot be sufficiently powered with less than two PSUs"

components.description: Casa C40G snap-on power supply unit cover with integrated air filter - the full-width panel across the bottom of the front face, below the card band and the brand band. It covers the four AC PSU positions and carries the filter that protects them, and it snaps on rather than sliding into an opening.
components.name: c40g-psu-cover

provenance.artwork: drawing - the face carries four groups of horizontal louvre lines with a raised swept form across the middle two. Drawn as read from Figure 1-1 at 2.858 px/mm; the exact louvre count is at the limit of what that figure resolves
provenance.placement: it is a PLACEMENT, not a bay. It SNAPS ON to the outside of the front face - the guides own word - rather than sliding into an opening in the metal, so it paints over the panel behind it. The four AC PSUs it covers are a separate question and are NOT modelled yet
provenance.power: none, and none is expected. This is a cover with a filter in it. The four 1100 W AC PSUs behind it are the power-bearing parts and they are not modelled
provenance.relief: one feature and one refusal. The louvres are given `vent` because this part's whole job is to pass air through a filter - the guide's own sentence is "PSUs are protected with a serviceable air filter within the removable front" cover - and the skin draws them as dark cells, which is what `vent` needs. Depth 12.0 is this contract's own ESTIMATED cover depth, restated because the hole opens into the cover, not a new claim. NOT RAISED: `sweep`, the swept form across the middle. The artwork entry above calls it raised and it probably is, but it is three STROKED paths with fill:none, and `out` builds a box from a node's bounding rect - so raising it would produce a 140 x 23 mm blank slab with three lines painted on top, which is the failure mode the depth notes warn about for bare paths. Making it stand proud needs the swoop drawn as a closed filled shape first. Nothing in any C40G figure gives its height in any case. NO Z DIMENSION for this part exists in either guide; searched "cover", "air filter", "snap-on".
provenance.size: drawing-measured off Figure 1-1, which passes the orthographic gate at 1.795 against a true 1.813. The panel spans x 37.5 to 386.7 and y 226.7 to 264.9 in body coordinates, so 349.2 x 38.2. The depth is estimated - a snap-on cover is shallow and no document gives the figure
provenance.what-it-is: drawing - the guide names it and gives it a job: "PSUs are protected with a serviceable air filter within the removable front" cover, and a figure callout reads "Snap-on power supply unit cover and integrated air filter". So the wavy-line panel across the bottom of Figure 1-1 is not decoration, it is a serviceable part with a filter in it

features.source: this contract own ESTIMATED 12.0 cover depth re-expressed. Not a second claim

components.description: Casa C100G front cable manager. Two brackets across the bottom of the front face, left and right, that carry the coax down and away from the exhaust.
components.name: cable-manager

provenance.depth: MOVED FROM size.d TO relief, and the sign was wrong. `size.d` on a kind: component compiles to data-depth, which the 3D viewer reads as a CAVITY - so a bracket that carries coax AWAY from the face was rendering as a 71.4 x 10.8 x 40 mm HOLE in the front of the chassis. That is the deepest pit in the Casa set and it is the same defect the library has recorded before, on rivets and a grounding plate. THE NUMBER IS UNCHANGED AND STILL ESTIMATED. 40.0 is what this file has always carried and no C100G document states a projection for this bracket; it is now expressed as `out`, which is what a bracket bolted to the outside of a faceplate actually does. Re-expressing an estimate is not the same as sourcing one - what has been fixed is the DIRECTION, which was certainly wrong, not the magnitude, which is still a guess. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: one photograph of a C100G front from the side. Note the `out` sits on `bracket`, the group's outer rect, so the extruded solid is textured with the bracket's own face art rather than coming out blank.
provenance.detail: NOTE - his source is a PLAIN grey rect with a black outline and no internal detail, so only the outline is measured. The end mounting screws drawn here are the minimum needed to read as a bracket and are not from any source. Anything more would be invention
provenance.flush-not-proud: THE 40.0 IS WITHDRAWN. It rendered these two as brackets standing 40 mm - about an inch and a half - off the bottom of the front face, and the owner, looking at the hardware, says they are FLUSH OR NEARLY FLUSH with the panel. No feature replaces it: "nearly flush" is not a number and a small one invented to look humble is still invented.
provenance.relief-not-on-the-screws: the two end screws are deliberately left flat. The `detail` entry above says in as many words that they "are not from any source" - they were drawn to make the part read as a bracket. Giving them a height would put a sourced- looking Z claim on art that is itself acknowledged invention, which is worse than leaving them painted on.
provenance.size: drawing - Jason's hand-built front SVG, `chassisManager1` and `chassisManager2`, 31.38 x 5.18 in a 190.26-wide frame, mapped fractionally onto our 432.95 x 571 body. The two are symmetric about the centre line
provenance.what-these-are-is-NOT-SETTLED: THIS COMPONENT'S NAME AND DESCRIPTION ARE AN INFERENCE AND SHOULD NOT BE TRUSTED. Neither Casa guide names the two items at the bottom of the C100G front face. The description here - brackets that "carry the coax down and away from the exhaust" - was reasoning from position, not read from a source. The owner's account, from the hardware: they are an ACTIVE component, "like a PCB card with a faceplate on it that goes inside there and manages the actual line cards" - and he is not certain of the name either. If that is right, this is not furniture at all and belongs in a bay rather than as a placement. WHAT IS SETTLED, and was got backwards: the REAL cable management on this chassis is the row of fourteen fingers above the slot numbers, which Figure 1-1 draws and which this device models as decor at y 60.5. Those DO stand proud. These do not. Closed by: a Casa document naming the bottom-front items, or a photograph of one removed.

components.description: Casa C100G/C40G chassis identity and compliance label, affixed to the top front of the chassis. Placeholder art - the blocks stand for the printed fields and no real model or serial is reproduced.
components.name: chassis-label

provenance.artwork: placeholder blocks, deliberately. The vendor's own figure prints Serial # 00, but transcribing any real identifier into artwork is a rule this library keeps regardless. The rectangle is a stand-in for the printed fields
provenance.content: drawing - Figure 1-3 of the C100G Hardware Installation Guide, "Casa C100G chassis label", and the bulleted list beside it. The label carries the Casa triangle logo and wordmark, Model # and Serial # fields, the FCC part 15 statement and FCC mark, the electrical rating, the CE mark, a TUV / C-NRTL-US mark citing UL/CSA/IEC 60950, and a "Do not open risk of electric shock" warning
provenance.location: drawing - "The C100G product label is affixed to the top front side of the chassis", which is why it is placed on the top view near the front edge rather than on the bottom cover where a 1RU switch would carry it
provenance.relief: out 0.2 on the label, which is the thickness of an adhesive label and is edgecore's figure for the same thing - agr-label-spec@1, agr-label-serial@1 and agr-label-caution@1 all carry 0.2. It is ESTIMATED and no Casa document states it; the point of declaring it at all is that a label is a thing stuck ON the metal, so at zero it is indistinguishable from print. The placeholder blocks inside it are NOT given relief - they stand for printed fields, and print has no height. Note this part has no `size.d` and must not acquire one: depth on a kind: component compiles to a cavity, so a 0.2 there would make the label a pit rather than a sticker.
provenance.size: ESTIMATED, and this is the weak figure. Figure 1-3 reproduces the label alone with nothing of known size beside it, so only its ASPECT can be read - about 2.1 to 1, which 120 x 57 preserves. No guide states the label's dimensions and no photograph of the chassis top exists here. A tape measure on a real unit closes this in one minute

features.source: edgecore/agr-label-spec@1 - the library one figure for an adhesive label. NOT MEASURED: that part has photo-measured SIZE provenance and no depth provenance at all

components.description: Casa CCAP Services Card (CSC8x10G) for the C100G/C40G CCAP chassis. Eight 10GbE SFP+ ports (XG0-XG7) in two ganged blocks of four, carrying the DOCSIS and EQAM MAC functions to Distributed Access nodes, plus a bank of eight two-lamp port rows and the STATUS, ACTIVE and ALARM cluster. Out-of-band signalling is on the separate optional CSC I/O card, not on this faceplate.
components.name: csc-8x10g

provenance.compliance: not stated - the CSC8x10G data sheet carries no compliance line at all, unlike the SMM300G sheets which both give NEBS level 3
provenance.depth-known-wrong: THE 380.0 IS NOT MERELY UNMEASURED, IT IS IMPOSSIBLE, and this contract now says so in a field a tool can read - size-confidence: {d: known-wrong}. THE CONSTRAINT. Front and rear cards MEET AT A MIDPLANE, which the owner photographed: working/photos/casa/c40g-empty-midplane.png shows the emptied cage with the card guides and the midplane at the back of it, and the opening where the rear I/O card reaches through to the front card. So a front card and its rear partner have to share the chassis depth - 386.0 on the C100G, 388.45 on the C40G. Two cards at 380.0 need 760, which is not a wide error bar, it is twice the box. WHAT THE SHAPE IS, from the owner: "the front card is mostly rectangular, but the I/O card is kind of L SHAPED where the top part of the top connector PASSES THROUGH THE MIDPLANE and plugs into the front card, and the other one is plugged into the midplane. So they ultimately kind of meet in the middle." So the rear card is a body against the midplane PLUS A TONGUE at the top reaching forward through it. NOTE WHAT THAT DOES AND DOES NOT ALLOW, because the obvious rule is wrong. front + rear CAN exceed the chassis depth, by about the tongue length, because the tongue overlaps the front card at a height where the front card is not - they interleave rather than tile. The constraint is therefore an inequality with slack, not an equality. What it cannot absorb is a 374 mm overlap where a tongue is tens of millimetres. ONE PHOTOGRAPH IS USABLE AND IT IS NOT THIS CARD-FAMILY-WIDE. bdm2m-solder-side.jpeg has the faceplate FULLY IN FRAME, so its 345.5 long axis anchors the scale at 5.00 px/mm; the card measures 1336 px from the faceplate to the top of its midplane connectors. They are not second opinions and must not be averaged in. provenance.faceplate-hardware-photo: THE OWNER SUPPLIED AN ISOMETRIC OF THE C100G FRONT and it corrects the SHAPE of two things on this faceplate. working/photos/casa/ - c100g-front-isometric.png and the crop crop-ejectors.png, read at high zoom. WHAT IT SETTLES: - The captive screw is not a flat slotted head. It is a substantial BLACK KNURLED KNOB standing well proud, with a dark top face and a light metallic band. `knurl` is added for that reason - it is a shape fact and costs no dimension. The drawn 2D head is still a slotted circle and is NOT redrawn; the figures draw it that way and this photograph cannot give a true elevation of it. - The EJECTOR LEVER is the most prominent thing on the whole face: a large CURVED BLACK lever, not the rounded strip this skin draws, with a thin vertical linkage rod running down the card from the knob to it. - RELATIVE PROMINENCE, which is the one quantitative thing a perspective view CAN give: lever stands proud of knob stands proud of lamp. This contract already orders them that way - 4.2, 1.6, 0.3 - so the photograph CONFIRMS the ordering rather than correcting it. Only the absolute magnitudes are understated, and it gives no absolute magnitude. WHAT IT DOES NOT SETTLE, and why nothing else moved. So it fails gate 1 outright, exactly as the Cisco perspective figures did. provenance.layout: photo-measured - the CSC8x10G data sheet (CSC R7, May 2019) product photograph, read as fractions of the known 345.5 card height. provenance.legend: drawing - the model legend sits between TWO orange bands, not below one, which is the first thing three product photographs settle and which casa/smm-8x10g does not show. provenance.port-lamps: photo-inferred - two lamps per port, on either side of the port legend, in a bank BELOW the cages rather than beside them. The photograph resolves the dots and the XG0-XG7 legends; no document held here gives their colour vocabulary, so no states are declared
provenance.port-pitch: registry (SFF-8433 B04, 14.25 Basic) confirmed by photograph - the photograph measures 13.8-14.1 between adjacent cages, and the standard figure is carried because a ganged block's pitch is specified, not chosen. provenance.ports: composed from std/ aperture components rather than drawn as rectangles. provenance.size: shared with the rest of the C100G front-card family, taken from the chassis slot envelope (30.47 x 345.5, C100G device manifest); the depth is the family estimate carried by casa/smm-8x10g
provenance.stripes: photo-measured - five stripes below the lamp cluster, thick to thin downward. The lower two measure under 0.2mm, which is the photograph's resolution limit, and are drawn at 0.35

provenance.layout: drawing - Figure 1-11 of the Casa C100G Hardware Installation Guide (rev 07/08/2022) draws US 16X4, US 16X8, DS 8X8, DS 8X96 and DS 8X192 side by side on ONE shell. It is authoritative for WHAT is on the face - which is nothing but three lamps, because the RF connectors live on the rear I/O module - and for the lamp ORDER, which is STATUS, ALARM, ACTIVE and is NOT the STATUS, ACTIVE, ALARM order the SMM and CSC faceplates use
provenance.leds: drawing-measured - Figure 1-17 of the C40G Hardware Installation Guide (rev 07/07/2022), "DOCSIS downstream and upstream line cards", which draws US 16X4, US 16X8, DS 8X8, DS 8X96 and DS 8X192 side by side. THIS CARD'S OWN PLATE was boxed at 117 x 1420 px, un- clipped, with clear white margin above and below, and its three lamp centres read at 0.57183, 0.58239, 0.59296 of that height. The figure's own spacing wobbles by half a pixel, so the pitch is the group's span divided evenly: 0.010563 of the height. Anchored to the 345.5 height this contract already holds, that is a pitch of 3.66 mm and centres at 197.56, 201.22 and 204.88. THE OTHER FOUR PLATES IN THE SAME FIGURE WERE MEASURED SEPARATELY AND AGREE TO WITHIN A PIXEL, which is said here rather than left for silence to imply; they are five instances of one drawing, not five sources. The order is STATUS, ALARM, ACTIVE with the dark lamp in the MIDDLE, which the figure shows by colour as well as by label - unlike the SMM pair, where ALARM is third and dark. It replaces a 6.6 mm pitch that was never measured on this card or on any other: casa/bdm's provenance said outright that 6.6 was picked so the lamps would "read as separate indicators", and the same three numbers had been carried onto every Casa front card. This entry is a separate reading of a separate plate and is not that number under a new name. THE 3.0 LAMP DIAMETER IS UNCHANGED AND STILL UNMEASURED, for the reason the BDM gave: these drawings are anisotropic, so a round lamp scales to two different diameters depending on the axis, which tells you the drawing is wrong rather than telling you the size.
provenance.positions: drawing, reconciled against casa/bdm - these are the BDM's numbers to the millimetre, because the BDM and the DQM/DCU cards are ONE faceplate. Figure 1-14 (the BDM) and Figure 1-11 (the DQM/DCU) put the bands, both stripe groups and the lamp cluster within 0.5mm of each other, and casa/bdm was built from the first of them. The DS8x96 photograph, scaled by the full card height, puts the stripe groups 5.6 and 8.0mm lower; that is a three-quarter view's perspective error over a 345.5mm card rather than a real difference, and six of these cards sit side by side in a C100G where a 6mm offset between two members of one family would read as a modelling fault. The lamp pitch is the one place the figure is the outlier: it draws the dots nearly touching on a 3.6 pitch, the photograph measures 8.14, and casa/bdm's 6.6 is carried
provenance.positions-rejected: photo-measured - taken as FRACTIONS of the known 345.5 card height from the DS8x96 data sheet product photograph. Figure 1-11 fails the orthographic gate: its plate renders 147 x 1951 px, aspect 0.0753 against the real 0.0882, so it is drawn about 15 percent narrow, and its five cards are drawn small enough that the lamp dots are squeezed onto a 3.6 pitch. Scaled by the full card height the photograph puts them on 8.14, and the DS8x96 and SMM300G photographs independently agree with each other on the two legend bands to within 0.5mm. So the photograph is used for placement and the figure for arrangement
provenance.power-draw-max-w: install guide - THE TWO SOURCES DISAGREE. Table A-3 of the C100G install guide (rev 07/08/2022) gives 'DS8x192: 350W' as maximum consumption with the I/O module; the DS8x192 data sheet (R6, April 2018) prints 'Total Power 320W'. Both numbers are recorded here rather than one being quietly dropped. 350 is the figure carried, because max means the highest rated case and the install guide is the later and more specific document. The check was worth making: the DS8x96 data sheet prints 320W too, for a card of half the density, so the datasheet pair alone would have read as one number covering both densities
provenance.power-scope: READ THIS BEFORE SUMMING. Casa does not state a bare card's draw. Every figure in Tables A-3 and A-4 is the card PLUS its paired rear RF I/O module - the vendor's own column headings are 'Maximum consumption with I/O module', 'Single QAM w/ QAM I/O' and 'Single DCU w/ RFU I/O'. On a C100G that pairing spans TWO bays, a front DOCSIS card and a rear RF I/O card, so power-draw-max-w here already accounts for both and adding a rear I/O figure to it would double count. That the pairing is what is measured is not an inference: the same US16x8 is 200W with the F-connector RFU and 220W with the UPS 32x4 MCX I/O, which is one card and two answers. A single per-card key may be the wrong shape for these devices; that is a schema question, and until it is settled this note is what stops the number being read as something the vendor never said

So a front card and its rear partner have to share the chassis depth - 386.0 on the C100G, 388.45 on the C40G. Two cards at 380.0 need 760, which is not a wide error bar, it is twice the box. WHAT THE SHAPE IS, from the owner: "the front card is mostly rectangular, but the I/O card is kind of L SHAPED where the top part of the top connector PASSES THROUGH THE MIDPLANE and plugs into the front card, and the other one is plugged into the midplane.
