components.description: Casa C100G fan assembly module. Three sit side by side above the rear card band - LEFT, CENTER and RIGHT - and each contains two fans, designated 0 = front and 1 = back. The face is a punched perforation grid with a pull handle across the lower third and an indicator panel carrying a hot-swap button and HS / alarm / OK indicators. Maximum 100 W each, 300 W across the three.
components.name: fan

provenance.airflow: CONFLICT, unresolved. Figure 1-5 and the body text say the fans draw air in at the FRONT BOTTOM through the filter and exhaust at the rear top, which would make this face an OUTLET. Jason states the opposite from the hardware - in at the rear, out at the front bottom. The filter sits on the front bottom opening, and filters belong on intakes, which favours the guide. Recorded rather than decided; see docs/casa-modular-chassis.md
provenance.body: the 150.0 is the size entry's own ESTIMATED depth restated as a body so the tray draws as a solid rather than a face floating in the rear plate. NOTE the viewer will not eject it even so: it builds FRU groups for data-class psu, fan and tab, and every Casa and Cisco fan is class `cooling` while every Edgecore, UfiSpace and common one is class `fan` (library/demo2/relief.js). That split is reported, not papered over here
provenance.count: datasheet - the guide names three fan modules, LEFT, CENTER and RIGHT, each with two fans designated either front or back
provenance.depth: estimated - not measured
provenance.layout: drawing - Figure 1-4 of the C100G Hardware Installation Guide, "C100G fan module", left panel "Fan tray front view". Measured as percentages of that figure's face and stretched onto this module. The figure's aspect is 1.563 against this module's 1.505, so it is close to scale, but fractions are used anyway
provenance.panel: drawing - indicator panel at 33.8 to 68.3 percent of the width and 1.6 to 31.7 percent of the height. Hot-swap button at 40.2 percent, three indicators at 49.2 / 55.9 / 62.5 percent with their icons above them and the LEDs below - HS, warning triangle, boxed OK
provenance.perforation: drawing - 19 columns x 9 rows of punched cells, each 4.15 percent of the face wide and 7.83 percent tall, on a 5.09 x 10.84 percent pitch, starting at 2.31 / 2.75 percent. Three cells in the bottom row are blanked where the handle latches land
provenance.perforation-colour: Jason - the punched cells look THROUGH the faceplate into the chassis, so they are drawn dark with a light punch edge. Figure 1-4 shows them white, which is line-art convention, not what the part looks like
provenance.power: CONFLICT, recorded not resolved. The HIG body text states "Each fan assembly module has a maximum power consumption of 100W, totaling 300W across the three fan assemblies", and Table A-2 gives the row "Fan assembly (3)" as "330W maximum, 220W typical" - both statements are about the set of three, and 300 is not 330. 100 W is taken because it is the only figure the vendor states PER MODULE, which is the granularity this contract needs; dividing 330 by three would be our arithmetic rather than the vendor's, and 220/3 would invent a per-module typical nobody published. The C100G carries a fan-power-sources gap naming both figures
provenance.relief: estimated depths, sourced kinds. WHICH nodes stand off the face and what they are is drawing - Figure 1-4, "C100G fan module", left panel "Fan tray front view", and Figure 7-11, "Fan assembly installation", which draws the same three trays in the chassis at higher fidelity. Between them: a punched perforation grid across the whole face, an indicator panel sitting on top of it, a pull handle across the lower third and three spring-latch slots in the bottom row. NO C100G DOCUMENT GIVES A DEPTH for any of them. Searched both guides for "fan assembly", "fan tray", "fan module" and Appendix A Table A-2; the tables carry power and airflow and no mechanical dimension at all. So: vent 25.0 is the library's figure for a fan grille (common/fan-module@1 uses 25, edgecore/agr-fan@1 uses 26); NEITHER OF THOSE IS A MEASUREMENT - neither part gives a grille depth, only a module depth. cyl 1.2 and dome 0.3 are the pushbutton and lamp idiom this library already uses (common/led-dot@1). The HANDLE is the one number that is not borrowed and not invented: bar 9.0 is the handle rect's own drawn height, so the tube is as thick as the handle is drawn. Whether it stands 9 mm proud or 20 is unknown - a pull handle must clear enough for fingers, and 9.0 is the floor rather than a reading. THE INDICATOR BEZEL IS NOW RAISED, and the history is worth keeping. It was left FLAT in the first pass - deliberately, and recorded as such - because `dome` carried no `lift` in the relief extractor, so raising the bezel 1.5 would have buried the three lamps it holds at z 0 inside it, and the lamps are this module's state display. That extractor gap has since been fixed (library/demo2/relief.js now sums data-z-lift up the ancestor chain and domes honour it), so the reason no longer applies and the panel is raised with the button and lamps lifted onto its face. A part that was deliberately wrong for a reason that has gone away must not quietly stay wrong. The 1.5 is the bolted-plate estimate, edgecore/agr-ground-plate@1's. NOT RAISED, on purpose and not by oversight: - `latch-slots`. There is no way to declare a body that is full slot height for part of its depth and a narrower section for the rest. So this contract declares NO body rather than declaring a box that is wrong in a way nothing records. provenance.depth-known-wrong: THE 380.0 IS NOT MERELY UNMEASURED, IT IS IMPOSSIBLE, and this contract now says so in a field a tool can read - size-confidence: {d: known-wrong}. THE CONSTRAINT. Front and rear cards MEET AT A MIDPLANE, which the owner photographed: working/photos/casa/c40g-empty-midplane.png shows the emptied cage with the card guides and the midplane at the back of it, and the opening where the rear I/O card reaches through to the front card. So a front card and its rear partner have to share the chassis depth - 386.0 on the C100G, 388.45 on the C40G. Two cards at 380.0 need 760, which is not a wide error bar, it is twice the box. WHAT THE SHAPE IS, from the owner: "the front card is mostly rectangular, but the I/O card is kind of L SHAPED where the top part of the top connector PASSES THROUGH THE MIDPLANE and plugs into the front card, and the other one is plugged into the midplane. So they ultimately kind of meet in the middle." So the rear card is a body against the midplane PLUS A TONGUE at the top reaching forward through it. NOTE WHAT THAT DOES AND DOES NOT ALLOW, because the obvious rule is wrong. front + rear CAN exceed the chassis depth, by about the tongue length, because the tongue overlaps the front card at a height where the front card is not - they interleave rather than tile. The constraint is therefore an inequality with slack, not an equality. What it cannot absorb is a 374 mm overlap where a tongue is tens of millimetres. ONE PHOTOGRAPH IS USABLE AND IT IS NOT THIS CARD-FAMILY-WIDE. bdm2m-solder-side.jpeg has the faceplate FULLY IN FRAME, so its 345.5 long axis anchors the scale at 5.00 px/mm; the card measures 1336 px from the faceplate to the top of its midplane connectors. Raw that is 267 mm. The shot is NOT orthographic - the PCB reads 4.66 percent wider at the connector end than at the faceplate end, which is perspective, not a taper - so correcting to the mean scale gives about 261, and taking the card top at the outermost connector edge instead pushes it to about 282. CALL IT 270 PLUS OR MINUS 12 AND DO NOT ROUND THAT AWAY. REJECTED, and the rejection is the useful part: bdm2m-top-plan.jpeg and both qam-io-card plan shots have the faceplate CLIPPED BY THE FRAME, so the 345.5 anchor is truncated and every number off them is understated by an unknown amount. Measured anyway, the top-plan gives 227 mm for the same card the solder side gives 270 - a 19 percent disagreement that is entirely the broken anchor. They are not second opinions and must not be averaged in. NOTHING IS REPLACED. 270 plus or minus 12 is one reading of one card from one photograph that fails gate 1, and stamping it on twelve cards would be the family-number pattern doing harm instead of good - these cards share a FACEPLATE, which is established, not a depth, which is not. What is established is that 380.0 cannot be true. WANTED, in order of how much each unlocks: a tape on any one front card (fixes it outright); a tape on any one rear I/O card; an unclipped side-on photograph of a rear card showing where the tongue begins, which would give the midplane position and both halves at once.
provenance.figure-check: drawing - RE-MEASURED against Figure 1-15 at 600 dpi for the v2 bump, rather than trusted because v1 had used them. Detecting the orange jack fills by colour and walking out to the plate gives twelve U jacks at x 6.974 of a 30.47 plate, y 41.93 to 254.50 on a 19.324 pitch, and six D jacks at x 18.066, y 46.78 to 240.58 on a 38.761 pitch. What this contract carries - 6.855 / 41.93 / 19.34 and 17.985 / 46.72 / 38.79 - agrees with all six to 0.12 mm, so the composed apertures land where the FIGURE puts them and not merely where they used to be. The figure also settles the size question the bump raises. The drawn jack is 7.82 mm across overall (36 radii, spread 0.4 mm) with a 3.28 mm coloured centre. That is not the panel hole - it is the connector as seen, and an MCX bulkhead jack's front flange is 6.5 mm dia on the Radiall sheet, which at this figure's demonstrated 14 percent scale error is the same thing. So a 4.95 mm hole under a 6.5 mm flange is what the figure draws; v1's 3.87 x 3.14 was smaller than either. Clearance is not close. The U pitch is 19.32 and the columns are 11.1 apart, so a 4.95 aperture (and even a 6.5 flange) fits with room; nothing had to be compressed to make the sourced size fit the figure's pitch.
provenance.layout: drawing - Figure 1-15 of the Casa C100G Hardware Installation Guide (rev 07/08/2022). Twelve U jacks in the left column, six D in the right, interleaved. Port COUNT and ARRANGEMENT are read straight off the figure and are reliable
provenance.mcx-is-recessed: THE OWNER, AGAINST THE HARDWARE: "the MCX connector is RECESSED INTO the faceplate, so it actually doesn't stick out from the faceplate, it's recessed from the faceplate ... whereas the US I/O and the DS I/Os have the F fitting STICKING OUT of the faceplate." So the two connector families on these chassis go OPPOSITE WAYS - MCX recessed, F-type proud - and that is a fact about the world, recorded in his terms so it does not have to be rediscovered. THIS SENTENCE IS COPIED FROM casa/io-6p12-sw@2, where it was written first. One statement from one person about one pair of connector families, restated on every card it applies to - not several observations that agreed. THE FIGURES AGREE, INDEPENDENTLY AND AFTERWARDS. Figure 1-12 (C100G), "RF IO upstream and downstream modules", draws the three rear I/O cards side by side and treats the families completely differently: every F port on QAM IO and US IO is a HEX NUT with concentric rings and a shadow, a connector body standing off the plate, while every MCX port on UPS IO 32 is a small flat dark circle with no hex and no body. Figures 1-15 and 1-16 draw the 6+12 cards' MCX the same flat way. NOTHING IS CHANGED HERE YET, and the reason is not indecision. The aperture is composed from std/mcx@1, whose relief is {node: barrel, cyl: 2.0} - a PROTRUSION read off the Radiall R113.553.000 side elevation, which is a FRONT-MOUNT bulkhead jack whose flange does sit on the front of its panel. std/mcx@1 is not wrong about that connector; it is the wrong VARIANT for every card that composes it, and all five of its users are Casa. It is a std/ part and the registry note in spec/schemas/standards.yaml says the same thing, so the two have to move together and the decision is not this contract's to take. Reported to the team lead. NO DEPTH IS GUESSED: the owner gave a topology, not a dimension, and no Casa document gives a recess depth. WANTED: how far below the faceplate the MCX interface sits - one caliper reading or one side-on photograph.
provenance.missing-component: THE CABLE COMB IS A REAL, NAMED PART AND THIS LIBRARY DOES NOT HAVE ONE. The `comb` entry above describes it from a photograph; the guides name it and draw it. Figures 1-15 and 1-16 of the C100G guide are captioned "6+12 IO Module w/ cable retention bracket" and "6+12 SW IO Modules w/ cable retention bracket", and each draws the bracket as its OWN object beside the card - a notched strip with the U and D numbers printed between the notches and three screws through it, one per standoff. Figure 2-15 of the C40G guide names the equivalent outright, "UPS 32x4 I/O cable retention plate", and draws it separated from its module. So casa/ is missing a component, not a decision: there is no cable-retention-plate part and none of the four I/O card families can seat one, even though the three standoffs on this faceplate exist for no other purpose than to carry it. Recorded rather than built - building it is a modelling job with its own sourcing, not part of a relief pass. It is NOT casa/cable-manager, which is a different bracket on the chassis front. WRITTEN FIRST IN casa/ups-32x4@1 and restated here.
provenance.power: NONE STATED, AND THIS IS WHERE THAT BELONGS. No table in either Casa guide gives an I/O module a power figure - Tables A-8 and A-9 give the RFD and RFU their connectors and nothing else - and the BDM's "approximately 300W" is scoped to the BDM WITH its paired I/O card, which is why the front half carries that figure under power-draw-scope: module-with-paired-io. Writing a number here would double count the pairing, so the absence is CORRECT rather than merely unsourced and the L27 warning is its record. WHERE THIS CAME FROM: casa/io-6p12-io2 and casa/io-6p12-sw-io2 have carried this reasoning since they were built, and both open it with "same as the plain card" - so they were asserting a fact about THIS file, in their own, where nothing could check it and where this card never said it. Restated here in this card's own terms. It is the same finding, not a second one, and the two io2 entries are echoes of it rather than independent corroboration.
provenance.relief: the C100G/C40G card family treatment - two captive screws (cyl 1.6), the ejector latch strip (out 4.2). THE FULL ARGUMENT IS IN casa/bdm@1 AND THIS IS A POINTER TO IT, not a second reading: the magnitudes are one estimate per kind of hardware, taken from edgecore/agr-panel-screw@1 for a screw head and edgecore/agr-psu-dc@1 for the ejector latch, applied across the family because these cards share a faceplate. No Casa document states a depth for any of them. Eleven cards carrying 4.2 is ONE estimate written eleven times, not eleven readings that agreed. NOTE this card has NO LAMPS, so the family's dome figure is deliberately not cited here - citing a source for a number a file does not carry is how an inert wrong claim gets started. The three brass comb standoffs above are a separate, PHOTO-MEASURED number and are not part of this family treatment.
provenance.size: ESTIMATED. The guide figures are schematic, not to scale - the drawn chassis aspect is 0.936 against a specified 0.844, and the drawn slot pitches are irregular (108, 130, 78, 112 px for what should be one pitch). Width is arithmetic from Table A-1 instead - 19in rack, ~440mm interior, 14 slots gives 31.43. Height is bracketed by two schematic estimates that disagree by 10 percent - 461mm from the front-view proportion, 417mm from the Fig 1-15 faceplate aspect - so 440 is the midpoint. Needs a caliper

provenance.depth-known-wrong: THE 380.0 IS NOT MERELY UNMEASURED, IT IS IMPOSSIBLE, and this contract now says so in a field a tool can read - size-confidence: {d: known-wrong}. THE CONSTRAINT. Front and rear cards MEET AT A MIDPLANE, which the owner photographed: working/photos/casa/c40g-empty-midplane.png shows the emptied cage with the card guides and the midplane at the back of it, and the opening where the rear I/O card reaches through to the front card. So a front card and its rear partner have to share the chassis depth - 386.0 on the C100G, 388.45 on the C40G. Two cards at 380.0 need 760, which is not a wide error bar, it is twice the box. WHAT THE SHAPE IS, from the owner: "the front card is mostly rectangular, but the I/O card is kind of L SHAPED where the top part of the top connector PASSES THROUGH THE MIDPLANE and plugs into the front card, and the other one is plugged into the midplane. So they ultimately kind of meet in the middle." So the rear card is a body against the midplane PLUS A TONGUE at the top reaching forward through it. NOTE WHAT THAT DOES AND DOES NOT ALLOW, because the obvious rule is wrong. front + rear CAN exceed the chassis depth, by about the tongue length, because the tongue overlaps the front card at a height where the front card is not - they interleave rather than tile. The constraint is therefore an inequality with slack, not an equality. What it cannot absorb is a 374 mm overlap where a tongue is tens of millimetres. ONE PHOTOGRAPH IS USABLE AND IT IS NOT THIS CARD-FAMILY-WIDE. bdm2m-solder-side.jpeg has the faceplate FULLY IN FRAME, so its 345.5 long axis anchors the scale at 5.00 px/mm; the card measures 1336 px from the faceplate to the top of its midplane connectors. Raw that is 267 mm. The shot is NOT orthographic - the PCB reads 4.66 percent wider at the connector end than at the faceplate end, which is perspective, not a taper - so correcting to the mean scale gives about 261, and taking the card top at the outermost connector edge instead pushes it to about 282. CALL IT 270 PLUS OR MINUS 12 AND DO NOT ROUND THAT AWAY. REJECTED, and the rejection is the useful part: bdm2m-top-plan.jpeg and both qam-io-card plan shots have the faceplate CLIPPED BY THE FRAME, so the 345.5 anchor is truncated and every number off them is understated by an unknown amount. Measured anyway, the top-plan gives 227 mm for the same card the solder side gives 270 - a 19 percent disagreement that is entirely the broken anchor. They are not second opinions and must not be averaged in. NOTHING IS REPLACED. 270 plus or minus 12 is one reading of one card from one photograph that fails gate 1, and stamping it on twelve cards would be the family-number pattern doing harm instead of good - these cards share a FACEPLATE, which is established, not a depth, which is not. What is established is that 380.0 cannot be true. WANTED, in order of how much each unlocks: a tape on any one front card (fixes it outright); a tape on any one rear I/O card; an unclipped side-on photograph of a rear card showing where the tongue begins, which would give the midplane position and both halves at once.
provenance.figure-check: drawing - RE-MEASURED against Figure 1-16 at 600 dpi for the v2 bump, rather than trusted because v1 had used them. Twelve U jacks at x 8.685 of a 30.47 plate, y 67.11 to 251.00 on a 16.717 pitch, and six D jacks at x 19.917, y 64.12 to 225.81 on a 32.339 pitch. What this contract carries - 8.61 / 67.11 / 16.729 and 19.87 / 64.18 / 32.356 - agrees with all six to 0.08 mm, so the composed apertures land where the FIGURE puts them and not merely where they used to be. It also re-confirms the separate measurement this card's `rf-layout` note records - the SW card's port field really is shorter and tighter than the plain card's. The drawn jack is 7.85 mm across overall (36 radii, spread 0.4 mm) with a 3.28 mm coloured centre, the same art as Figure 1-15. That is the connector as seen rather than the panel hole - the Radiall sheet gives an MCX bulkhead flange at 6.5 mm dia - so a 4.95 hole under a 6.5 flange is what the figure draws, and v1's 3.88 x 3.88 was smaller than either. Clearance is not close even here, where the pitch is tightest of the two cards - 16.72 between U jacks and 11.2 between the columns against a 4.95 aperture. Nothing had to be compressed.
provenance.layout: drawing - Figure 1-15 of the Casa C100G Hardware Installation Guide (rev 07/08/2022). Twelve U jacks in the left column, six D in the right, interleaved. Port COUNT and ARRANGEMENT are read straight off the figure and are reliable
provenance.mcx-is-recessed: THE OWNER, AGAINST THE HARDWARE: "the MCX connector is RECESSED INTO the faceplate, so it actually doesn't stick out from the faceplate, it's recessed from the faceplate ... whereas the US I/O and the DS I/Os have the F fitting STICKING OUT of the faceplate." Figure 1-12, "RF IO upstream and downstream modules", draws all three rear I/O cards side by side and gives the two connector families completely different treatments: on QAM IO and US IO each F port is a HEX NUT with concentric rings and a shadow - a connector body standing off the plate - while on UPS IO 32 each MCX port is a small flat dark circle with no hex and no body at all. Figures 1-15 and 1-16 draw the 6+12 cards' MCX the same flat way. That is a second source, and it was read after the owner spoke rather than before, so it is confirmation and not the thing that suggested it. THIS CONTRACT CANNOT ACT ON IT YET. The aperture is composed from std/mcx@1, whose relief is {node: barrel, cyl: 2.0} - a PROTRUSION, sourced from the Radiall R113.553.000 side elevation, which is a FRONT-MOUNT bulkhead jack whose flange genuinely does sit on the front of its panel. That part is not wrong about the Radiall connector; it is the wrong VARIANT for every card that uses it, and all five of its users are Casa. Reported to the team lead rather than edited, because it is a std/ part and because the registry note in spec/schemas/standards.yaml says the same thing ("a hole through sheet metal with the barrel standing proud of it"), so the two would have to move together. NO DEPTH IS GUESSED. The owner gave a topology, not a dimension, and nothing in either guide gives a recess depth. WANTED: how far below the faceplate the MCX interface sits - one caliper reading, or a side-on photograph of a 6+12 card.

provenance.power: NONE STATED, and the reasoning is the plain card's - see casa/io-6p12, which carries it in full. provenance.rf-block-3d: CORRECTED, AND THE CORRECTION REVERSES PART OF THE FIRST PASS. Read this before touching the RF section again. WHAT WAS FIXED AND STAYS FIXED: `rf-block` was a BARE RECT. A raised solid is textured from ITS OWN node's art, so a 27.27 x 202.02 rect at fill-opacity 0.18 extruded as a blank translucent slab standing over everything - the "switch I/O card with no ports in it". It is now a GROUP holding that rect and the eighteen U0-U11 / D0-D5 legends, which is right whether or not it is ever raised. WHAT WAS UNDONE: the `out: 15.9` on that group and the `lift: 15.9` on the eighteen composed jacks. Both are gone. THREE INDEPENDENT STRANDS point away from a raised RF section on this card and none of them existed when the 15.9 was written: (1) THE OWNER, LOOKING AT THE HARDWARE: "on some of the 6 plus 12 I/O cards the MCX connector is RECESSED INTO the faceplate, so it actually doesn't stick out from the faceplate ... whereas the US I/O and the DS I/Os have the F fitting STICKING OUT". Jacks mounted on a section standing 15.9 proud would stick out further than anything else on the card, which is the opposite. (2) THE FIGURE DRAWS THE SAME OUTLINE ON THE PLAIN CARD. Figure 1-15, "Casa 6+12 IO modules", and Figure 1-16, "Casa 6+12 Switch I/O modules", are the same artwork in this respect: both enclose the port field in one light rectangle with three hex standoffs inside it, and both put a notched cable retention bracket beside it. So the rectangle is not what distinguishes the switch card. casa/ups-32x4 reads the IDENTICAL artwork as "the footprint the cable retention plate seats against ... drawn as a silkscreen outline, not as relief, because nothing states its depth" - and that call was made independently, before this one, on a different card. (3) THE STANDOFF ARITHMETIC. The owner has since confirmed the topology - FACEPLATE, then RF section, then COMB, with the standoffs "raising the comb up above the faceplate" - so a standoff must clear everything under it. At 9.5 it cannot clear a 15.9 block. That contradiction only exists if the block is raised, and it disappears when it is not, which is evidence rather than convenience. WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED: that Jason's 5/8in reading is wrong. It is a photograph of real hardware and it stays recorded in `shape` above, untouched. Something on this card stands proud; what is now in doubt is whether it is the port field. THIS IS A SUSPENDED MEASUREMENT, NOT A WITHDRAWN ONE. THE RECESS CANNOT BE MODELLED AT ALL TODAY, and that is the real gap. Portrayal has no way to say "this REGION of a module's face is a pocket": `sink` is the right word and exists in the schema, but the extractor only reads it inside a node that already carries data-depth, and `relief.cavity` on a module would turn the whole 380 mm card into a cavity. So the port field is flat - which is wrong, but it is wrong by the same amount the plain card is, instead of wrong in the opposite direction by 15.9. WANTED: a way to declare a face pocket, and then the pocket depth, which no figure or document gives.
provenance.rf-layout: drawing - Figure 1-16, measured separately from Figure 1-15 rather than copied. The SW card's port field is SHORTER and more compressed - it spans 18.6 to 72.7 percent of the plate against the plain card's 12.1 to 73.7, and its U pitch is 4.84 percent of plate height against 5.60. Jason flagged this; the figures agree

This one has slightly different overall dimensions and a section carrying the RF ports that stands about 5/8in (15.9mm) proud of the faceplate, ahead of the comb. The dimensional difference is visible but not yet measured, so this card is modelled at the plain card's envelope for now - that part is ESTIMATED

provenance.standoff-vs-block: THE SWITCH CARD'S STANDOFF HEIGHT WAS NEVER MEASURED, and 9.5 is carried here without confirmation. This entry supersedes the unresolved contradiction the first pass recorded; the owner has since answered the question that was put to him. WHAT HE SETTLED - the topology: "the comb stands in front of the RF block. So it's away from the card ... That's what the standoffs do is they raise the comb up above the faceplate and help hold the cables." So the order outward from the card is FACEPLATE, RF SECTION, COMB, with the comb furthest out. That is now a sourced fact and should not have to be asked again. WHAT HE DID NOT SETTLE - the 9.5. The `comb` entry above has him measuring the brass standoffs about 3/8in proud of the faceplate off ONE C40G rear photograph, and that same photograph contains PLAIN 6+12 CARDS IN SLOTS 0 AND 5 WITH NO RF SECTION AT ALL. On one of those, 9.5 is entirely sensible - there is nothing to clear. So the most likely reading is that 9.5 is a correct measurement OF A DIFFERENT CARD and this card's standoff was never measured. That is a materially different state from "9.5 is wrong", and it is why the number is left alone rather than replaced: 15.9-plus-a-bit would be arithmetic dressed as a measurement. AND IF THE RF SECTION DOES STAND 15.9 PROUD, THE STANDOFF MUST EXCEED IT. That constraint is recorded even though this contract no longer raises the section (see rf-block-3d for why), because it is the check that will catch the error if the section turns out to be raised after all. WANTED: a photograph of a SWITCH I/O card with a rule in frame, or a Casa mechanical drawing. One reading closes both this and the 15.9.

provenance.mcx-is-recessed: THE OWNER, AGAINST THE HARDWARE: "the MCX connector is RECESSED INTO the faceplate, so it actually doesn't stick out from the faceplate, it's recessed from the faceplate ... whereas the US I/O and the DS I/Os have the F fitting STICKING OUT of the faceplate." Recorded here in his terms so it does not have to be rediscovered, and it is a fact about the WORLD, not about a drawing. THE FIGURES AGREE, INDEPENDENTLY. Figure 1-12, "RF IO upstream and downstream modules", draws all three rear I/O cards side by side and gives the two connector families completely different treatments: on QAM IO and US IO each F port is a HEX NUT with concentric rings and a shadow - a connector body standing off the plate - while on UPS IO 32 each MCX port is a small flat dark circle with no hex and no body at all. Figures 1-15 and 1-16 draw the 6+12 cards' MCX the same flat way. That is a second source, and it was read after the owner spoke rather than before, so it is confirmation and not the thing that suggested it. THIS CONTRACT CANNOT ACT ON IT YET. The aperture is composed from std/mcx@1, whose relief is {node: barrel, cyl: 2.0} - a PROTRUSION, sourced from the Radiall R113.553.000 side elevation, which is a FRONT-MOUNT bulkhead jack whose flange genuinely does sit on the front of its panel. That part is not wrong about the Radiall connector; it is the wrong VARIANT for every card that uses it, and all five of its users are Casa. Reported to the team lead rather than edited, because it is a std/ part and because the registry note in spec/schemas/standards.yaml says the same thing ("a hole through sheet metal with the barrel standing proud of it"), so the two would have to move together. NO DEPTH IS GUESSED. The owner gave a topology, not a dimension, and nothing in either guide gives a recess depth. WANTED: how far below the faceplate the MCX interface sits - one caliper reading, or a side-on photograph of a 6+12 card.
provenance.missing-component: THE CABLE COMB IS A REAL, NAMED PART AND THIS LIBRARY DOES NOT HAVE ONE. The `comb` entry above describes it from a photograph; the guides name it and draw it. Figures 1-15 and 1-16 of the C100G guide are captioned "6+12 IO Module w/ cable retention bracket" and "6+12 SW IO Modules w/ cable retention bracket", and each draws the bracket as its OWN object beside the card - a notched strip with the U and D numbers printed between the notches and three screws through it, one per standoff. Figure 2-15 of the C40G guide names the equivalent outright, "UPS 32x4 I/O cable retention plate", and draws it separated from its module. So casa/ is missing a component, not a decision: there is no cable-retention-plate part and none of the four I/O card families can seat one, even though the three standoffs on this faceplate exist for no other purpose than to carry it. Recorded rather than built - building it is a modelling job with its own sourcing, not part of a relief pass. It is NOT casa/cable-manager, which is a different bracket on the chassis front. WRITTEN FIRST IN casa/ups-32x4@1 and restated here.

provenance.rf-block-3d: THE THREE ENTRIES rf-block-3d, mcx-is-recessed AND standoff-vs-block ARE THE SAME TEXT casa/io-6p12-sw@2 CARRIES, written there and copied here. ONE analysis of one defect that both files share because the two skins were built from each other - NOT two independent findings that agreed. Restated rather than cross-referenced for the reason this file's power entry gives. CORRECTED, AND THE CORRECTION REVERSES PART OF THE FIRST PASS. Read this before touching the RF section again. WHAT WAS FIXED AND STAYS FIXED: `rf-block` was a BARE RECT. A raised solid is textured from ITS OWN node's art, so a 27.27 x 202.02 rect at fill-opacity 0.18 extruded as a blank translucent slab standing over everything - the "switch I/O card with no ports in it". It is now a GROUP holding that rect and the eighteen U0-U11 / D0-D5 legends, which is right whether or not it is ever raised. WHAT WAS UNDONE: the `out: 15.9` on that group and the `lift: 15.9` on the eighteen composed jacks. Both are gone. THREE INDEPENDENT STRANDS point away from a raised RF section on this card and none of them existed when the 15.9 was written: (1) THE OWNER, LOOKING AT THE HARDWARE: "on some of the 6 plus 12 I/O cards the MCX connector is RECESSED INTO the faceplate, so it actually doesn't stick out from the faceplate ... whereas the US I/O and the DS I/Os have the F fitting STICKING OUT". Jacks mounted on a section standing 15.9 proud would stick out further than anything else on the card, which is the opposite. (2) THE FIGURE DRAWS THE SAME OUTLINE ON THE PLAIN CARD. Figure 1-15, "Casa 6+12 IO modules", and Figure 1-16, "Casa 6+12 Switch I/O modules", are the same artwork in this respect: both enclose the port field in one light rectangle with three hex standoffs inside it, and both put a notched cable retention bracket beside it. So the rectangle is not what distinguishes the switch card. casa/ups-32x4 reads the IDENTICAL artwork as "the footprint the cable retention plate seats against ... drawn as a silkscreen outline, not as relief, because nothing states its depth" - and that call was made independently, before this one, on a different card. (3) THE STANDOFF ARITHMETIC. The owner has since confirmed the topology - FACEPLATE, then RF section, then COMB, with the standoffs "raising the comb up above the faceplate" - so a standoff must clear everything under it. At 9.5 it cannot clear a 15.9 block. That contradiction only exists if the block is raised, and it disappears when it is not, which is evidence rather than convenience. WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED: that Jason's 5/8in reading is wrong. It is a photograph of real hardware and it stays recorded in `shape` above, untouched. Something on this card stands proud; what is now in doubt is whether it is the port field. THIS IS A SUSPENDED MEASUREMENT, NOT A WITHDRAWN ONE. THE RECESS CANNOT BE MODELLED AT ALL TODAY, and that is the real gap. Portrayal has no way to say "this REGION of a module's face is a pocket": `sink` is the right word and exists in the schema, but the extractor only reads it inside a node that already carries data-depth, and `relief.cavity` on a module would turn the whole 380 mm card into a cavity. So the port field is flat - which is wrong, but it is wrong by the same amount the plain card is, instead of wrong in the opposite direction by 15.9. WANTED: a way to declare a face pocket, and then the pocket depth, which no figure or document gives.

provenance.standoff-vs-block: THE SWITCH CARD'S STANDOFF HEIGHT WAS NEVER MEASURED, and 9.5 is carried here without confirmation. This entry supersedes the unresolved contradiction the first pass recorded; the owner has since answered the question that was put to him. WHAT HE SETTLED - the topology: "the comb stands in front of the RF block. So it's away from the card ... That is now a sourced fact and should not have to be asked again. WHAT HE DID NOT SETTLE - the 9.5. On one of those, 9.5 is entirely sensible - there is nothing to clear. So the most likely reading is that 9.5 is a correct measurement OF A DIFFERENT CARD and this card's standoff was never measured. That is a materially different state from "9.5 is wrong", and it is why the number is left alone rather than replaced: 15.9-plus-a-bit would be arithmetic dressed as a measurement. components.description: Casa C-series Power Entry Module. Two per chassis, PEM B on the left and PEM A on the right when facing the rear. Each carries four 30 A power branches. A branch is a -48/-60 VDC feed with its return, landed on a pair of studs in one of the two terminal blocks, and protected by its own rocker circuit breaker in the row above. The faceplate draws a leader line from each branch's terminal-cover screw up to the breaker that protects it.
components.name: pem

provenance.body: the box behind the face is the size entry's own depth, 250.0, which that entry already records as ESTIMATED - not a second claim. `body` is declared so the module draws as a solid that fills its bay instead of a floating faceplate; without it the 3D viewer has no box to build and the PEM reads as art painted on the rear plate, which is what the owner is seeing. NOTE that declaring it is necessary but not sufficient here: the viewer builds FRU groups only for data-class psu, fan and tab (library/demo2/relief.js), and this module is class power, so it will not eject until that list admits it. Reported rather than worked around by mislabelling a power ENTRY module as a psu
provenance.branches: datasheet - "Each PEM provides power terminals for four 30A power branches. Each power branch consists of a -48VDC cable and a corresponding return cable protected by a 30A circuit breaker" (Chapter 1). provenance.breaker-order: drawing - measured breaker centres are 18.04 / 37.99 / 61.36 / 81.33 percent of the faceplate, so four evenly-paired rockers. They map to Branch 4 / 3 / 2 / 1 LEFT TO RIGHT, which the leader lines in the figure make unambiguous

provenance.electrical: datasheet - Table A-1 of the C100G install guide gives "Voltage -42 to -60VDC" and "Current 20A nominal per feed"; the chassis nameplate reproduced at Figure 1-3 gives "-48VDC, 30A per Feed (4+4 Feeds)". Four feeds per PEM, two PEMs, hence 4+4

provenance.labels: Jason - the guide interrupts each leader where its Branch label sits. At this drawing scale that reads as text cutting through the line, so the lines are drawn UNBROKEN and the labels moved clear - outer labels above their horizontal run, inner labels below theirs. The -48/-60VDC and RTN captions are centred in the clear lane between each block and the nearest leader vertical, at a size that fits it, rather than overlapping the block
provenance.layout: drawing - Figure 1-6 of the C100G Hardware Installation Guide, "C100G Power Entry Module, terminal covers removed". Every feature position below is a measured PERCENTAGE of that figure's faceplate, stretched onto this module's size. The figure's own aspect is 3.43 against this module's 2.26, so its absolute geometry is not usable - the same trap the isolated card figures set, and the reason fractions are used throughout
provenance.leaders: drawing - the routing is NOT uniform. The two OUTER branches (4 and 1) leave their rocker's outer side edge at 12.9 percent height, run outward to 3.41 / 96.27 percent, then drop to the cover screw. The two INNER branches (3 and 2) drop from their rocker's bottom CENTRE and run inward to the screw. Each run is interrupted where its Branch label sits
provenance.power: NO WATT FIGURE IS STATED, and it is not there to be found. Casa rates a power ENTRY module in amps and volts, never in watts. Recording one would mean multiplying, and the multiplication has no single answer: the guide gives TWO current figures - Table A-1s "20A nominal per feed" and the chassis nameplates "30A per Feed" - across a voltage range 18 V wide, so V x I lands anywhere from about 810 W to 1800 W per feed depending on which pair you pick. Any one number would be this library choosing a point the vendor deliberately left open. What IS stated is recorded in attrs. The L27 warning stays standing: it is the honest record that the figure is missing, and an unsourced watt figure is the same number minus the warning. Note too that a power entry module does not convert or regulate - it filters and distributes what the plant feeds it - so its rating is a current-carrying limit rather than a continuous output in the sense power-output-w means
provenance.relief: estimated, and the split matters. WHAT is raised, what it is, and where it sits are read off Figure 1-6, "C100G Power Entry Module, terminal covers removed" - the breakers are bezels standing off the plate, the terminal blocks are moulded bodies with the studs on their faces, the cover screws are captive brass, the HS control is a pushbutton and the three indicators are lamps. That is what an elevation can answer and it is what this contract was missing. HOW FAR each stands proud is NOT in any Casa document. Neither hardware installation guide, nor Table A-1, nor the chassis nameplate carries a single Z dimension for this module; the only figures of it are flat elevations, and this one fails the orthographic gate outright at an aspect of 3.43 against this module's 2.26, so even a fraction off it would be worthless. Searched: both guides for "Power Entry", "PEM", "terminal", "breaker" and the Appendix A tables. So every mm here is ESTIMATED, and each is the Portrayal library's existing figure for the same class of hardware rather than a fresh guess: the 2.2 mm nut is agr-psu-dc's, the 1.6 mm screw head is edgecore/agr-panel-screw@1 and the 0.3 mm lamp dome is common/led-dot@1 - AND NONE OF THE THREE WAS MEASURED THERE EITHER, which an earlier version of this entry got wrong by calling the nut "read off real Edgecore terminal hardware". What the owner measured on that PSU is its walls at 12.7 and its bolts at 6.35; the nut subdivides the 6.35. agr-panel-screw says "estimated - not measured" outright and led-dot carries no depth provenance at all. The two with no library precedent are the 3.0 mm breaker bezel and the 6.0 mm terminal block, and they are flagged here rather than buried: they are the only invented magnitudes in this file. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: a caliper on a C100G PEM, or any three-quarter photograph of the rear face - one oblique shot with the terminal covers off would fix the block height, the bezel and the stud length together

provenance.terminals: drawing - two blocks at 6.99 and 71.1 percent, each 21.5 percent wide. Figure 1-6 draws them 61.9 percent tall with an uneven split; corrected on Jason's eye against the hardware to 40.4mm total in TWO EQUAL halves of 20.2, top edge unchanged. Breaker height likewise cut a quarter, 19.5 to 14.6. Four studs per block in 2 columns x 2 rows: the TOP row is -48/-60VDC and the BOTTOM row is RTN, labelled once per block in the central gap. Left block holds Branch 4 (left column) and Branch 3; right block holds Branch 2 and Branch 1 (right column)

components.description: Casa RF Downstream I/O module (RFD) - the rear half of a DQM position, carrying the eight downstream F-type ports for one DS 8x8, DS 8x96 or DS 8x192 line card in the paired front slot. Silkscreened QAM IO. It carries no electronics of its own that the guide describes; it is the mechanical and electrical QAM connection to the HFC network.
components.name: rfd

provenance.body-shape-not-a-box: THIS CARD IS AN L IN SIDE ELEVATION AND PORTRAYAL CANNOT SAY SO. The owner: the rear I/O card has a main body that seats against the midplane plus a TONGUE at the top that passes THROUGH an opening in the midplane and plugs directly into the front card. `body:` takes a depth, a colour, an optional smaller footprint and a plate - all of which describe a BOX. There is no way to declare a body that is full slot height for part of its depth and a narrower section for the rest. So this contract declares NO body rather than declaring a box that is wrong in a way nothing records. That is the same call this library made on the MCX recess: where the vocabulary cannot express the shape, say so and leave the record, because a wrong shape with no note is worse than an absent one. WANTED: either a body section - a list of depth bands with their own footprints - or the honest acknowledgement that a mid-plane-mating card needs its own kind.
provenance.depth-known-wrong: THE 380.0 IS NOT MERELY UNMEASURED, IT IS IMPOSSIBLE, and this contract now says so in a field a tool can read - size-confidence: {d: known-wrong}. THE CONSTRAINT. Front and rear cards MEET AT A MIDPLANE, which the owner photographed: working/photos/casa/c40g-empty-midplane.png shows the emptied cage with the card guides and the midplane at the back of it, and the opening where the rear I/O card reaches through to the front card. So a front card and its rear partner have to share the chassis depth - 386.0 on the C100G, 388.45 on the C40G. Two cards at 380.0 need 760, which is not a wide error bar, it is twice the box. WHAT THE SHAPE IS, from the owner: "the front card is mostly rectangular, but the I/O card is kind of L SHAPED where the top part of the top connector PASSES THROUGH THE MIDPLANE and plugs into the front card, and the other one is plugged into the midplane. So they ultimately kind of meet in the middle." So the rear card is a body against the midplane PLUS A TONGUE at the top reaching forward through it. NOTE WHAT THAT DOES AND DOES NOT ALLOW, because the obvious rule is wrong. front + rear CAN exceed the chassis depth, by about the tongue length, because the tongue overlaps the front card at a height where the front card is not - they interleave rather than tile. The constraint is therefore an inequality with slack, not an equality. What it cannot absorb is a 374 mm overlap where a tongue is tens of millimetres. ONE PHOTOGRAPH IS USABLE AND IT IS NOT THIS CARD-FAMILY-WIDE. bdm2m-solder-side.jpeg has the faceplate FULLY IN FRAME, so its 345.5 long axis anchors the scale at 5.00 px/mm; the card measures 1336 px from the faceplate to the top of its midplane connectors. Raw that is 267 mm. The shot is NOT orthographic - the PCB reads 4.66 percent wider at the connector end than at the faceplate end, which is perspective, not a taper - so correcting to the mean scale gives about 261, and taking the card top at the outermost connector edge instead pushes it to about 282. CALL IT 270 PLUS OR MINUS 12 AND DO NOT ROUND THAT AWAY. REJECTED, and the rejection is the useful part: bdm2m-top-plan.jpeg and both qam-io-card plan shots have the faceplate CLIPPED BY THE FRAME, so the 345.5 anchor is truncated and every number off them is understated by an unknown amount. Measured anyway, the top-plan gives 227 mm for the same card the solder side gives 270 - a 19 percent disagreement that is entirely the broken anchor. They are not second opinions and must not be averaged in. NOTHING IS REPLACED. 270 plus or minus 12 is one reading of one card from one photograph that fails gate 1, and stamping it on twelve cards would be the family-number pattern doing harm instead of good - these cards share a FACEPLATE, which is established, not a depth, which is not. What is established is that 380.0 cannot be true. WANTED, in order of how much each unlocks: a tape on any one front card (fixes it outright); a tape on any one rear I/O card; an unclipped side-on photograph of a rear card showing where the tongue begins, which would give the midplane position and both halves at once.
provenance.f-type-stands-proud: THE OWNER, AGAINST THE HARDWARE: "the US I/O and the DS I/Os have the F fitting STICKING OUT of the faceplate", against the MCX cards where "the MCX connector is RECESSED INTO the faceplate". This card is on the PROUD side of that distinction and it must not inherit the MCX treatment. THIS SENTENCE IS COPIED FROM casa/io-6p12-sw@2, where the pair was written up first. One statement about one pair of families, restated where it applies. NOTHING NEEDED CHANGING, WHICH IS THE POINT OF RECORDING IT. std/f-type@1 already models the connector as proud - a hex nut at cyl 2.4 with the 3/8-32 threaded neck as a threaded cyl running 2.4 to 13.0 off the face - because the F thread IS the mating interface and has to be outside the panel. So the owner's statement CONFIRMS an existing model rather than correcting one, and this entry exists so that a later pass correcting the MCX cards does not sweep these two along with them. THE FIGURE AGREES AND SHOWS THE CONTRAST DIRECTLY. Figure 1-12 (C100G), "RF IO upstream and downstream modules", draws QAM IO, US IO and UPS IO 32 side by side: every F port is a hex nut with concentric rings and a drop shadow, every MCX port on the neighbouring card is a flat dark circle with no body at all. One figure, both families, opposite treatments.
provenance.furniture: drawing - the same figure. Two captive screws on the card centreline, the orange band(s) and the legend below them, and the latch strip on the RIGHT of the plate. Note that casa/io-6p12 draws its latch strip on the LEFT while both Figure 1-12 and Figure 1-15 put it on the right; these cards follow the figures
provenance.layout: drawing - Figure 1-12 of the Casa C100G Hardware Installation Guide (rev 07/08/2022), "RF IO upstream and downstream modules", which draws all three rear I/O cards side by side. Port COUNT, port ORDER and the column arrangement are read straight off it and are reliable; positions are taken as fractions of the drawn plate, measured by colour detection at 600 dpi
provenance.ports: drawing - Table A-8 of the same guide, headed "RFD specifications", gives "8 ports per RFD" and a connector row reading "F-type, 75 ohm, SCTE compliant" with a maximum torque of 20 inch-pounds. The aperture itself is the registry's `f-type` key - Casa states the connector type and no dimension, which is exactly the case the registry exists for
provenance.positions: drawing - one column at 0.528 of the plate width, eight ports on a uniform 26.43 mm pitch from 77.65. The measured per-port x scatters +-0.4 mm down the card, which is figure jitter rather than a real skew, so a single column x is used. Note the RFU's column measures 1.15 mm further right on the same figure; the two cards are NOT forced onto one x, because nothing says they share one
provenance.power: NO FIGURE. Tables A-8 and A-9 give the RFD and RFU ports and connector type and no power at all, and Table A-3's DQM figures are headed "Maximum consumption WITH I/O module", so the only published numbers already contain this card and no document divides them. L27 stands, and the C100G and C40G `paired-module-power` gap carries the reason
provenance.relief: the C100G/C40G card family treatment - two captive screws (cyl 1.6), the ejector latch strip (out 4.2). THE FULL ARGUMENT IS IN casa/bdm@1 AND THIS IS A POINTER TO IT, not a second reading: the magnitudes are one estimate per kind of hardware, taken from edgecore/agr-panel-screw@1 for a screw head and edgecore/agr-psu-dc@1 for the ejector latch, applied across the family because these cards share a faceplate. No Casa document states a depth for any of them. Eleven cards carrying 4.2 is ONE estimate written eleven times, not eleven readings that agreed. NOTE this card has NO LAMPS, so the family's dome figure is deliberately not cited here - citing a source for a number a file does not carry is how an inert wrong claim gets started.
provenance.size: ESTIMATED, and shared with the whole C100G/C40G rear-slot family. Figure 1-12 is schematic - it draws these three cards 309, 295 and 288 px wide for one physical card, and the guide's chassis aspect is 0.936 against a specified 0.844 - so nothing absolute is taken from it. The envelope is the rear-slot bay in the C100G device manifest, 30.47 x 345.5, and the depth is the family estimate carried by casa/io-6p12

provenance.faceplate-hardware-photo: THE OWNER SUPPLIED AN ISOMETRIC OF THE C100G FRONT and it corrects the SHAPE of two things on this faceplate. working/photos/casa/ - c100g-front-isometric.png and the crop crop-ejectors.png, read at high zoom. WHAT IT SETTLES: - The captive screw is not a flat slotted head. It is a substantial BLACK KNURLED KNOB standing well proud, with a dark top face and a light metallic band. `knurl` is added for that reason - it is a shape fact and costs no dimension. The drawn 2D head is still a slotted circle and is NOT redrawn; the figures draw it that way and this photograph cannot give a true elevation of it. - The EJECTOR LEVER is the most prominent thing on the whole face: a large CURVED BLACK lever, not the rounded strip this skin draws, with a thin vertical linkage rod running down the card from the knob to it. - RELATIVE PROMINENCE, which is the one quantitative thing a perspective view CAN give: lever stands proud of knob stands proud of lamp. This contract already orders them that way - 4.2, 1.6, 0.3 - so the photograph CONFIRMS the ordering rather than correcting it. Only the absolute magnitudes are understated, and it gives no absolute magnitude. WHAT IT DOES NOT SETTLE, and why nothing else moved. It is a three-quarter view: every forward projection is foreshortened by an unknown factor, nothing of known size is in frame, and the one feature that looks measurable - the knob ellipse - needs a diameter nobody has. So it fails gate 1 outright, exactly as the Cisco perspective figures did. THE LEVER SILHOUETTE IS DELIBERATELY NOT REDRAWN: the true elevation outline of a curved lever is precisely what a three-quarter crop cannot give, and drawing sixteen faceplates from it would replace a sourced schematic strip with an invented curve. The 4.2 stays, marked `borrowed`. WANTED, and it closes both at once: ONE STRAIGHT-ON PHOTOGRAPH OF A SINGLE CARD, with a rule or any part of known size in frame. That would give the lever its silhouette AND its projection, and it is the cheapest open question on this family. THIS ENTRY IS ONE READING OF ONE PHOTOGRAPH restated across the thirteen front-slot cards that share this faceplate. The photograph shows DS 8X96, US 16X4 and SMM 8X10G specifically; the rest inherit it because the family shares a plate, which the DS/US positions provenance already establishes to the millimetre. It is NOT thirteen observations. The REAR cards - the 6+12 I/O family, rfd, rfu-16x8, ups-32x4, lc-sw-bdm and the two SMM Switch BDMs - are NOT in this photograph and are deliberately left alone.
provenance.lamp-pitch: drawing-measured, BY A DIFFERENT ANCHOR, and the difference matters. Figure 1-13 of the C40G guide, "Standard SMM 2x10GE (eight GigE, two 10GigE ports)", draws this card, but EVERY FIGURE OF THE SMM PAIR IN BOTH GUIDES IS CLIPPED at the plate edge - C40G Figures 1-13 to 1-16 and C100G Figures 1-7 to 1-10 all run the plate grey to the last pixel row - so the drawn plate height cannot be recovered and the plate-fraction method used on casa/bdm and on the DS/US cards is unavailable here. THE TWO CAPTIVE SCREWS ARE THE ANCHOR INSTEAD: this skin places them at cy 6.00 and 339.50, 333.50 mm apart, and the figure draws both. They measure at rows 28.0 and 1390.0, a separation of 1362.0 px, giving 4.08396 px/mm and an implied plate top at row 3.50. The plate box read y 3 to 1415 independently, so on this card the anchor recovers the drawn top edge to half a pixel. Lamp centres then land at 272.40, 276.05 and 279.70 for a pitch of 3.65 mm. THE METHOD WAS VALIDATED ON A CONTROL BEFORE BEING TRUSTED HERE: run against the un-clipped BDM in Figure 1-20, the screw anchor puts the plate top at row 71.62 where the plate box reads 70 - agreement to 1.6 px. THE 3.0 LAMP DIAMETER IS UNCHANGED AND STILL UNMEASURED, for the reason the BDM gave: these drawings are anisotropic, so a round lamp scales to two different diameters depending on the axis, which tells you the drawing is wrong rather than telling you the size.
provenance.lamps: drawing - Figure 1-7 prints STATUS, ACTIVE, ALARM top to bottom, as do Figures 1-8 and 1-9, and the CSC8x10G photograph shows the same order at a legible size. casa/smm-8x10g once drew the three the other way up with ALARM at the top, and this entry used to record that disagreement as live. provenance.depth-known-wrong: THE 380.0 IS NOT MERELY UNMEASURED, IT IS IMPOSSIBLE, and this contract now says so in a field a tool can read - size-confidence: {d: known-wrong}. THE CONSTRAINT. Front and rear cards MEET AT A MIDPLANE, which the owner photographed: working/photos/casa/c40g-empty-midplane.png shows the emptied cage with the card guides and the midplane at the back of it, and the opening where the rear I/O card reaches through to the front card. So a front card and its rear partner have to share the chassis depth - 386.0 on the C100G, 388.45 on the C40G. Two cards at 380.0 need 760, which is not a wide error bar, it is twice the box. WHAT THE SHAPE IS, from the owner: "the front card is mostly rectangular, but the I/O card is kind of L SHAPED where the top part of the top connector PASSES THROUGH THE MIDPLANE and plugs into the front card, and the other one is plugged into the midplane. So they ultimately kind of meet in the middle." So the rear card is a body against the midplane PLUS A TONGUE at the top reaching forward through it. NOTE WHAT THAT DOES AND DOES NOT ALLOW, because the obvious rule is wrong. front + rear CAN exceed the chassis depth, by about the tongue length, because the tongue overlaps the front card at a height where the front card is not - they interleave rather than tile. The constraint is therefore an inequality with slack, not an equality. What it cannot absorb is a 374 mm overlap where a tongue is tens of millimetres. ONE PHOTOGRAPH IS USABLE AND IT IS NOT THIS CARD-FAMILY-WIDE. bdm2m-solder-side.jpeg has the faceplate FULLY IN FRAME, so its 345.5 long axis anchors the scale at 5.00 px/mm; the card measures 1336 px from the faceplate to the top of its midplane connectors. Raw that is 267 mm. The shot is NOT orthographic - the PCB reads 4.66 percent wider at the connector end than at the faceplate end, which is perspective, not a taper - so correcting to the mean scale gives about 261, and taking the card top at the outermost connector edge instead pushes it to about 282. CALL IT 270 PLUS OR MINUS 12 AND DO NOT ROUND THAT AWAY. REJECTED, and the rejection is the useful part: bdm2m-top-plan.jpeg and both qam-io-card plan shots have the faceplate CLIPPED BY THE FRAME, so the 345.5 anchor is truncated and every number off them is understated by an unknown amount. Measured anyway, the top-plan gives 227 mm for the same card the solder side gives 270 - a 19 percent disagreement that is entirely the broken anchor. They are not second opinions and must not be averaged in. NOTHING IS REPLACED. 270 plus or minus 12 is one reading of one card from one photograph that fails gate 1, and stamping it on twelve cards would be the family-number pattern doing harm instead of good - these cards share a FACEPLATE, which is established, not a depth, which is not. What is established is that 380.0 cannot be true. WANTED, in order of how much each unlocks: a tape on any one front card (fixes it outright); a tape on any one rear I/O card; an unclipped side-on photograph of a rear card showing where the tongue begins, which would give the midplane position and both halves at once.
provenance.faceplate-hardware-photo: THE OWNER SUPPLIED AN ISOMETRIC OF THE C100G FRONT and it corrects the SHAPE of two things on this faceplate. working/photos/casa/ - c100g-front-isometric.png and the crop crop-ejectors.png, read at high zoom. WHAT IT SETTLES: - The captive screw is not a flat slotted head. It is a substantial BLACK KNURLED KNOB standing well proud, with a dark top face and a light metallic band. `knurl` is added for that reason - it is a shape fact and costs no dimension. The drawn 2D head is still a slotted circle and is NOT redrawn; the figures draw it that way and this photograph cannot give a true elevation of it. - The EJECTOR LEVER is the most prominent thing on the whole face: a large CURVED BLACK lever, not the rounded strip this skin draws, with a thin vertical linkage rod running down the card from the knob to it. - RELATIVE PROMINENCE, which is the one quantitative thing a perspective view CAN give: lever stands proud of knob stands proud of lamp. This contract already orders them that way - 4.2, 1.6, 0.3 - so the photograph CONFIRMS the ordering rather than correcting it. Only the absolute magnitudes are understated, and it gives no absolute magnitude. WHAT IT DOES NOT SETTLE, and why nothing else moved. It is a three-quarter view: every forward projection is foreshortened by an unknown factor, nothing of known size is in frame, and the one feature that looks measurable - the knob ellipse - needs a diameter nobody has. So it fails gate 1 outright, exactly as the Cisco perspective figures did. THE LEVER SILHOUETTE IS DELIBERATELY NOT REDRAWN: the true elevation outline of a curved lever is precisely what a three-quarter crop cannot give, and drawing sixteen faceplates from it would replace a sourced schematic strip with an invented curve. The 4.2 stays, marked `borrowed`. WANTED, and it closes both at once: ONE STRAIGHT-ON PHOTOGRAPH OF A SINGLE CARD, with a rule or any part of known size in frame. That would give the lever its silhouette AND its projection, and it is the cheapest open question on this family. THIS ENTRY IS ONE READING OF ONE PHOTOGRAPH restated across the thirteen front-slot cards that share this faceplate. The photograph shows DS 8X96, US 16X4 and SMM 8X10G specifically; the rest inherit it because the family shares a plate, which the DS/US positions provenance already establishes to the millimetre. It is NOT thirteen observations. The REAR cards - the 6+12 I/O family, rfd, rfu-16x8, ups-32x4, lc-sw-bdm and the two SMM Switch BDMs - are NOT in this photograph and are deliberately left alone.
provenance.layout: drawing - Figure 1-9 of the Casa C100G Hardware Installation Guide (rev 07/08/2022) gives the faceplate order top to bottom: SMM 300G, XG0 through XG9, CG0, CG1, 10/100MI, IOIOI, then STATUS, ACTIVE, ALARM. Unlike the SMM 8x10G the management jack is at the BOTTOM, after the ports, not at the top
provenance.legend: drawing - the model legend sits between TWO orange bands, not below one, which is the first thing three product photographs settle and which casa/smm-8x10g does not show. Position is casa/bdm's, from Figure 1-14: 20.42 and 33.76. provenance.port-lamps: photo-inferred - each optical port carries one lamp ABOVE and one BELOW its legend, in a column to the right of the cages, which is why the cages sit left of the plate centre at 12.6 rather than centred. provenance.positions: photo-measured - the SMM300G data sheet product photograph, read as fractions of the known 345.5 card height (the plate renders 3438px for 345.5mm). provenance.relief: the C100G/C40G card family treatment - two captive screws (cyl 1.6), the ejector latch strip (out 4.2) and the 3 status lamps and 24 port lamps (dome 0.3). THE FULL ARGUMENT IS IN casa/bdm@1 AND THIS IS A POINTER TO IT, not a second reading: the three magnitudes are one estimate per kind of hardware, taken from edgecore/agr-panel-screw@1, edgecore/agr-psu-dc@1 and common/led-dot@1 - NONE of which measured them, which is why all three are tokened `estimated` rather than `borrowed` - applied across the family because these cards share a faceplate. provenance.rotation: every cage is ROTATED 90. A ganged SFP opening is 14.25 x 10.4 and the faceplate is only 30.47 wide, so the long axis has to run down the card. The SMM300G photograph measures the openings at 10.1mm across (7.5 to 17.6mm from the plate edge on the CSC, independently), which is the rotated width, and the vertical pitch measures 14.0-14.2 against the 14.25 the standard specifies
provenance.size: shared with the rest of the C100G front-card family, taken from the chassis slot envelope (30.47 x 345.5, C100G device manifest); the depth is the family estimate carried by casa/smm-8x10g
provenance.two-datasheets: THE TWO SMM300G DATA SHEETS ARE DIFFERENT DOCUMENTS AND THEY DISAGREE. Data-Sheet-SMM300G (SMM300G-DS_RevA, 12-2024) is CommScope-branded and covers the SMM300G and the newer SMM300Gm; Casa-Datasheet-SMM300G (SMM300G R2, May 2018) is Casa-branded and covers the SMM300G alone. The dated 2024 sheet is preferred. Where they differ: (1) the 2018 sheet claims 'IEEE 1588v2 Precision Timing AND SyncE' / 'Synchronous Ethernet support', the 2024 sheet drops SyncE from the wording entirely, so only 1588v2 is recorded here; (2) the 2018 sheet advertises 10G EPON OLT / DPoEv2 service with 16x10G PON cards, which the 2024 sheet does not mention; (3) the 2018 sheet scopes the two-module limit to the C100G, the 2024 sheet to 'a chassis'; (4) the 2024 sheet contradicts ITSELF - its spec table says ten 10GE interfaces while its ordering table describes C100G-SMM-300-GM as '2X100GbE SFP + 8X10GbE SFP'. The install guide, the figure and the photograph all show ten, so ten is modelled and the ordering line is recorded as the vendor's error

provenance.lamp-pitch: drawing-measured, BY A DIFFERENT ANCHOR, and the difference matters. Figure 1-14 of the C40G guide, "High-density SMM 8x10GigE (eight 10GigE, two GigE ports)", draws this card, but EVERY FIGURE OF THE SMM PAIR IN BOTH GUIDES IS CLIPPED at the plate edge - C40G Figures 1-13 to 1-16 and C100G Figures 1-7 to 1-10 all run the plate grey to the last pixel row - so the drawn plate height cannot be recovered and the plate-fraction method used on casa/bdm and on the DS/US cards is unavailable here. THE TWO CAPTIVE SCREWS ARE THE ANCHOR INSTEAD: this skin places them at cy 6.00 and 339.50, 333.50 mm apart, and the figure draws both. They measure at rows 15.0 and 1370.0, a separation of 1355.0 px, giving 4.06297 px/mm and an implied plate top at row -9.38. The implied top edge is NEGATIVE, which is the clipping stated as a number: the crop starts 9 px inside the plate. Lamp centres then land at 272.60, 276.25 and 279.90 for a pitch of 3.65 mm. THE METHOD WAS VALIDATED ON A CONTROL BEFORE BEING TRUSTED HERE: run against the un-clipped BDM in Figure 1-20, the screw anchor puts the plate top at row 71.62 where the plate box reads 70 - agreement to 1.6 px. It carries a systematic though, and it is stated rather than hidden: the two anchors disagree by 0.9 percent, because the drawn plate is 1417 px where the screws imply 1404, so a position taken this way is about 2 mm softer than one taken from a plate box. Both underlying numbers - the 345.5 height and the 6.00/339.50 screw positions - are conventions rather than measurements, which is why neither anchor can settle the other. It replaces a 6.6 mm pitch that was never measured on this card or on any other: casa/bdm's provenance said outright that 6.6 was picked so the lamps would "read as separate indicators", and the same three numbers had been carried onto every Casa front card. This entry is a separate reading of a separate plate and is not that number under a new name. THE 3.0 LAMP DIAMETER IS UNCHANGED AND STILL UNMEASURED, for the reason the BDM gave: these drawings are anisotropic, so a round lamp scales to two different diameters depending on the axis, which tells you the drawing is wrong rather than telling you the size.

provenance.body-shape-not-a-box: THIS CARD IS AN L IN SIDE ELEVATION AND PORTRAYAL CANNOT SAY SO. The owner: the rear I/O card has a main body that seats against the midplane plus a TONGUE at the top that passes THROUGH an opening in the midplane and plugs directly into the front card. `body:` takes a depth, a colour, an optional smaller footprint and a plate - all of which describe a BOX. There is no way to declare a body that is full slot height for part of its depth and a narrower section for the rest. So this contract declares NO body rather than declaring a box that is wrong in a way nothing records. That is the same call this library made on the MCX recess: where the vocabulary cannot express the shape, say so and leave the record, because a wrong shape with no note is worse than an absent one. WANTED: either a body section - a list of depth bands with their own footprints - or the honest acknowledgement that a mid-plane-mating card needs its own kind.
provenance.depth-known-wrong: THE 380.0 IS NOT MERELY UNMEASURED, IT IS IMPOSSIBLE, and this contract now says so in a field a tool can read - size-confidence: {d: known-wrong}. THE CONSTRAINT. Front and rear cards MEET AT A MIDPLANE, which the owner photographed: working/photos/casa/c40g-empty-midplane.png shows the emptied cage with the card guides and the midplane at the back of it, and the opening where the rear I/O card reaches through to the front card. So a front card and its rear partner have to share the chassis depth - 386.0 on the C100G, 388.45 on the C40G. Two cards at 380.0 need 760, which is not a wide error bar, it is twice the box. WHAT THE SHAPE IS, from the owner: "the front card is mostly rectangular, but the I/O card is kind of L SHAPED where the top part of the top connector PASSES THROUGH THE MIDPLANE and plugs into the front card, and the other one is plugged into the midplane. So they ultimately kind of meet in the middle." So the rear card is a body against the midplane PLUS A TONGUE at the top reaching forward through it. NOTE WHAT THAT DOES AND DOES NOT ALLOW, because the obvious rule is wrong. front + rear CAN exceed the chassis depth, by about the tongue length, because the tongue overlaps the front card at a height where the front card is not - they interleave rather than tile. The constraint is therefore an inequality with slack, not an equality. What it cannot absorb is a 374 mm overlap where a tongue is tens of millimetres. ONE PHOTOGRAPH IS USABLE AND IT IS NOT THIS CARD-FAMILY-WIDE. bdm2m-solder-side.jpeg has the faceplate FULLY IN FRAME, so its 345.5 long axis anchors the scale at 5.00 px/mm; the card measures 1336 px from the faceplate to the top of its midplane connectors. Raw that is 267 mm. The shot is NOT orthographic - the PCB reads 4.66 percent wider at the connector end than at the faceplate end, which is perspective, not a taper - so correcting to the mean scale gives about 261, and taking the card top at the outermost connector edge instead pushes it to about 282. CALL IT 270 PLUS OR MINUS 12 AND DO NOT ROUND THAT AWAY. REJECTED, and the rejection is the useful part: bdm2m-top-plan.jpeg and both qam-io-card plan shots have the faceplate CLIPPED BY THE FRAME, so the 345.5 anchor is truncated and every number off them is understated by an unknown amount. Measured anyway, the top-plan gives 227 mm for the same card the solder side gives 270 - a 19 percent disagreement that is entirely the broken anchor. They are not second opinions and must not be averaged in. NOTHING IS REPLACED. 270 plus or minus 12 is one reading of one card from one photograph that fails gate 1, and stamping it on twelve cards would be the family-number pattern doing harm instead of good - these cards share a FACEPLATE, which is established, not a depth, which is not. What is established is that 380.0 cannot be true. WANTED, in order of how much each unlocks: a tape on any one front card (fixes it outright); a tape on any one rear I/O card; an unclipped side-on photograph of a rear card showing where the tongue begins, which would give the midplane position and both halves at once.

No Casa document states a depth for any of them. Eleven cards carrying 4.2 is ONE estimate written eleven times, not eleven readings that agreed.
