Cisco ASR 9006 Router and Cisco ASR 9904 Router: All chassis line cards and RSP cards are front-facing and mounted HORIZONTALLY, with ejector levers and captive screws at the left and right ends of each card. Cisco ASR 9906 Router: ... mounted vertically ... Cisco ASR 9910 Router: ... vertically ... Cisco ASR 9922 Router: ... vertically ... Cisco ASR 9912 Router: ... vertically.' So only the ASR 9006 and the ASR 9904 lay their cards flat and rotate the bay; the other five place this component unrotated. The ejector-lever wording is the tell and it is why the guide is worth quoting rather than paraphrasing - 'top and bottom' means vertical, 'left and right ends' means horizontal, and the RU height of a chassis does not decide it.
provenance.generation: sourced, and it matters because it decides which cage this card has. The Lawful Intercept configuration guide names 'A9K-8X100GE-X-TR' among 'Cisco ASR 9000 4th Generation QSFP28 based dense 100GE line cards', alongside A9K-16X100GE-TR, A9K-32X100GE-TR and A99-16x100-X-SE. So the -X- pair is QSFP28, NOT the CPAK of the similarly named A9K-8X100GE-SE/-TR, and the two must not borrow geometry from each other. The artwork agrees independently: this master's eight apertures measure 8.67 x 18.56 mm, the QSFP28 cage the other QSFP28 cards in this stencil use, while the CPAK master's measure 6.93 x 29.58.
provenance.layout: drawing - the Cisco Visio master, scaled to the datasheet's own overall dimensions. CAUTION for anyone re-deriving this: index.json's props.height_in and width_in are the Visio SHAPE box, not the card. They read 1.72 x 14.75 in for EVERY card master, against the datasheet's 1.63 x 15.58 in, and are 5 percent out in both axes. The ART is orthographic and does carry geometry: taking Cisco's stated W - which the spec table says 'includes ejector bracket/lever' - as the full long extent of the art puts the faceplate rectangle at 41.6 mm against a stated H of 41.4, inside half a percent, which is the gate-1 check. So the drawing is the ruler and the shape box is not.
provenance.leds: install guide - 'Each line card has a single tristate Status LED to display card status. Each ... port on the line card has a port status LED visible on the front panel.' The state vocabulary on both is Table 32, 'Port Status and Line Card Status LEDs', of the Ethernet Line Card Installation Guide, transcribed rather than summarised: the card lamp's amber is TWO states, steady during boot and blinking for a software configuration error.
provenance.lifecycle: searched - this part number is NOT in bulletin EOL15321, which covers the rest of the 4th generation Ethernet line card family and was checked row by row. No other end-of-life notice for it is in the intake. Note the finding is 'no announcement found', not 'supported indefinitely'.
provenance.not-drawn: one thing on the real faceplate is deliberately NOT modelled: the coloured outlines that box each port group. They are real printing - the install guide spells the scheme out for the 400G combo card, 'Ports 0-5 (blue), 10-15 (red), 20-25 (magenta), 30-35 (orange)' - and the stencil draws them per group in solid and dashed strokes. They are omitted because the stencil builds them from many short stroked segments rather than closed rectangles, and guessing at a box that reads as a group boundary would put a line on the drawing that no measurement supports. Port grouping is carried structurally instead, by the port ids and by the lamp clusters that sit at each group's end.
provenance.ports: stencil - eight apertures, numbered 0 to 7 on the art, in two groups of four. No install-guide section covers this part number: the guide's 8-port 100GE sections are the CPAK card and the QSFP28/QSFPDD A9K-8HG-FLEX, neither of which is this.
provenance.power: NOT STATED. Table 35 of the Ethernet Line Card Installation Guide has no row that names this part number or its port count in this generation - its 8-port rows are the CPAK card's LAN and OTN versions at 1050 and 1100 W, which are a different card. No other document in the intake gives a wattage for it.
provenance.relief: RELIEF IS DECLARED, AND WHAT MATTERS ABOUT IT IS THAT IT IS A HANDFUL OF NUMBERS AND NOT A HANDFUL PER PART. This face carries: 9 panel lamps at dome 0.3 (one number, carried by 120 Cisco contracts); 4 ejector brackets, their levers and the grip flanges at out 4.2 (one number, carried by 61 Cisco contracts); 2 captive screw heads at cyl 1.6 (one number, carried by 63 Cisco contracts); 1 asset labels at out 0.2 (one number, carried by 22 Cisco contracts). EVERY MAGNITUDE BELOW IS ESTIMATED, AND THAT IS A DELIBERATE READING OF WHAT RELIEF IS FOR. The owner's ruling: 'the whole 3d part is kind of interpolated anyway... It's just to give it a realistic view instead of just being a flat 2d... All of the 3d stuff is going to be mostly conjecture unless the vendor provides that data.' So a proudness here is an interpolation for a realistic view, NOT a claim about the hardware, and the confidence token on every feature says so rather than leaving it to be inferred. WHY `estimated` AND NOT `borrowed`, SINCE EVERY NUMBER HERE DOES COME FROM ANOTHER PORTRAYAL PART. `borrowed` is defined as another part's MEASURED figure reused for the same class of hardware, and these origins are not measured - they are the library's first guess at that hardware, and the contracts say so themselves: agr-panel-screw's provenance reads 'estimated - it stands proud but was not measured', agr-psu-dc sources its latch's ARRANGEMENT from a photograph and never its proudness, agr-fan describes its handle and grille by appearance only, and common/led-dot's entire provenance is 'size: estimated'. Spelling that chain `borrowed` would convert a guess into an apparent measurement at one remove, a thousand times over. `source` still names the origin, so the coordinating benefit is kept and only the claim that is not true is dropped. READ THE COUNTS ABOVE AS THEY ARE MEANT: a figure carried by sixty-odd contracts is ONE ESTIMATE WRITTEN SIXTY-ODD TIMES, not sixty-odd readings that happened to agree. One caliper on any one Cisco captive screw, any one ejector lever or any one panel lamp corrects every part in the library that shares it, which is the whole reason the numbers are pooled instead of chosen per card. THE SEARCH FOR A REAL FIGURE WAS RUN FIRST AND IS RECORDED SO IT IS NOT REPEATED: all 112 doc.md extracts for 'protrud', 'extends outward', 'stands proud' and 'clearance in front' - the only vendor in the intake that publishes a projection is UfiSpace, on the S9510-28DC; the per-card dimension tables, including Table A-10 of the older Ethernet Line Card Installation Guide which the current revision dropped, all of which carry H, W, D and weight only; and the ASR 9000 Visio stencil, whose 119 masters are FRONT and REAR elevations with no side, top or isometric view, so it holds no depth axis at all and is closed as a source. Figure 48 of the Ethernet Line Card Installation Guide and Figure 1-8 of the ISM guide DO show this hardware in three dimensions and are perspective drawings with a vanishing point, so they settle the ARRANGEMENT - bracket off the plate, lever along it, domed screw head proud of both - and nothing about size. STILL REFUSED ON THIS FACE, and these are NOT the same kind of gap: pivot-top - each would need an EIGHTH family number for one or two nodes, which buys a little realism at the cost of another invented figure; left flat deliberately. The ruling sanctions interpolating a PROUDNESS for a realistic view. It does not sanction inventing an APERTURE, which is a dimension a specification is withholding rather than one nobody has measured.
provenance.size: INFERRED from the family, and the inference is weaker than the 16-port -SE's. No datasheet names this part number at all, so there is no same-drawing -TR with a stated size to borrow from - the -X-SE and -X-TR masters agree with each other to 0.00 mm but BOTH lack a datasheet. What is carried is the envelope every 4th generation 100GE card in this intake states: 41.4 x 395.7 x 604.5 mm, from the 16-port and 32-port datasheets. It is a slot envelope shared by seven documented cards and the art scales to it consistently, which is why it is used rather than left blank; it is NOT a figure Cisco has published for this part number. Weight is absent.
provenance.sources: READ THIS FIRST. This is one of three part numbers with artwork in Cisco's own Visio stencil and NO specification anywhere in the 78-document intake. It is real: the Secure Boot Product List prints 'ASR 9000 8-port 100GE QSFP TR line card' against it and the IOS XR 7.10.2, 24.2.1 and 24.3.2 firmware tables all carry it. What does not exist is a data sheet - no dimensions, no power, no LED table, and no entry on Cisco's own datasheet-listing index. Geometry here is stencil-derived; no figure is invented.

components.description: Cisco ASR 9000 version 3 AC power entry module - a power TRAY, not a supply. Three module openings labelled M0 to M2 and an ON/STANDBY switch at the right end. It holds three 6000 W AC power modules. IOS XR inventories the tray itself: it appears in `show platform` as 0/PT0 and 0/PT1 with this part number.
components.name: a9k-ac-pem-v3

provenance.bays: drawing - the module openings and their M0.. legends are measured off the master and counted off it. The count is corroborated by the guide's own arithmetic for this power system version, quoted under `generation`.
provenance.body: NO `body:` BLOCK, AND THIS IS THE RECORD OF WHY. The renderer now admits class `power` to the set that draws a solid body and ejects (relief.js, commit 9e3d0cb), so this part is ELIGIBLE for one. Both searches were run - the part number across every doc.md, and the field name ('depth', 'Physical specifications', 'Dimensions') across every doc.md, in the current Overview and Reference Guide AND in the older asr9kOVRGbk revision, since vendors delete tables between revisions. Exactly ONE Cisco fan tray or power module in the whole intake has a published depth - the ASR 9922/9912 tray, 23 inches, and it is stated in passing inside a sentence about a width change. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: a Cisco mechanical drawing, or the chassis interior measured from a photograph with a rule in frame. A body depth invented to make the part eject would be a solid-looking number in the one field a 3D viewer trusts absolutely, and `size.d` is deliberately absent for the same reason.
provenance.generation: sourced twice over. The Overview and Reference Guide's version 3 DC output table is the three-AC-module one - 'four 4400 W DC power modules or three 6000 W AC power modules per single tray' - and this master draws exactly three openings against the DC master's four. The part number is Cisco's own and appears verbatim in the Hardware Installation Guide's `show platform` output: '0/PT0 A9K-AC-PEM-V3 OPERATIONAL NSHUT'.
provenance.lifecycle: searched - no end-of-life notice is in the intake.
provenance.modules: the modules this tray takes are the 6000 W AC version 3 units, part number PWR-6KW- AC-V3 - named in the Overview and Reference Guide's FPD-upgrade caution, 'the ASR 9000 6kW AC Power Module Version 3 (PWR-6KW-AC-V3)'. provenance.nesting: the modules that seat in this tray are separate components and the schema cannot yet nest them: `bays` on a component is marked 'v0: unused' and nothing in the library uses it. So the tray draws its module openings as faceplate features and the modules are modelled alongside. When component-level bays land, this is the contract to revisit; until then a device that wants a populated tray places the tray.

components.description: Horizontal cable management bracket for an ASR 9000 rack. A full-width plate with a chevron of angled cable channels and a mounting hole at each corner. It bolts to the rack face rather than seating in a chassis opening.
components.name: a9k-cable-manager

provenance.channels: drawing - EIGHT angled channels, four leaning each way about the centre line. The master gives each one's 60.03 mm bounding square directly, and a rectangle L x W set at 45 degrees has a bounding square of (L + W) / root 2 a side, so 60.03 resolves to a 63 x 22 slot. That step matters: the first pass drew the bounding squares themselves, rounded, and the eight channels merged into one dark blob spread across the plate. Positions are measured; the slot shape is reconstructed from the bounding box rather than traced.
provenance.identity: NO PART NUMBER. The master is named 'Cable Manager' and no document in the intake gives an order code for it, so the component carries the stencil's own name.
provenance.lifecycle: searched - nothing to search for without a part number.
provenance.mounting: it BOLTS ON rather than seating in an opening, so a device places it rather than accepting it into a bay - the distinction the modelling skill draws between a bay occupant and a placement.
provenance.relief: NO RELIEF FEATURE, AND THIS IS THE ONE CISCO PART IN 128 THAT NOW PRODUCES NOTHING AT ALL IN 3D - said plainly because a single flat part in a set that is otherwise modelled looks like an oversight rather than a decision. The skin is a `plate` rect with eight `channel-N` slots as SIBLINGS of it, not children, and that is what blocks every option. `out` on the plate would strand the eight channels behind it - the skill's documented failure, a raised bare rect coming out as a blank slab with its detail missing - and `sink` on the channels needs a cavity floor this part does not have. What the bracket really is, per the `mounting` key above, is a plate BOLTED TO THE RACK FACE with open slots through it, so the honest primitive is a plate with holes and neither `out` nor `sink` is that. A DIMENSION FOR IT DOES EXIST and is deliberately not used: Figure 8 of the Overview and Reference Guide dimensions the ASR 9010 footprint's front band at 5.04 in (12.80 cm) ahead of the chassis face. That is the CABLE MANAGEMENT SPACE, not this bracket's own depth - the guide's own words are that the rails are 'set back 5.00 inches, INCLUDING front cable management space' - so taking 128 mm as the bracket would be a scope error dressed as a citation, which is worse than the blank. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: group the channels inside the plate in the skin, which is a drawing change rather than a measurement, and then one `out` carries the whole bracket.
provenance.size: drawing - the stencil master 'Cable Manager' at 1:10, 443.01 x 149.6 mm. Shape-box aspect 2.9706 against the art's 2.9613, agreeing to 0.3 percent.

components.description: Hinged fan tray door for the Cisco ASR 9006 Router. A cosmetic and EMC door across the top of the chassis front, covering both fan trays FT0 and FT1, hinged at one side and held by a single captive screw. THIS IS THE PART THAT CARRIES THE CHASSIS BRANDING: the cisco bridge, the wordmark and the "Cisco ASR 9000 Series" legend are printed on the door face, not on the chassis, which is why they belong here and are deliberately absent from the ASR 9006 device manifest. Open the door and the branding swings away with it.
components.name: a9k-fan-tray-door

provenance.branding: drawing - lifted from the ASR 9006 front master at its measured positions. The calibration is the ear-inclusive chassis face, 482.6 x 444.5 mm against an art box of 616.16 x 563.86, which gives 0.78324 mm per unit across and 0.78832 along - two independently derived scales agreeing to 0.64 percent, which is the cross-check that the art box really is the chassis face. Coordinates are then shifted by the 19.05 mm ear at the left and the 33.66 mm shroud at the top to land in the door's own frame. The bridge is nine teal (#005568) bars in the familiar 5.4 / 9.0 / 16.5 / 9.0 / 5.4 mm pattern spanning x 48.96 to 108.82, the wordmark is its five red (#c41230) glyph shapes at y 44.60 plus the two dots of the registered mark, and the legend "Cisco ASR 9000 Series" is live text in the master at 7.66 mm. components.description: Cisco ASR 9000 Series 160 Gigabyte Modular Line Card, Service Edge Optimized. A carrier, not a port card: the faceplate is two bays for Modular Port Adapters and almost nothing else - a Status lamp, an ejector and a captive screw at each end. provenance.art-box-is-not-a-size: A TRAP IN THIS STENCIL THAT COST ME A WRONG ARGUMENT, recorded because it will catch the next person. That was CIRCULAR: both had been scaled to 395.7 first, so of course their plates agreed. What is not circular is the RAW art box, and it does carry a signal - the card masters fall into exactly three: 46.55 x 413.95, 46.39 x 413.45 and 46.62 x 413.95, and the three contain cards whose data sheets say 43.7, 41.4 and 42.0 mm thick. It is very tempting to read the box as a thickness. IT IS NOT ONE. The A9K-MOD200-SE master is drawn on the 46.39 box, the one whose other occupants are all 41.4 mm 4th-generation cards - and the MPA drawn inside it measures 33.41 mm at a 43.7 anchor and 31.65 at a 41.4 anchor, so the card is 43.7. The art box identifies the TEMPLATE a master was drawn from and nothing more; Cisco reused a newer template for an older-sized card. The standard part inside the art is the authority for the scale, and the outline is not.
provenance.bays: install guide + drawing, and the two agree. The guide: 'The modular line card provides two bays that support the following Modular Port Adapters (MPAs)'. THE BAYS ARE DECLARED AT THE MPA'S ENVELOPE, not at the drawn opening, because the module's own dimension is the better of two measurements of one thing; the drawn opening is what corroborates it. Table A-10's 520.7 looks like the original- generation row value applied to a card that had not been measured separately; it is recorded here rather than discarded, because it is Cisco's and because it is what the 80 and 160 were first modelled at.
provenance.lifecycle: searched - no end-of-life notice for this part number is in the intake.
provenance.mpas: install guide - 'The modular line card provides two bays that support the following Modular Port Adapters (MPAs)', followed by the chapter's own MPA sections. provenance.power: install guide - Table 35 of the Ethernet Line Card Installation Guide, row '160 Gigabyte 4-NPU Modular Line Card (-TR or -SE)': 350 W at 25 C, 400 W at 40 C, 420 W at 55 C. max is the highest rated ambient. provenance.size: install guide - Table A-10, 'Ethernet Line Card Physical Dimensions', of the OL-17500-09 revision of the Ethernet Line Card Installation Guide, which lists THIS PART NUMBER by name: Height 14 inches / 35.56 cm, Width 1.72 inches / 4.37 cm, Depth 20.5 inches / 52.07 cm, Weight 16.34 pounds / 7.4117 kg '(without EPs)'. components.description: Cisco ASR 9000 Series 200 Gigabyte Modular Line Card, Service Edge Optimized. A carrier, not a port card: the faceplate is two bays for Modular Port Adapters and almost nothing else - a Status lamp, an ejector and a captive screw at each end. Every port this card presents belongs to the MPA seated in one of its bays.
components.name: a9k-mod200-se

provenance.art-box-is-not-a-size: A TRAP IN THIS STENCIL THAT COST ME A WRONG ARGUMENT, recorded because it will catch the next person. The first version of this provenance said these carriers share a plate 'to the hundredth of a millimetre' with the original-generation line cards. That was CIRCULAR: both had been scaled to 395.7 first, so of course their plates agreed. What is not circular is the RAW art box, and it does carry a signal - the card masters fall into exactly three: 46.55 x 413.95, 46.39 x 413.45 and 46.62 x 413.95, and the three contain cards whose data sheets say 43.7, 41.4 and 42.0 mm thick. It is very tempting to read the box as a thickness. IT IS NOT ONE. The A9K-MOD200-SE master is drawn on the 46.39 box, the one whose other occupants are all 41.4 mm 4th-generation cards - and the MPA drawn inside it measures 33.41 mm at a 43.7 anchor and 31.65 at a 41.4 anchor, so the card is 43.7. The art box identifies the TEMPLATE a master was drawn from and nothing more; Cisco reused a newer template for an older-sized card. The standard part inside the art is the authority for the scale, and the outline is not.
provenance.bays: install guide + drawing, and the two agree. The guide: 'The modular line card provides two bays that support the following Modular Port Adapters (MPAs)'. The drawing gives WHERE: the A9K-MOD400-SE master is drawn with two MPAs actually installed - a 20-port GE in the upper bay and a 2-port 100GE in the lower - and their outlines measure 33.23 x 161.21 and 33.23 x 160.94 mm at x 7.59, y 32.24 and 202.78. An MPA's own envelope is 33.81 x 160.02, so the drawn openings agree with it to 1.7 and 0.75 percent. THE BAYS ARE DECLARED AT THE MPA'S ENVELOPE, not at the drawn opening, because the module's own dimension is the better of two measurements of one thing; the drawn opening is what corroborates it. Bay 0 is the upper - the master prints '0' at y 27.45 and '1' at 366.39, one above each bay.
provenance.bays-are-inert: A NOTE ON WHAT `bays:` DOES HERE, so nobody reads more into it than is there. The component schema calls this key 'for modules that themselves host bays (v0: unused)', and it is accurate: nothing in render.py or lint.py reads a COMPONENT's bays - every bay the toolchain acts on today is a device view's. So these two entries are inert. They are declared anyway because the geometry is real, measured and sourced, and the alternative is to leave it in prose where no future renderer can reach it. When nested modules are supported the numbers are already here; until then a MOD carrier renders as a faceplate with two empty openings.
provenance.depth: THREE CISCO FIGURES FOR THIS DEPTH AND ONE IS CARRIED. Table A-10 of the OL-17500-09 line card guide gives the 80 and 160 Gigabyte carriers 20.5 in = 520.7 mm, unqualified, in a row alongside every original-generation line card at the same figure. data_sheet_c78-663866 gives the same two cards 22.40 in = 568.96 mm for the body and 24.25 in = 616.0 mm including ejector levers. datasheet-c78-735809 gives the 200 and 400 only the 616.0. 616.0 IS CARRIED, on all eight, for two reasons: it is the one figure both dedicated data sheets state, and it is the ejector-inclusive convention this library already uses for the 4th-generation cards, which carry the 604.5 their sheets give as '(includes ejector bracket/lever)'. Carrying 520.7 would have made these carriers shallower than the 4th-generation cards they sit beside in the same chassis, which they are not. Table A-10's 520.7 looks like the original- generation row value applied to a card that had not been measured separately; it is recorded here rather than discarded, because it is Cisco's and because it is what the 80 and 160 were first modelled at.
provenance.lifecycle: searched - no end-of-life notice for this part number is in the intake.
provenance.mpas: install guide - 'The modular line card provides two bays that support the following Modular Port Adapters (MPAs)', followed by the chapter's own MPA sections. NO PER- CARD LIST EXISTS FOR THIS CARRIER: the 400 Gigabyte card is the only one the guide narrows, with an explicit 'only support the following' list, and nothing equivalent is written for the 80, 160 or 200. `accepts` therefore carries the general family - every MPA in this library plus the blank - which is what the guide's general sentence supports and no more. If a per-card restriction exists in a data sheet not in this intake, this list is the thing it would narrow.
provenance.power: NOT CARRIED, and the elimination argument is set out so a reader can weigh it. Table 35 has exactly four modular line card rows and this family has exactly four capacities. Three rows name theirs - '80 Gigabyte 2-NPU', '160 Gigabyte 4-NPU', '400 Gigabyte' - and the fourth is headed 'Modular 4-NPU Line Card (-TR or -SE)', 520 W at 25 C, 590 at 40, 620 at 55. By elimination that row is the 200 Gigabyte card, and it is very likely right. It is NOT carried, because the heading is ambiguous ON ITS FACE: the 160 Gigabyte row ALSO says 4-NPU, so 'Modular 4-NPU Line Card' names a description that Table 35 has already used for a different card. An argument from what is left over is not a citation, and the same restraint is what kept a figure off cisco/a9k-16x100ge-se and cisco/asr-9922-sfc110. The L27 warning stands and is the correct signal.
provenance.relief: RELIEF IS DECLARED, AND WHAT MATTERS ABOUT IT IS THAT IT IS A HANDFUL OF NUMBERS AND NOT A HANDFUL PER PART. This face carries: 1 panel lamps at dome 0.3 (one number, carried by 120 Cisco contracts). EVERY MAGNITUDE BELOW IS ESTIMATED, AND THAT IS A DELIBERATE READING OF WHAT RELIEF IS FOR. The owner's ruling: 'the whole 3d part is kind of interpolated anyway... It's just to give it a realistic view instead of just being a flat 2d... All of the 3d stuff is going to be mostly conjecture unless the vendor provides that data.' So a proudness here is an interpolation for a realistic view, NOT a claim about the hardware, and the confidence token on every feature says so rather than leaving it to be inferred. WHY `estimated` AND NOT `borrowed`, SINCE EVERY NUMBER HERE DOES COME FROM ANOTHER PORTRAYAL PART. `borrowed` is defined as another part's MEASURED figure reused for the same class of hardware, and these origins are not measured - they are the library's first guess at that hardware, and the contracts say so themselves: agr-panel-screw's provenance reads 'estimated - it stands proud but was not measured', agr-psu-dc sources its latch's ARRANGEMENT from a photograph and never its proudness, agr-fan describes its handle and grille by appearance only, and common/led-dot's entire provenance is 'size: estimated'. Spelling that chain `borrowed` would convert a guess into an apparent measurement at one remove, a thousand times over. `source` still names the origin, so the coordinating benefit is kept and only the claim that is not true is dropped. READ THE COUNTS ABOVE AS THEY ARE MEANT: a figure carried by sixty-odd contracts is ONE ESTIMATE WRITTEN SIXTY-ODD TIMES, not sixty-odd readings that happened to agree. One caliper on any one Cisco captive screw, any one ejector lever or any one panel lamp corrects every part in the library that shares it, which is the whole reason the numbers are pooled instead of chosen per card. THE SEARCH FOR A REAL FIGURE WAS RUN FIRST AND IS RECORDED SO IT IS NOT REPEATED: all 112 doc.md extracts for 'protrud', 'extends outward', 'stands proud' and 'clearance in front' - the only vendor in the intake that publishes a projection is UfiSpace, on the S9510-28DC; the per-card dimension tables, including Table A-10 of the older Ethernet Line Card Installation Guide which the current revision dropped, all of which carry H, W, D and weight only; and the ASR 9000 Visio stencil, whose 119 masters are FRONT and REAR elevations with no side, top or isometric view, so it holds no depth axis at all and is closed as a source. Figure 48 of the Ethernet Line Card Installation Guide and Figure 1-8 of the ISM guide DO show this hardware in three dimensions and are perspective drawings with a vanishing point, so they settle the ARRANGEMENT - bracket off the plate, lever along it, domed screw head proud of both - and nothing about size.
provenance.size: drawing, WITH A STANDARD PART AS THE RULER, because Table A-10 does not reach this card: the OL-17500-09 physical-dimensions table stops at the 160 Gigabyte carrier and the 200 and 400 came later. The measurement is the MPA. An MPA's envelope is 33.81 x 160.02 mm, which is index.json's shapesheet for all seven MPA masters and is corroborated independently by the ASR 9001's bay openings. This master draws its two bays as outlines. Scale the art so the card is 43.7 x 395.7 - the original generation's stated dimensions - and those outlines measure 33.41 x 161.34 mm, both of them, which is 1.2 to 1.7 percent off the MPA. Scale it to the 4th generation's 41.4 instead and they come out 6.4 to 6.9 percent off. The card is 43.7 thick, and the depth of 520.7 is the one Table A-10 gives for its 80 and 160 Gigabyte siblings, carried across as a sibling's figure and flagged as one rather than measured. AND A SECOND DIRECT SOURCE, found later than the measurement above and kept beside it because it settles what the parenthetical means. Two Cisco data sheets carry this family in a 'Physical Dimensions' table. data_sheet_c78-663866, the ASR 9000 Modular Line Cards sheet, gives the 80 and 160 Gigabyte carriers in TWO LINES each: '14.5 W x 1.72 H x 22.40 L' and, underneath, '14.5 W x 1.72 H x 24.25 L (including ejector levers)'. datasheet-c78-735809 gives the 200 and 400 in ONE line, which is the second of those two: '14.5 W x 1.72 H x 24.25 L (including ejector levers)'. SO THE PARENTHETICAL ATTACHES TO L. The ejector levers add 1.85 in = 47.0 mm to the DEPTH and nothing to the width - which is physically right, since a card's levers protrude forward of its faceplate - and 14.5 in = 368.3 mm is the PLATE width in both sheets. The ejector-inclusive width, 395.7, is simply not stated on either; it comes from the family's own sheets, which give 368.3 and 15.58 in = 395.7 for the same cards, and from the MPA measurement above. An earlier version of this provenance said the parenthetical was misplaced. It is not; it was the two-line layout collapsing to one.
provenance.variants: install guide - 'Each type of card is available in -SE (Service Edge Optimized) and -TR (Packet Transport Optimized) variants. The two variants are functionally equivalent, but vary in configuration scale and buffer capacity.' THE STENCIL HAS ONLY THE -SE MASTERS. The -TR is modelled on the same drawing, which that sentence licenses: configuration scale and buffer capacity are internal and no faceplate can show them. Table 35 says the same thing from the other side - every modular line card power row is headed '(-TR or -SE)', so Cisco itself gives one figure for the pair.

THE DRAWING CONTRADICTS THE TEXT and the text wins: the A9K-MOD400-SE master is drawn with an A9K-MPA-20X1GE seated in its upper bay, and the 20-port GIGABIT Ethernet MPA is not on that list - only the 20-port 10-GIGABIT one is. provenance.art-box-is-not-a-size: A TRAP IN THIS STENCIL THAT COST ME A WRONG ARGUMENT, recorded because it will catch the next person. The first version of this provenance said these carriers share a plate 'to the hundredth of a millimetre' with the original-generation line cards. That was CIRCULAR: both had been scaled to 395.7 first, so of course their plates agreed. What is not circular is the RAW art box, and it does carry a signal - the card masters fall into exactly three: 46.55 x 413.95, 46.39 x 413.45 and 46.62 x 413.95, and the three contain cards whose data sheets say 43.7, 41.4 and 42.0 mm thick. It is very tempting to read the box as a thickness. IT IS NOT ONE. The A9K-MOD200-SE master is drawn on the 46.39 box, the one whose other occupants are all 41.4 mm 4th-generation cards - and the MPA drawn inside it measures 33.41 mm at a 43.7 anchor and 31.65 at a 41.4 anchor, so the card is 43.7. The art box identifies the TEMPLATE a master was drawn from and nothing more; Cisco reused a newer template for an older-sized card. The standard part inside the art is the authority for the scale, and the outline is not.
provenance.bays: install guide + drawing, and the two agree. The guide: 'The modular line card provides two bays that support the following Modular Port Adapters (MPAs)'. An MPA's own envelope is 33.81 x 160.02, so the drawn openings agree with it to 1.7 and 0.75 percent. THE BAYS ARE DECLARED AT THE MPA'S ENVELOPE, not at the drawn opening, because the module's own dimension is the better of two measurements of one thing; the drawn opening is what corroborates it. provenance.bays-are-inert: A NOTE ON WHAT `bays:` DOES HERE, so nobody reads more into it than is there. The component schema calls this key 'for modules that themselves host bays (v0: unused)', and it is accurate: nothing in render.py or lint.py reads a COMPONENT's bays - every bay the toolchain acts on today is a device view's. So these two entries are inert. They are declared anyway because the geometry is real, measured and sourced, and the alternative is to leave it in prose where no future renderer can reach it. provenance.depth: THREE CISCO FIGURES FOR THIS DEPTH AND ONE IS CARRIED. provenance.mpas: install guide - 'The modular line card provides two bays that support the following Modular Port Adapters (MPAs)', followed by the chapter's own MPA sections. provenance.power: install guide - Table 35 of the Ethernet Line Card Installation Guide, row '80 Gigabyte 2-NPU Modular Line Card (-TR or -SE)': 350 W at 25 C, 400 W at 40 C, 420 W at 55 C. max is the highest rated ambient. provenance.relief: RELIEF IS DECLARED, AND WHAT MATTERS ABOUT IT IS THAT IT IS A HANDFUL OF NUMBERS AND NOT A HANDFUL PER PART. components.description: Cisco 1-Port 40 Gigabit Ethernet Modular Port Adapter with QSFP+. A single QSFP+ cage with an A/L lamp beside it, a STATUS lamp and a captive screw at each end - the emptiest faceplate in the MPA family. provenance.cages: std/qsfp28 is the QSFP+ aperture here and the name is worth explaining. The registry key's own citation is SFF-8663 Rev 1.7 Figure 5-4, which is the QSFP BEZEL OPENING - one opening for QSFP, QSFP+ and QSFP28 alike, because they are one mechanical family and differ in signalling, not in sheet metal. Cisco says the same thing on its own faceplates: the 16-port card in this library is labelled 'QSFP28/QSFP+' on a single cage. The drawing corroborates it - this master's cage measures 19.84 x 9.78 mm against the registry's 20.0 x 10.15, inside half a millimetre on both axes - so the aperture is not assumed from the port's name, it is measured and then found to match. The port's SPEED is 40 Gbps and lives in attrs; conforms describes the hole.
provenance.compatibility: install guide - a compatibility fact stated as a Note beside this MPA's figure and worth carrying because nothing else in the model would show it: 'This MPA is not compatible with the MOD400 consumption-model line card.' Cisco adds that 'The consumption-model MPAs can only be used only with consumption-model line cards', so the A9K-MOD400-CM carrier takes the -CM MPAs and not this one.
provenance.envelope-was-wrong: drawing - and READ THE ORIENTATION FIRST, because this master is drawn on its side. index.json gives its shapesheet as 160.02 x 33.81 mm where the 4-port and 20-port MPA masters give 33.81 x 160.02: the same envelope, drawn landscape. Every coordinate below is therefore the master's transposed - the master's y becomes this component's x and its x becomes the y - so that all seven MPAs in this library share one frame and a chassis can rotate a bay once for all of them. The transposition is a relabelling of axes and not a scale, so it cannot introduce the mixed-source error that a stretch would.
provenance.frame: modelled PORTRAIT - x across the module's 33.8 mm thickness, y along its 160.0 mm length - which is how most of these masters are drawn and how every other card in this library is modelled. The ASR 9001 lays its two MPAs FLAT, so its bays rotate the component rather than the component carrying two orientations. Note the stencil is not consistent about this: A9K-MPA-1X40GE, -2X40GE and -8x10GE are drawn landscape and the rest portrait, for one physical form factor - which the intake notes flag as a reason to read the artwork rather than assume an orientation from index.json's axis order.
provenance.leds: install guide - Table 33, 'Modular Port Adapter LEDs', of the Ethernet Line Card Installation Guide gives the family vocabulary: 'The modular port adapters have two types of LEDs: an A/L LED for each individual port and a STATUS LED for the modular port adapter.' EACH MPA ALSO HAS ITS OWN TABLE and where the two differ the card's own table wins - Table 33 says the A/L is RED when the link is down, while this card's table says AMBER, and it is this card's table that is transcribed below. That divergence is the reason to cite the specific table rather than the general one.

The 2-port 10GE is a different adapter with a different aperture - XFP, not QSFP+ - and it has its own master in this stencil. This is a copy-and-edit that was not finished, the same class of error as the A9903-8HG-PEC master printing the 20HG's PID. Only A9K-MPA-1X40GE is carried onto the drawing; the stray legend is recorded here and not reproduced.

THE CHECK THAT SETTLES IT is the 4-port MPA, which is drawn portrait and needs no conversion at all: its cages sit at across-card x 15.29 and its port numerals at 26.89. Transpose it instead and they land at 8.68 and 6.90, on the other side of the plate. Two masters drawn in different orientations agreeing to a twentieth of a millimetre is not something the wrong conversion produces.

components.description: Cisco 20-Port Gigabit Ethernet Modular Port Adapter. Twenty SFP cages in two columns of ten - even-numbered ports in one column, odd in the other - with a STATUS lamp and a captive screw at each end. provenance.cages: composed from std/sfp-ganged, whose SFF-8433 aperture is 14.25 x 10.40 against the 14.4 x 9.24 drawn. The ganged part rather than std/sfp because these ports share walls in two continuous columns - std/sfp is 14.5 wide and explicitly cannot gang.

provenance.inset: READ THIS BEFORE RESCALING ANYTHING ON THIS MASTER. Its art measures 29.07 mm across where the shapesheet says 33.66, a 16 percent difference - far larger than the sub- millimetre gaps elsewhere in this stencil. The art is modelled as NOT stretched to fill the envelope: the plate is drawn INSET and centred, and the cages keep the art's own scale. THE QUESTION IS OPEN, and the reason is measurable rather than a shrug. THE FIRST ARGUMENT WAS WRONG: it said 'stretching x by 1.158 would have made the cage 16.7 mm wide, which no SFP cage is', but 16.7 is 14.4 x 1.158 and 14.4 is the cage's ALONG-CARD dimension, which a stretch of the across axis does not touch. Done correctly the two readings are 9.24 mm across (inset, 7.6 percent under SFF-8433's 10.00 opening) and 10.98 (stretched to Cisco's stated 34.54 envelope, 9.8 percent over). THEN THE RULER WAS MEASURED AGAINST ITS OWN STANDARD, which is what settles whether it can be trusted here at all. Across the eight cards in this library whose cages can be compared to a registry entry, the stencil draws the ALONG-CARD dimension to a mean error of 3.2 percent, worst 7.2, and every one of them slightly under. It draws the ACROSS-CARD dimension to a mean error of 14.7 percent, worst 20.4, and the sign scatters both ways - the same SFP opening appears at 8.96, 9.24, 10.72 and 12.04 mm on four different masters. So this stencil's cages are a good ruler along the card and a bad one across it, by a factor of four and a half. A LIMITATION OF THAT STUDY, because it bounds what the figure may be used for: all eight samples are apertures of essentially ONE SIZE, nominal 10.00 to 10.15 mm. The absolute errors spread 0.72 to 2.06 mm and the percentage errors 7.2 to 20.4 - the same 2.9-fold scatter expressed two ways - so with no size leverage in the sample it cannot be told whether the error scales with the feature or is a fixed drawing tolerance. Quote it as '14.7 percent mean, measured on ~10 mm apertures' and do not carry it onto a large opening in either form: not as 14.7 percent, which may be too harsh, and not as the 3.9 percent a fixed 1.5 mm would give on a 37 mm hole, which is unsupported. It bounds this card's question because this card's cages ARE ~10 mm. The inset-versus-stretched question is entirely an across-card question, the candidates are 16 percent apart, and the ruler's own accuracy on that axis is 15 to 20 percent. IT CANNOT RESOLVE IT. What is NOT in doubt: the envelope, which Cisco states at 34.54 x 161.80, and the along-card positions, which the A9K-MOD400 bay measurement corroborates to 0.4 percent. What is in doubt is where twenty cages sit across a 34.54 mm face, by at most 2.7 mm. A photograph, or any drawing of this MPA that is not this master, would settle it. FOR THE METROLOGY RULE: the counter-case clause this card was originally used to justify is unaffected - it was independently confirmed on the A9K-MOD200, where the ruler gave 1.2 percent against 6.4 and settled the question outright - but it needs the rider that a ruler discriminates only when the drawing is more accurate than the difference being resolved, AND that accuracy can differ per AXIS on the same ruler, as it does here by four and a half times.

components.description: Cisco 2-Port 100 Gigabit Ethernet Modular Port Adapter with CFP2. Two CFP2 cages on the MPA envelope, each with a triangular A/L indicator and a numeral beside it, plus a STATUS lamp - all of them drawn as outlined glyphs rather than as text, which is why a text scan of this master finds only the PID. Seats in an A9K-MOD carrier; it is on the 400 Gigabyte carrier's explicit supported list, which names it as the '2-Port 100-Gigabit Ethernet Modular Port Adapter with CFP2-DCO and CPAK'.
components.name: a9k-mpa-2x100ge

provenance.aperture: DRAWN, NOT COMPOSED, AND DECLARED `class: cutout` ANYWAY - which takes an L26 warning, and the warning is the point. THE CFP2 SPECIFICATION EXCLUDES THE NUMBER EXPLICITLY. Revision 1.0 was fetched and read: section 5.3 states 'All mechanical hardware dimensions in this document are for reference only. Normative dimensions are found in the latest published CFP2 baseline drawing', and section 5.4, Host System Dimensions, is one sentence pointing at the same members-only document. The cages here are transcribed from the master at 15.23 x 37.13 mm and conform to nothing, because there is nothing to conform to. The earlier instinct on cards like this was to withhold `class: cutout` so the aperture census stayed clean; that is backwards. L26's own message ends 'if the dimension cannot be sourced yet, this warning is the record of that'. A census kept tidy by not declaring a cutout has been routed around, not satisfied. WHAT WOULD CLOSE THIS, stated so a contributor is not sent on an errand that cannot be run: CFP MSA membership and the baseline drawing it gives access to, or a Cisco mechanical drawing of this faceplate. NOT 'look harder' - this is not a search that failed, it is a specification that withholds the figure. Contrast the XFP on the 4-port and 2-port 10GE MPAs in this library, where INF-8077i gives the bezel opening outright in two figures and the only thing missing had been anyone looking outside the vendor's own guide. AND TWO CISCO MASTERS DRAW THIS SAME APERTURE DIFFERENTLY, which is worth knowing before anyone is tempted to register a key from either. This master draws its CFP2 opening at 15.23 x 37.13 mm; the A9K-400G-DWDM-TR master draws its CFP2 openings at 13.61 x 42.63. Same form factor, same vendor, same stencil, 12 percent apart across and 13 percent along. Neither can be the standard's opening and at most one is this card's, so the drawing is a poor witness here even setting aside that there is no registry entry to compare it against.
provenance.lamps: drawing - an A/L triangle per port and one STATUS lamp for the adapter, which is the same complement every other MPA in this library carries. NO PER-CARD LED TABLE EXISTS for this MPA - the guide has one for six of the others and none for this - so the vocabularies are the family's and are BORROWINGS, flagged as such.

The owner's ruling: 'the whole 3d part is kind of interpolated anyway... It's just to give it a realistic view instead of just being a flat 2d... All of the 3d stuff is going to be mostly conjecture unless the vendor provides that data.' So a proudness here is an interpolation for a realistic view, NOT a claim about the hardware, and the confidence token on every feature says so rather than leaving it to be inferred. WHY `estimated` AND NOT `borrowed`, SINCE EVERY NUMBER HERE DOES COME FROM ANOTHER PORTRAYAL PART. `borrowed` is defined as another part's MEASURED figure reused for the same class of hardware, and these origins are not measured - they are the library's first guess at that hardware, and the contracts say so themselves: agr-panel-screw's provenance reads 'estimated - it stands proud but was not measured', agr-psu-dc sources its latch's ARRANGEMENT from a photograph and never its proudness, agr-fan describes its handle and grille by appearance only, and common/led-dot's entire provenance is 'size: estimated'. Spelling that chain `borrowed` would convert a guess into an apparent measurement at one remove, a thousand times over. `source` still names the origin, so the coordinating benefit is kept and only the claim that is not true is dropped. READ THE COUNTS ABOVE AS THEY ARE MEANT: a figure carried by sixty-odd contracts is ONE ESTIMATE WRITTEN SIXTY-ODD TIMES, not sixty-odd readings that happened to agree. One caliper on any one Cisco captive screw, any one ejector lever or any one panel lamp corrects every part in the library that shares it, which is the whole reason the numbers are pooled instead of chosen per card. THE SEARCH FOR A REAL FIGURE WAS RUN FIRST AND IS RECORDED SO IT IS NOT REPEATED: all 112 doc.md extracts for 'protrud', 'extends outward', 'stands proud' and 'clearance in front' - the only vendor in the intake that publishes a projection is UfiSpace, on the S9510-28DC; the per-card dimension tables, including Table A-10 of the older Ethernet Line Card Installation Guide which the current revision dropped, all of which carry H, W, D and weight only; and the ASR 9000 Visio stencil, whose 119 masters are FRONT and REAR elevations with no side, top or isometric view, so it holds no depth axis at all and is closed as a source. Figure 48 of the Ethernet Line Card Installation Guide and Figure 1-8 of the ISM guide DO show this hardware in three dimensions and are perspective drawings with a vanishing point, so they settle the ARRANGEMENT - bracket off the plate, lever along it, domed screw head proud of both - and nothing about size. STILL REFUSED ON THIS FACE, and these are NOT the same kind of gap: the 2 drawn aperture(s) cfp2-0, cfp2-1 - an optical or connector aperture that conforms to no published standard, so no depth exists to interpolate from. The ruling sanctions interpolating a PROUDNESS for a realistic view. It does not sanction inventing an APERTURE, which is a dimension a specification is withholding rather than one nobody has measured.
provenance.screws: drawing - three captive screws, all stroked circles found by scanning fill:none paths: 8.11 mm at (4.21, 76.90), 5.38 at (27.45, 78.25) and 5.38 at (2.18, 88.11). Two sizes and an asymmetric arrangement, which is what the master draws. ONE ARTEFACT REPRODUCED RATHER THAN CORRECTED: the smallest screw's circle extends about 0.5 mm past the plate's own edge in the master. That is the drawing's, not a modelling error, and nudging it inward would have made the component disagree with the artwork it is transcribed from without making it agree with the hardware.
provenance.size: datasheet - Cisco ASR 9000 Series data sheet c78-735809, Table 3, 'Physical dimensions', row 'A9K-MPA-2X100GE': 6.37 W x 1.36 H x 6.70 L, and a second line 6.37 W x 1.36 H x 8.30 L (including jackscrew); weight 38.4 oz (1.09 kg). Every MPA in that table carries the same envelope and a different weight.

provenance.compatibility: install guide - a compatibility fact stated as a Note beside this MPA's figure and worth carrying because nothing else in the model would show it: 'This MPA is not compatible with consumption-model MOD400 consumption-model line card.' Every coordinate below is therefore the master's transposed - the master's y becomes this component's x and its x becomes the y - so that all seven MPAs in this library share one frame and a chassis can rotate a bay once for all of them. provenance.leds: install guide - Table 33, 'Modular Port Adapter LEDs', of the Ethernet Line Card Installation Guide gives the family vocabulary: 'The modular port adapters have two types of LEDs: an A/L LED for each individual port and a STATUS LED for the modular port adapter.' EACH MPA ALSO HAS ITS OWN TABLE and where the two differ the card's own table wins - Table 33 says the A/L is RED when the link is down, while this card's table says AMBER, and it is this card's table that is transcribed below. provenance.lifecycle: searched - no end-of-life notice for this part number is in the intake.

Two masters drawn in different orientations agreeing to a twentieth of a millimetre is not something the wrong conversion produces.

Eight SFP+ cages in two blocks of four down the faceplate, each with its own A/L lamp, plus a STATUS lamp and a captive screw at each end. The densest of the single-row MPAs. One of the adapters the ASR 9001 takes; it also seats in the A9K-MOD carrier line cards.
components.name: a9k-mpa-8x10ge

provenance.cages: std/sfp is the SFP+ aperture. SFP, SFP+ and SFP28 share one bezel opening and differ in signalling; the drawn cage measures 14.12 x 8.96 mm against the registry's 14.5 x 10.0, the same slight under-height the 20-port GE MPA's cages show in this stencil, and well inside what would distinguish it from any other aperture on this faceplate.
provenance.compatibility: install guide - a Note beside this MPA's figure: 'This MPA is not compatible with MOD400 consumption-model line card.' Cisco adds that 'The consumption-model MPAs can only be used only with consumption-model line cards', so the A9K-MOD400-CM carrier takes the -CM MPAs and not this one.
provenance.envelope-was-wrong: drawing - and READ THE ORIENTATION FIRST, because this master is drawn on its side. index.json gives its shapesheet as 160.02 x 33.81 mm where the 4-port and 20-port MPA masters give 33.81 x 160.02: the same envelope, drawn landscape. Every coordinate below is therefore the master's transposed - the master's y becomes this component's x and its x becomes the y - so that all seven MPAs in this library share one frame and a chassis can rotate a bay once for all of them. The transposition is a relabelling of axes and not a scale, so it cannot introduce the mixed-source error that a stretch would.
provenance.frame: modelled PORTRAIT - x across the module's 33.8 mm thickness, y along its 160.0 mm length - which is how most of these masters are drawn and how every other card in this library is modelled. The ASR 9001 lays its two MPAs FLAT, so its bays rotate the component rather than the component carrying two orientations. Note the stencil is not consistent about this: A9K-MPA-1X40GE, -2X40GE and -8x10GE are drawn landscape and the rest portrait, for one physical form factor - which the intake notes flag as a reason to read the artwork rather than assume an orientation from index.json's axis order.
provenance.leds: install guide - Table 33, 'Modular Port Adapter LEDs', of the Ethernet Line Card Installation Guide gives the family vocabulary: 'The modular port adapters have two types of LEDs: an A/L LED for each individual port and a STATUS LED for the modular port adapter.' EACH MPA ALSO HAS ITS OWN TABLE and where the two differ the card's own table wins - Table 33 says the A/L is RED when the link is down, while this card's table says AMBER, and it is this card's table that is transcribed below. That divergence is the reason to cite the specific table rather than the general one.
provenance.lifecycle: searched - no end-of-life notice for this part number is in the intake.
provenance.orientation: THE CONVERSION IS A ROTATION AND NOT A TRANSPOSE, and the difference is a mirrored faceplate. Swapping the axes - master y to component x, master x to component y - is a reflection, and it puts every A/L lamp on the wrong side of its cage. The rotation is fixed by one requirement: port 0 must sit at the TOP, which is where the portrait-drawn 4-port and 20-port masters put theirs and what lets a chassis rotate one bay for all seven MPAs. THE CHECK THAT SETTLES IT is the 4-port MPA, which is drawn portrait and needs no conversion at all: its cages sit at across-card x 15.29 and its port numerals at 26.89. Rotate the 1-port 40GE master and its cage lands at 15.35 and its numeral at 26.91 - both inside 0.06 mm of a card that was never converted. Transpose it instead and they land at 8.68 and 6.90, on the other side of the plate. Two masters drawn in different orientations agreeing to a twentieth of a millimetre is not something the wrong conversion produces.
provenance.ports: install guide + drawing. The guide gives the count and the media - '8-port 10GE Modular Port Adapter (MPA) with SFP+' - and notes that 'Each SFP+ cage on the 8-Port 10GE MPA has an adjacent A/L (Active/Link) LED of the card'. THE MASTER NUMBERS EVERY PORT ITSELF and the numerals are text, not outlined glyphs, so they are read rather than inferred: '0' through '7' at transposed y 24.8, 39.1, 53.1, 67.4, 92.6, 106.6, 120.9 and 134.9, each landing on the cage beside it. Note the gap in the middle - the cages run 17.71, 31.82, 45.94, 60.06 and then jump to 85.33 - so the card is two blocks of four and not eight evenly spaced, and the numbering runs straight through the gap.
provenance.power: NOT STATED. Table 35 of the Ethernet Line Card Installation Guide gives per-card power for the modular-chassis line cards including the A9K-MOD carriers, but nothing for the MPAs that go inside them, and the ASR 9001 data sheet gives a chassis figure only (425 W typical, 525 W maximum). An MPA's draw is inside its carrier's.
provenance.relief: RELIEF IS DECLARED, AND WHAT MATTERS ABOUT IT IS THAT IT IS A HANDFUL OF NUMBERS AND NOT A HANDFUL PER PART. This face carries: 9 panel lamps at dome 0.3 (one number, carried by 120 Cisco contracts). EVERY MAGNITUDE BELOW IS ESTIMATED, AND THAT IS A DELIBERATE READING OF WHAT RELIEF IS FOR. The owner's ruling: 'the whole 3d part is kind of interpolated anyway... It's just to give it a realistic view instead of just being a flat 2d... All of the 3d stuff is going to be mostly conjecture unless the vendor provides that data.' So a proudness here is an interpolation for a realistic view, NOT a claim about the hardware, and the confidence token on every feature says so rather than leaving it to be inferred. WHY `estimated` AND NOT `borrowed`, SINCE EVERY NUMBER HERE DOES COME FROM ANOTHER PORTRAYAL PART. `borrowed` is defined as another part's MEASURED figure reused for the same class of hardware, and these origins are not measured - they are the library's first guess at that hardware, and the contracts say so themselves: agr-panel-screw's provenance reads 'estimated - it stands proud but was not measured', agr-psu-dc sources its latch's ARRANGEMENT from a photograph and never its proudness, agr-fan describes its handle and grille by appearance only, and common/led-dot's entire provenance is 'size: estimated'. Spelling that chain `borrowed` would convert a guess into an apparent measurement at one remove, a thousand times over. `source` still names the origin, so the coordinating benefit is kept and only the claim that is not true is dropped. READ THE COUNTS ABOVE AS THEY ARE MEANT: a figure carried by sixty-odd contracts is ONE ESTIMATE WRITTEN SIXTY-ODD TIMES, not sixty-odd readings that happened to agree. One caliper on any one Cisco captive screw, any one ejector lever or any one panel lamp corrects every part in the library that shares it, which is the whole reason the numbers are pooled instead of chosen per card. THE SEARCH FOR A REAL FIGURE WAS RUN FIRST AND IS RECORDED SO IT IS NOT REPEATED: all 112 doc.md extracts for 'protrud', 'extends outward', 'stands proud' and 'clearance in front' - the only vendor in the intake that publishes a projection is UfiSpace, on the S9510-28DC; the per-card dimension tables, including Table A-10 of the older Ethernet Line Card Installation Guide which the current revision dropped, all of which carry H, W, D and weight only; and the ASR 9000 Visio stencil, whose 119 masters are FRONT and REAR elevations with no side, top or isometric view, so it holds no depth axis at all and is closed as a source. Figure 48 of the Ethernet Line Card Installation Guide and Figure 1-8 of the ISM guide DO show this hardware in three dimensions and are perspective drawings with a vanishing point, so they settle the ARRANGEMENT - bracket off the plate, lever along it, domed screw head proud of both - and nothing about size.
provenance.size: datasheet - Cisco ASR 9000 Series data sheet c78-735809, Table 3, 'Physical dimensions', which lists EVERY MPA by part number: 'A9K-MPA-8X10GE: 6.37 W x 1.36 H x 6.70 L; 28 oz (0.79 kg). 6.37 W x 1.36 H x 8.30 L (including jackscrew)'. In millimetres that is 161.80 long by 34.54 thick by 170.18 deep, or 210.82 deep with the jackscrew, which protrudes and is not part of the body. AN EARLIER VERSION OF THIS COMPONENT SAID 'NO document in the intake gives an MPA's dimensions' and took index.json's shapesheet, 33.81 x 160.02. That claim was false and the shapesheet was a good proxy: 1.1 percent short on the length and 2.1 on the thickness. The stated figures are now carried and every measured coordinate on this faceplate is scaled to them, which is exactly equivalent to having read the master at this anchor in the first place. THE CORROBORATION IS WORTH KEEPING: the A9K-MOD400-SE master draws its two MPA bays as outlines, and at that carrier's own 43.7 x 395.7 anchor they measure 161.21 and 160.94 mm long - 0.4 percent from Cisco's stated 161.80. Two Cisco documents, a drawing and a table, agreeing through a third part.

components.description: Cisco ASR 9000 version 1 power module for a modular-chassis power tray. Three axial fans behind finger guards across the face, an ejector door with a latch on the right, and Input, Output and Fault lamps. Three of these fill a version 1 tray.
components.name: a9k-power-module

provenance.generation: the version is read off the WIDTH, not off the name. This master is 139.12 mm wide and the version 2 tray's four module positions are on a 107.3 mm pitch; the 'A9K Power Module V2' master is 99.62 mm and fits one, while this one cannot. The Overview and Reference Guide's own arithmetic agrees: the version 1 tray holds THREE modules ('three 2100 W power modules in a single tray, 6300 W') and the version 2 tray holds four ('four 2100 W DC power modules or 3000 W AC power modules in a single tray'). A 139.12 mm module fits three across a 429 mm tray and not four.
provenance.lamps: install guide - the Overview and Reference Guide's 'Power Module Status Indicators', which gives one table for the version 1 module and a second for version 2 and says 'The status indicators for the version 3 power module are similar'. Both tables read the same and are transcribed here: Input LED - 'ON continuously when the input voltage is present and within the correct range. BLINKING when the input voltage is out of acceptable range. OFF when no input voltage is present.' Output LED - 'ON when the power module output voltage is present. BLINKING when the power module is in a power limit or overcurrent condition.' Fault LED - 'ON indicates that a power supply failure has occurred.' Note what Cisco does NOT give: a colour for any of the three. So the states are on/blinking/off and no colour is asserted.
provenance.lifecycle: searched - no end-of-life notice for this part is in the intake.
provenance.power: NOT STATED FOR THIS DRAWING, and the reason is worth the paragraph because the numbers themselves are not missing - the attribution is. components.description: Cisco ASR 9000 Series Route Switch Processor with 4 GB of DRAM, the ORIGINAL generation - the card the ASR 9006 and ASR 9010 shipped with before the RSP-440. Two SYNC timing ports, two management LAN ports, a console and an auxiliary port, a nine- pin alarm output, ACO and LAMPTEST push buttons, an eight-lamp cluster and the two removable-media carrier panels the later control cards do not have. It was found by grepping all 78 documents for the string 'Power consumption' - an audit prompted by three earlier claims of vendor silence that turned out false - and not by searching for this part number. provenance.ruler-was-tried: THE STANDARD-PART RULER WAS TRIED HERE AND IT IS TOO BLUNT, kept because the method works elsewhere and this is the clearest record of its limit. This faceplate is full of RJ-45 jacks and std/rj45's opening is 16.0 x 14.0 mm from IEC 60603-7. Scale this master to 42.0 x 406.0 and its six jacks measure 12.8 x 16.67; scale it to 43.7 and they measure 13.32 x 16.67. Against a rotated 14.0 x 16.0 that is 8.6 percent under and 4.9 under - so THE RULER PREFERS 43.7, and the data sheet says 41.9. The ruler was not merely inconclusive, it pointed at the answer furthest from the truth. The reason is that the stencil draws these jacks about eight percent narrow, which is twice the spread between the candidate sizes: a ruler only discriminates when the drawing is more accurate than the difference being resolved. Contrast the A9K-MOD200, where the MPA gave 1.2 percent against 6.4 and settled it outright.
provenance.size: datasheet - data_sheet_c78-500699, the Cisco ASR 9000 Series Route Switch Processor data sheet, 'Physical specifications': 'Occupies one slot; dual redundant RSPs in 2 slots in Cisco ASR 9010 and ASR 9006 chassis. Height: 1.65 in. (4.19 cm). Width: 16 in. (40.64 cm). Depth: 26.53 in (67.38 cm). Weight: 18 lb (8.16 kgs).' Cisco's own centimetre column gives 41.9 x 406.4 x 673.8 mm and those are the numbers carried; the inch column rounds. Note the axis convention - Height is the THICKNESS here, which is the newer sheets' convention and not the original line cards'.
provenance.variants: datasheet - data_sheet_c78-500699, the Cisco ASR 9000 Series Route Switch Processor data sheet treats the two as ONE product entry: 'A9K-RSP-4G and A9K-RSP-8G: Route switch processor, bidirectional nonblocking fabric, controller, 40-GB hard drive', with a single physical specification block, a single power block, and the difference stated once - '4-GB Error-Correcting Code (ECC)-protected DRAM for A9K-RSP-4G; 8-GB ... for A9K-RSP-8G'. So one drawing serves both and the only thing that differs between these two components is the DRAM figure and the printed PID. The stencil has one master and it prints A9K-RSP-4G; the 8G's faceplate legend is substituted, which is the one thing here NOT taken from a drawing. Cisco adds an operational constraint worth carrying: 'RSP redundancy (both RSPs must be the same version, either A9K-RSP-4G or A9K-RSP-8G)' - a chassis may not mix them.

Scale this master to 42.0 x 406.0 and its six jacks measure 12.8 x 16.67; scale it to 43.7 and they measure 13.32 x 16.67. provenance.alarm-out: install guide - 'Each RSP/RP card drives a set of three alarm output contacts. provenance.cages: composed from std/, never drawn. The ruling sanctions interpolating a PROUDNESS for a realistic view. It does not sanction inventing an APERTURE, which is a dimension a specification is withholding rather than one nobody has measured.

attrs.timing: 2 x SYNC (BITS/J.211/DTI) RJ-45, IEEE 1588 RJ-45, 2 x inter-chassis sync RJ-45, 10 MHz and 1 PPS SMB

components.description: Cisco ASR 9000 Route Switch Processor 880, Service Edge optimised, with eight cores at 1.9 GHz and four 10-GE SFP+ ports for external server connectivity. Ten RJ-45 jacks - two SYNC timing ports configurable as BITS, J.211 or DTI, an IEEE 1588 timestamp port, two inter-chassis sync ports of which ICS1 doubles as the RS232/422 GPS time-of-day input, two management LAN ports, a CMP port, a console and an auxiliary port - plus 10 MHz and 1 PPS SMB clock inputs, a nine-pin alarm output, a USB 2.0 type A port, nine discrete status lamps, a four-character LED dot-matrix display and a LAMP TEST push button.
components.name: a9k-rsp880-se

provenance.alarm-out: install guide - 'Each RSP/RP card drives a set of three alarm output contacts. Alarm circuitry on the RSP/RP activates dry contact closures that are accessible through the nine-pin Alarm Out connector on the RSP/RP front panel... Both normally-open and normally-closed contacts are available. Only the active RSP/RP drives the alarm outputs.'
provenance.buttons: install guide - 'Alarm Cut Off (ACO) and Lamp Test momentary push buttons', and on the RSP5 the guide adds that they 'can be used to eject the RSP5 card'. Both are drawn on the master as stroked circles with their legends beside them. Worth recording how nearly they were missed: the first extraction pass reported one button, because a circle is a curve and the outline reader skips curves - the second was found by looking at the artwork at 8 px/mm rather than by trusting the count.
provenance.cages: composed from std/, never drawn. The RJ-45s go in as std/rj45-ganged (12.7 x 11.0) rather than std/rj45 (16.0 x 14.0): the IEC 60603-7 single-port cutout is the wrong part for a stacked pair whose ports share walls, and 16.0 will not fit twice across a 41 mm card. The drawn jack measures 10.83 x 12.81, which rotated is 12.81 x 10.83 against the ganged registry's 12.7 x 11.0 - agreement to one percent, which is the check. Timing coax is std/smb, sourced from the same 10-32 UNF figure the registry carries; the USB is std/usb-a.
provenance.db9: the ALARM OUT connector is DRAWN, not composed, and it IS declared `class: cutout` - which is a reversal of what these components said until now and the reversal is the point. There is no std/ part for a D-subminiature DE-9, no `db9` key in spec/schemas/standards.yaml, and no document in this intake dimensions the panel opening; the geometry here is transcribed from the master. The earlier version withheld `class: cutout` on the reasoning that a cutout conforming to nothing would corrupt the aperture census L26 keeps. THAT WAS BACKWARDS. L26's own message ends 'if the dimension cannot be sourced yet, this warning is the record of that', and its docstring calls the rule a to-do list for std/ rather than an accusation. Withholding the declaration did not keep the census clean, it kept a real gap OUT of the one rule built to hold it - a count kept tidy by routing around the detector. So the cutout is declared, the L26 warning stands, and the register is one entry more honest. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: a `db9` key in standards.yaml carrying the D-sub panel cutout from MIL-DTL-24308 or its commercial equivalent, plus a std/db9 part. That is a real errand somebody can run, unlike the CFP family's, and nobody has run it. CONTRAST cisco/a9k-750w-dc, whose DC terminal block is correctly NOT a cutout: that is hardware bolted to the face rather than a hole punched in it, and the distinction is between a thing that needs an opening and a thing that does not.
provenance.jack-orientation: the ICS and MGT LAN jacks are STACKED PAIRS in one bezel, not two singles side by side, and the pair MIRRORS: read at high zoom the upper jack's keyway points up and the lower one's points down, so both release tabs stay reachable. The upper of each pair is therefore placed at rotate 270 and everything else at 90. This is the failure that was caught by eye on the AGR400's RJ-45s and would have linted clean here too. Which jack is 0: the artwork prints '0' beside the upper of each pair and '1' beside the lower, and ICS0 sits above ICS1/TOD under the GPS bracket.
provenance.lamps: install guide - Table 4, 'RSP, RSP-440, RSP-440 Lite, RSP-880, RSP880-LT, RSP4-S, RSP5 Discrete LED Display Definitions', and Table 5 for the RP, transcribed per lamp with Cisco's own sentence kept beside the state tokens. WHICH lamp is where was read off the artwork at high zoom, not guessed: three columns of three, SSD/CRIT/FAIL, FC FAULT/MAJ/ACO and GPS/MIN/SYNC, and the same nine names appear on the rsp5, rsp880, rsp880-lt, rp3 and a99-rsp masters. FC FAULT is in none of Cisco's tables - see its own description.
provenance.lifecycle: searched - no end-of-life notice for this part number is in the intake.
provenance.one-drawing: READ THIS BEFORE TRUSTING A FEATURE POSITION TO THE MILLIMETRE. Nine RSP and RP masters in this stencil are ONE DRAWING: extracted jack, SMB, USB, DB9, LED-matrix and lamp coordinates agree to 0.00 mm across a9k-rsp5-se and -tr, a9k-rsp880-se and -tr, a9k-rsp880-lt-se and -tr, a99-rp3-se and -tr, and a99-rsp-se. The DATASHEETS do not agree: these cards are 402.8, 428.5, 428.2 and 403.4 mm wide and 41.0 to 46.0 mm high. So the drawing is generic across the family and cannot be all four sizes. Each card here is scaled to its OWN stated envelope - long axis to its width, short axis to its height, two factors, exactly as the line cards were - which makes the OUTLINE right for every one and makes the interior positions proportional rather than measured. A jack centre is therefore good to a few millimetres, not to a tenth, and anyone needing better needs a mechanical drawing Cisco has not published.
provenance.ports: install guide - the Overview and Reference Guide's per-card 'Front Panel and Access Ports' section, corroborated feature by feature by the artwork. For the RSP5: 'Two RJ-45 Sync timing ports with Link and Fault LEDs built into the RJ-45. IEEE1588 RJ-45 Timestamp port. Two Inter-Chassis Sync ports - nVSync1 is shared with RS232/422 GPS TOD RJ-45 port. RS232/422 GPS TOD RJ-45 port for system timing input. 10 MHz and 1 PPS clock input SMB ports. Alarm Output DB9 port with three alarm outputs. External USB2, class-A port. Two dual-speed 100/1000 Mbit Ethernet Management ports. One Connectivity Management Processor (CMP) port. Two EIA/TIA-232 RJ232 serial RJ-45 ports - one each for Console and Auxiliary modem ports.' That is ten RJ-45s, and the master draws ten.
provenance.power: install guide - Table 23, row 'RSP-880 Card': 425 W at 27 C, 430 W at 40 C, 450 W at 55 C. max is the highest rated ambient. Table 23 lists 'RSP880-LT Card' as a SEPARATE row at 285/295/315 W, so the two models are distinguished for power even though they share a data sheet and an envelope. Table 23 names the CARD, not the part number: its rows are 'RSP5 Card', 'RSP-880 Card', 'RP3 Card' and so on, with no -SE/-TR distinction anywhere in the table. So the figure below is carried on both variants of a card, which is transcription of Cisco's own scope rather than an inference across it. Contrast Table 35 for the line cards, which DOES split by variant and where the 16-port -TR and -SE differ by two thirds - that is why the scope of each table is worth stating.
provenance.relief: RELIEF IS DECLARED, AND WHAT MATTERS ABOUT IT IS THAT IT IS A HANDFUL OF NUMBERS AND NOT A HANDFUL PER PART. This face carries: 13 panel lamps at dome 0.3 (one number, carried by 120 Cisco contracts); 4 ejector brackets, their levers and the grip flanges at out 4.2 (one number, carried by 61 Cisco contracts); 2 captive screw heads at cyl 1.6 (one number, carried by 63 Cisco contracts); 2 pushbuttons at cyl 1.2 (one number, carried by 15 Cisco contracts). EVERY MAGNITUDE BELOW IS ESTIMATED, AND THAT IS A DELIBERATE READING OF WHAT RELIEF IS FOR. The owner's ruling: 'the whole 3d part is kind of interpolated anyway... It's just to give it a realistic view instead of just being a flat 2d... All of the 3d stuff is going to be mostly conjecture unless the vendor provides that data.' So a proudness here is an interpolation for a realistic view, NOT a claim about the hardware, and the confidence token on every feature says so rather than leaving it to be inferred. WHY `estimated` AND NOT `borrowed`, SINCE EVERY NUMBER HERE DOES COME FROM ANOTHER PORTRAYAL PART. `borrowed` is defined as another part's MEASURED figure reused for the same class of hardware, and these origins are not measured - they are the library's first guess at that hardware, and the contracts say so themselves: agr-panel-screw's provenance reads 'estimated - it stands proud but was not measured', agr-psu-dc sources its latch's ARRANGEMENT from a photograph and never its proudness, agr-fan describes its handle and grille by appearance only, and common/led-dot's entire provenance is 'size: estimated'. Spelling that chain `borrowed` would convert a guess into an apparent measurement at one remove, a thousand times over. `source` still names the origin, so the coordinating benefit is kept and only the claim that is not true is dropped. READ THE COUNTS ABOVE AS THEY ARE MEANT: a figure carried by sixty-odd contracts is ONE ESTIMATE WRITTEN SIXTY-ODD TIMES, not sixty-odd readings that happened to agree. One caliper on any one Cisco captive screw, any one ejector lever or any one panel lamp corrects every part in the library that shares it, which is the whole reason the numbers are pooled instead of chosen per card. THE SEARCH FOR A REAL FIGURE WAS RUN FIRST AND IS RECORDED SO IT IS NOT REPEATED: all 112 doc.md extracts for 'protrud', 'extends outward', 'stands proud' and 'clearance in front' - the only vendor in the intake that publishes a projection is UfiSpace, on the S9510-28DC; the per-card dimension tables, including Table A-10 of the older Ethernet Line Card Installation Guide which the current revision dropped, all of which carry H, W, D and weight only; and the ASR 9000 Visio stencil, whose 119 masters are FRONT and REAR elevations with no side, top or isometric view, so it holds no depth axis at all and is closed as a source. Figure 48 of the Ethernet Line Card Installation Guide and Figure 1-8 of the ISM guide DO show this hardware in three dimensions and are perspective drawings with a vanishing point, so they settle the ARRANGEMENT - bracket off the plate, lever along it, domed screw head proud of both - and nothing about size. STILL REFUSED ON THIS FACE, and these are NOT the same kind of gap: the 1 drawn aperture(s) alarm-out - an optical or connector aperture that conforms to no published standard, so no depth exists to interpolate from; led-matrix - an alphanumeric display whose glass may be flush or recessed and no figure says; usb-bezel, sfp-block - each would need an EIGHTH family number for one or two nodes, which buys a little realism at the cost of another invented figure; left flat deliberately. The ruling sanctions interpolating a PROUDNESS for a realistic view. It does not sanction inventing an APERTURE, which is a dimension a specification is withholding rather than one nobody has measured.
provenance.size: datasheet - Cisco ASR 9000 Route Switch Processor 880 Data Sheet, 'Physical specifications': Height 1.81 in. (4.60 cm), Width 16.87 in. (42.85 cm), Depth 24.74 in. (62.89 cm), Weight 17.8 lb (8.07 kg). That data sheet covers all four part numbers - A9K-RSP880-SE, -TR, A9K-RSP880-LT-SE and -LT-TR - with ONE physical block, so the LT variants take the same envelope from Cisco's own scoping rather than by inference. Note this card is 46.0 mm high where the RSP5 is 41.0: it is a thicker card, and a bay sized for one is not sized for the other.
