components.description: Cisco ASR 9000 SIP-700 SPA Interface Processor with 4 GB of memory. A carrier for shared port adapters rather than a port card: the faceplate is four SPA subslots in a two-by-two grid and a single Status lamp. Cisco: 'up to 2 single-width, double-height SPAs, up to 4 single-width, single-height SPAs, or up to 2 double-width, single-height SPAs. The Cisco ASR 9000 SIP-700 does not support double-width, double-height SPAs.' Supported on all ASR 9000 Series routers except the ASR 9906.
components.name: a9k-sip-700

provenance.accepts-is-singles-only: THE 22 SINGLE-WIDTH SPAs ARE LISTED AND THE TWO DOUBLES ARE NOT, and that is a limit of the bay model rather than a statement about the hardware. SPA-2XCHOC12/DS0 and SPA-1XCHOC48/DS3 occupy TWO SUBSLOTS SIDE BY SIDE - about 34.58 across against a subslot's 17.29 - and an occupant that spans two bays has no representation here: a bay holds one module sized to itself. Listing them would put a 34.58 part in a 17.29 opening and the drawing would lie. They are built and correct as components; what is missing is a way to say a module fills two bays. Note the guide names this class 'double-height' in Table 10 and 'double-width' in the SIP-700 chapter - one axis, two vocabularies, which is why the count of affected parts (2 of 24) matters more than either word.
provenance.bay-split: THE SPLIT DOWN THE MIDDLE IS MINE. The master draws only the two double-width panels, at 6.98, 27.71 and 6.98, 195.59, each 34.58 mm across and 167.87 and 165.47 mm long - those two bands are measured. Where the dividing line falls between the left and right subslots inside a band is NOT drawn, because the SPAs installed in the figure span both. It is taken as the middle. The guide supports halves rather than any other split - 'up to 4 single-width, single-height SPAs' in a 2 x 2 grid - but not the exact millimetre, and the printed numerals at x 21.19 and 37.42 fall on either side of that middle, which is consistent with it without proving it.
provenance.bays: install guide + drawing, AND THEY CORROBORATE EACH OTHER ON THE NUMBERING, which is the part worth setting out because SPA subslot numbering is not in reading order. The guide lists it flatly: 'Bay 2 (Top Left), Bay 0 (Top Right), Bay 3 (Bottom Left), Bay 1 (Bottom Right)'. The master prints all four numerals on its end flanges: '2' and '0' together at one end of the card and '3' and '1' at the other, and within each pair the 2/3 numeral sits at across-card x 21.19 and the 0/1 numeral at 37.42. So the master says {2,0} share one end, {3,1} the other, {2,3} one side and {0,1} the other - which is exactly the guide's Top/Bottom/Left/Right partition, with Top mapping to the low-y end and Left to the low-x side. Two sources, different media, same answer. IT ALSO FIXES WHICH CARD AXIS IS 'WIDTH': the guide captions its figure '2 double-width, single-height SPAs' and the master draws exactly two panels, each spanning the FULL 34.58 mm across the card at one position along it. So width runs across the card and height along it, and a single-width single-height subslot is half of one of those panels. The four bays here are those halves.
provenance.bays-were-inert-and-are-not: THIS WAS RECORDED AS INERT AND IS NO LONGER. Two things that were true when the geometry was written have both changed: component-level `bays:` is now read by render.py, which seats an occupant into a seated module's own bay, and 24 SPAs are now modelled from the SIP and SPA Hardware Installation Guide's Table 10. So `accepts` can name real parts and does.
provenance.blank-is-a-real-part-we-do-not-have: NO DEFAULT OCCUPANT IS SET, and the reason is a missing component rather than a missing decision. Cisco requires a filler: 'When a bay is not in use, a blank must fill the empty bay to allow the router or switch to conform to electromagnetic interference requirements... If you plan to install a SPA in a bay that is not in use, you must first remove the blank.' That blank is a real orderable part and this library has no component for it, so the four subslots render as openings. The guide gives it neither a part number nor a dimension in any section searched, so it is not buildable from what we hold. When somebody builds it, the `default` goes on these four bays the way a9k-mpa-blank goes on the MOD carriers' two.
provenance.capacity: install guide - Table 3, 'SIP Summary', names this part '20G SPA Interface Processor, 4 GB memory'.
provenance.chassis: install guide - 'Cisco ASR 9000 SIP-700 SIPs are supported on all Cisco ASR 9000 Series Routers.' ONE EXCEPTION IS STATED ELSEWHERE and is easy to miss because it is not in the SIP guide at all: the Overview and Reference Guide notes that 'The Cisco ASR 9906 supports A9K-VSM-500 and Tomahawk-based line cards; it does not support SIP-700'. Two Cisco books disagreeing, and the narrower statement is the one carried.
provenance.lifecycle: searched - no end-of-life notice for this part number is in the intake. Note the guide's own note that 'The ASR 9000 SIP-700 is not supported on Cisco IOS XR 64-bit images', which is a software limit rather than a lifecycle statement but is the nearest thing to one that the intake carries.
provenance.operating-temp: datasheet + install guide, AND THEY DISAGREE, so both are here. data_sheet_c78-573452, the Cisco ASR 9000 SIP-700 data sheet: 'Operating temperature (nominal): 41 to 104F (5 to 40C). Operating temperature (short-term): 23 to 131F (-5 to 55C).' The SIP and SPA Hardware Installation Guide's Table 6: 'Operating temperature 32 to 104F (0 to 40C)'. The ceilings agree at 40 C for continuous operation; the floors differ, 5 C against 0 C, and only the data sheet mentions a short-term range at all. attrs carries the data sheet's nominal range because it is the more conservative floor and the more completely specified pair.
provenance.power: datasheet - data_sheet_c78-573452, the Cisco ASR 9000 SIP-700 data sheet: 'Power: 375W (maximum)'. No typical and no ambient are given with it. AN EARLIER VERSION OF THIS COMPONENT SAID 'NOT STATED ANYWHERE IN THE INTAKE' and was wrong. What that sentence got right is that the SIP and SPA Hardware Installation Guide has no power table, Table 35 of the Ethernet Line Card guide has no SIP row, and Table 23 of the Overview and Reference Guide covers RSPs, RPs and fabric cards only - all three true, and all three about the wrong books. WHAT THE FIGURE COVERS IS NOT STATED and an earlier version of this sentence said it was. The sheet gives 375W maximum against the SIP and says nothing about whether the measurement was taken with SPAs seated or bare. It could be the populated carrier, in which case adding a SPA's draw would double-count, or the bare carrier, in which case a budget built from it is short by whatever the adapters take. NOTHING TURNS ON IT TODAY - no SPA is modelled in this library and none has a figure anywhere in the intake - but the day one does, this is the question to answer before the two are summed.
provenance.relief: RELIEF IS DECLARED, AND WHAT MATTERS ABOUT IT IS THAT IT IS A HANDFUL OF NUMBERS AND NOT A HANDFUL PER PART. This face carries: 1 panel lamps at dome 0.3 (one number, carried by 120 Cisco contracts). EVERY MAGNITUDE BELOW IS ESTIMATED, AND THAT IS A DELIBERATE READING OF WHAT RELIEF IS FOR. The owner's ruling: 'the whole 3d part is kind of interpolated anyway... It's just to give it a realistic view instead of just being a flat 2d... All of the 3d stuff is going to be mostly conjecture unless the vendor provides that data.' So a proudness here is an interpolation for a realistic view, NOT a claim about the hardware, and the confidence token on every feature says so rather than leaving it to be inferred. WHY `estimated` AND NOT `borrowed`, SINCE EVERY NUMBER HERE DOES COME FROM ANOTHER PORTRAYAL PART. `borrowed` is defined as another part's MEASURED figure reused for the same class of hardware, and these origins are not measured - they are the library's first guess at that hardware, and the contracts say so themselves: agr-panel-screw's provenance reads 'estimated - it stands proud but was not measured', agr-psu-dc sources its latch's ARRANGEMENT from a photograph and never its proudness, agr-fan describes its handle and grille by appearance only, and common/led-dot's entire provenance is 'size: estimated'. Spelling that chain `borrowed` would convert a guess into an apparent measurement at one remove, a thousand times over. `source` still names the origin, so the coordinating benefit is kept and only the claim that is not true is dropped. READ THE COUNTS ABOVE AS THEY ARE MEANT: a figure carried by sixty-odd contracts is ONE ESTIMATE WRITTEN SIXTY-ODD TIMES, not sixty-odd readings that happened to agree. One caliper on any one Cisco captive screw, any one ejector lever or any one panel lamp corrects every part in the library that shares it, which is the whole reason the numbers are pooled instead of chosen per card. THE SEARCH FOR A REAL FIGURE WAS RUN FIRST AND IS RECORDED SO IT IS NOT REPEATED: all 112 doc.md extracts for 'protrud', 'extends outward', 'stands proud' and 'clearance in front' - the only vendor in the intake that publishes a projection is UfiSpace, on the S9510-28DC; the per-card dimension tables, including Table A-10 of the older Ethernet Line Card Installation Guide which the current revision dropped, all of which carry H, W, D and weight only; and the ASR 9000 Visio stencil, whose 119 masters are FRONT and REAR elevations with no side, top or isometric view, so it holds no depth axis at all and is closed as a source. Figure 48 of the Ethernet Line Card Installation Guide and Figure 1-8 of the ISM guide DO show this hardware in three dimensions and are perspective drawings with a vanishing point, so they settle the ARRANGEMENT - bracket off the plate, lever along it, domed screw head proud of both - and nothing about size.
provenance.size: datasheet + install guide, and they say it two ways. THE DATA SHEET GIVES NUMBERS: data_sheet_c78-573452, the Cisco ASR 9000 SIP-700 data sheet, 'Physical dimensions (H x W x D); weight: 14 x 1.72 x 20.5 in.; 14 lb' - 355.6 x 43.7 x 520.7 mm and 6.35 kg, the original generation's envelope exactly. The INSTALL GUIDE gives the same fact by reference: Table 6, 'Cisco ASR 9000 SIP-700 Physical Specifications', says 'Physical dimensions: Occupies one line card slot on a Cisco ASR 9000 Series Aggregation Services Router' and no numbers at all. 355.6 is the PLATE; the component carries 395.7, the ejector-inclusive step every original-generation card in this library uses and which Cisco's own sheets write as 15.58 in where the plate is 14.5. Depth 520.7 is the sheet's own 20.5 in. AN EARLIER VERSION OF THIS COMPONENT modelled no depth at all, on the reasoning that 'occupies one line card slot' fixes the opening and not how far back the card reaches. That reasoning was sound and the conclusion was unnecessary - the number was stated in a data sheet I had not found.
provenance.status-lamp: install guide - Table 32, 'Port Status and Line Card Status LEDs', of the Ethernet Line Card Installation Guide, section 'Card Status LED (one per card)'. Green: 'Line card has booted properly, and is ready to pass or is passing traffic.' Steady amber: 'Line card boot process is underway. When the Cisco IOS XR software finishes loading, the LED turns green.' Blinking amber: 'Software configuration error has occurred that prevents the line card from passing traffic. It is possible that the line card is still passing traffic, but there is some degradation.' Red: 'Line card has encountered a hardware error, and is not passing traffic.' Off: 'Line card is powered off. The LED might turn off momentarily when switching between the states described above, although the line card has not powered off.' Steady and blinking amber share one colour and are not carried as two states; the distinction is recorded here because it is the difference between a card booting and a card misconfigured. A SIP IS NOT AN ETHERNET LINE CARD, so the scope needs a licence and Cisco gives one explicitly: the SIP and SPA Hardware Installation Guide carries the note 'References to line cards in the router hardware installation and configuration guides apply equally to SIPs.' That sentence is what makes Table 32 this card's table rather than a neighbour's. An earlier version of this component said the guide gave the lamp's existence and no colour table and carried a flagged BORROWING; the colour table was in the other book, which that note points at.
provenance.variants: install guide - 'There are two types of Cisco ASR 9000 SIP-700 available; A9K-SIP-700 and A9K-SIP-700-8G. A9K-SIP-700 supports 4 GB of memory. A9K-SIP-700-8G supports 8 GB of memory. BOTH TYPES ... ARE IDENTICAL IN APPEARANCE and can be identified by the PID located on the faceplate of the SIP.' That last clause is why both are modelled from the one master: Cisco says the faceplates differ in exactly one thing, the printed PID, and that is the only thing that differs between these two components.
provenance.weight: datasheet - data_sheet_c78-573452, the Cisco ASR 9000 SIP-700 data sheet gives '14 lb' with the physical dimensions, which is 6.35 kg and is the CARD. The install guide's Table 6 gives 'Shipping weight 10kg (22 lbs)', which is the card plus its packaging. Both are Cisco's and they are not the same quantity; attrs carries the card at 6.35 and this sentence is the record of the other, so that nobody later reads the two as a contradiction.

components.description: Line card and RSP/RP blank filler for a Cisco ASR 9000 modular chassis. A plain plate on the line-card envelope with a captive installation screw at each end and nothing else on it. It is a functional part, not trim: the installation guide is explicit that "unoccupied card slots must have a blank filler card installed for electromagnetic compatibility (EMC)", and the high-density 100GE cards additionally require the two-screen A9K-LC-FILR-V2 in the slots around them "for optimal cooling and EMI". An empty slot in a real chassis has one of these in it.
components.name: a9k-slot-cover

provenance.cutouts: NONE. A blank is unpunched by definition, which is the entire point of the part.
provenance.depth: ESTIMATED, and deliberately shallow. A blank has no body behind its face - it is a plate with a stiffening flange - so 25 mm is plate-plus-flange and NOT the 604.5 mm a line card occupies. No document states it. This is the one number here that a source would improve.
provenance.purpose: install guide - the Ethernet Line Card Installation Guide's removal procedure ends "If the line card slot is to remain empty, install a line card blank (Product Number A9K-LC-FILR) to keep the chassis dust free and to maintain proper airflow", and the Hardware Installation Guide carries the EMC caution. The Overview and Reference Guide lists "Line card and RSP blank fillers" among the chassis's own field-replaceable units, which is what makes this a bay occupant rather than decoration.
provenance.relief: RELIEF IS DECLARED, AND WHAT MATTERS ABOUT IT IS THAT IT IS A HANDFUL OF NUMBERS AND NOT A HANDFUL PER PART. This face carries: 2 captive screw heads at cyl 1.6 (one number, carried by 63 Cisco contracts). EVERY MAGNITUDE BELOW IS ESTIMATED, AND THAT IS A DELIBERATE READING OF WHAT RELIEF IS FOR. The owner's ruling: 'the whole 3d part is kind of interpolated anyway... It's just to give it a realistic view instead of just being a flat 2d... All of the 3d stuff is going to be mostly conjecture unless the vendor provides that data.' So a proudness here is an interpolation for a realistic view, NOT a claim about the hardware, and the confidence token on every feature says so rather than leaving it to be inferred. WHY `estimated` AND NOT `borrowed`, SINCE EVERY NUMBER HERE DOES COME FROM ANOTHER PORTRAYAL PART. `borrowed` is defined as another part's MEASURED figure reused for the same class of hardware, and these origins are not measured - they are the library's first guess at that hardware, and the contracts say so themselves: agr-panel-screw's provenance reads 'estimated - it stands proud but was not measured', agr-psu-dc sources its latch's ARRANGEMENT from a photograph and never its proudness, agr-fan describes its handle and grille by appearance only, and common/led-dot's entire provenance is 'size: estimated'. Spelling that chain `borrowed` would convert a guess into an apparent measurement at one remove, a thousand times over. `source` still names the origin, so the coordinating benefit is kept and only the claim that is not true is dropped. READ THE COUNTS ABOVE AS THEY ARE MEANT: a figure carried by sixty-odd contracts is ONE ESTIMATE WRITTEN SIXTY-ODD TIMES, not sixty-odd readings that happened to agree. One caliper on any one Cisco captive screw, any one ejector lever or any one panel lamp corrects every part in the library that shares it, which is the whole reason the numbers are pooled instead of chosen per card. THE SEARCH FOR A REAL FIGURE WAS RUN FIRST AND IS RECORDED SO IT IS NOT REPEATED: all 112 doc.md extracts for 'protrud', 'extends outward', 'stands proud' and 'clearance in front' - the only vendor in the intake that publishes a projection is UfiSpace, on the S9510-28DC; the per-card dimension tables, including Table A-10 of the older Ethernet Line Card Installation Guide which the current revision dropped, all of which carry H, W, D and weight only; and the ASR 9000 Visio stencil, whose 119 masters are FRONT and REAR elevations with no side, top or isometric view, so it holds no depth axis at all and is closed as a source. Figure 48 of the Ethernet Line Card Installation Guide and Figure 1-8 of the ISM guide DO show this hardware in three dimensions and are perspective drawings with a vanishing point, so they settle the ARRANGEMENT - bracket off the plate, lever along it, domed screw head proud of both - and nothing about size.
provenance.screws: drawing - one captive installation screw at each end, at the same positions the line cards carry theirs (centres 24.5 and 387.4 mm down the envelope), which is what lets a blank and a card share a slot's screw holes. The stencil draws no ejector levers on the blank, and none are drawn here: a filler is pulled out by its screws, not levered.
provenance.size: drawing - the stencil's "A9K Slot Cover" master, read the way the line cards were: its own shape box is the same padded 1.72 x 14.75 in every card master carries and is not the part, while the art measures a plate of 42.05 x 362.24 mm inside a 395.7 mm envelope. provenance.variants: TWO part numbers exist and they are NOT modelled separately, because no document here draws the difference. A9K-LC-FILR is the original; A9K-LC-FILR-V2 is described only as the one "that ha[s] two screens", required beside the 4-port and 12-port 100GE cards. Nothing states where those screens sit, how big they are, or what the plate looks like around them, so drawing them would be invention. The plain plate here is the A9K-LC-FILR as the stencil draws it, and the V2's screens are an open gap - a photograph would close it.

components.description: Cisco ASR 9006 Router fan tray. Six axial 92 mm (3.62 in) fans behind a perforated face, secured by a single captive screw and aligned on two guide pins. The ASR 9006 carries two of these for redundancy, side by side above the card cage and BEHIND A HINGED DOOR - which is why, uniquely in this family, no drawing of this tray exists anywhere: on the chassis master you see the door, not the tray.
components.name: asr-9006-fan

provenance.cages: composed from std/. RJ-45s are std/rj45-ganged (12.7 x 11.0) rather than std/rj45 (16.0 x 14.0): the IEC single-port cutout will not fit twice across a 41 mm card and the drawn jack measures 12.81 x 10.83. Timing coax is std/smb; the USB is std/usb-a; SFP+ is std/sfp-ganged.
provenance.db9: the ALARM OUT connector is DRAWN, not composed, and it IS declared `class: cutout` - which is a reversal of what these components said until now and the reversal is the point. There is no std/ part for a D-subminiature DE-9, no `db9` key in spec/schemas/standards.yaml, and no document in this intake dimensions the panel opening; the geometry here is transcribed from the master. The earlier version withheld `class: cutout` on the reasoning that a cutout conforming to nothing would corrupt the aperture census L26 keeps. THAT WAS BACKWARDS. L26's own message ends 'if the dimension cannot be sourced yet, this warning is the record of that', and its docstring calls the rule a to-do list for std/ rather than an accusation. Withholding the declaration did not keep the census clean, it kept a real gap OUT of the one rule built to hold it - a count kept tidy by routing around the detector. So the cutout is declared, the L26 warning stands, and the register is one entry more honest. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: a `db9` key in standards.yaml carrying the D-sub panel cutout from MIL-DTL-24308 or its commercial equivalent, plus a std/db9 part. That is a real errand somebody can run, unlike the CFP family's, and nobody has run it. CONTRAST cisco/a9k-750w-dc, whose DC terminal block is correctly NOT a cutout: that is hardware bolted to the face rather than a hole punched in it, and the distinction is between a thing that needs an opening and a thing that does not.
provenance.family: these masters are NOT the one-drawing family the RSP5, RSP-880, RP3 and RSP4-S masters are. Each has its own jack column, its own lamp cluster and its own legends - the RSP-440's five upper jacks sit at 42.6, 60.6, 102.6, 121.0 and 139.4 mm where the RSP5's sit at 42.5, 60.4, 117.7 and a stacked pair at 139.3 - so every feature here is read off the master it belongs to. The port IDS come from the legends that master prints, matched by proximity and asserted unique, not from a table of mine: that is how ICS0/ICS1/TOD on the RSP-440 and nV Sync0/nV Sync1/TOD on the ASR-9922-RP came out different without anyone deciding they should.

The two are easy to conflate because they share an envelope to the millimetre - 46.0 x 428.5 x 628.9 - and differ by 4.2 kg and 151 W. provenance.cages: composed from std/. RJ-45s are std/rj45-ganged (12.7 x 11.0) rather than std/rj45 (16.0 x 14.0): the IEC single-port cutout will not fit twice across a 41 mm card and the drawn jack measures 12.81 x 10.83. Timing coax is std/smb; the USB is std/usb-a; SFP+ is std/sfp-ganged.
provenance.db9: the ALARM OUT connector is DRAWN, not composed, and it IS declared `class: cutout` - which is a reversal of what these components said until now and the reversal is the point. There is no std/ part for a D-subminiature DE-9, no `db9` key in spec/schemas/standards.yaml, and no document in this intake dimensions the panel opening; the geometry here is transcribed from the master. The earlier version withheld `class: cutout` on the reasoning that a cutout conforming to nothing would corrupt the aperture census L26 keeps. THAT WAS BACKWARDS. L26's own message ends 'if the dimension cannot be sourced yet, this warning is the record of that', and its docstring calls the rule a to-do list for std/ rather than an accusation. Withholding the declaration did not keep the census clean, it kept a real gap OUT of the one rule built to hold it - a count kept tidy by routing around the detector. So the cutout is declared, the L26 warning stands, and the register is one entry more honest. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: a `db9` key in standards.yaml carrying the D-sub panel cutout from MIL-DTL-24308 or its commercial equivalent, plus a std/db9 part. That is a real errand somebody can run, unlike the CFP family's, and nobody has run it. CONTRAST cisco/a9k-750w-dc, whose DC terminal block is correctly NOT a cutout: that is hardware bolted to the face rather than a hole punched in it, and the distinction is between a thing that needs an opening and a thing that does not.
provenance.family: these masters are NOT the one-drawing family the RSP5, RSP-880, RP3 and RSP4-S masters are. Each has its own jack column, its own lamp cluster and its own legends - the RSP-440's five upper jacks sit at 42.6, 60.6, 102.6, 121.0 and 139.4 mm where the RSP5's sit at 42.5, 60.4, 117.7 and a stacked pair at 139.3 - so every feature here is read off the master it belongs to. The port IDS come from the legends that master prints, matched by proximity and asserted unique, not from a table of mine: that is how ICS0/ICS1/TOD on the RSP-440 and nV Sync0/nV Sync1/TOD on the ASR-9922-RP came out different without anyone deciding they should.
provenance.identity: this is the card Table 23 calls the 'RP Card', NOT the RP2. The RP2 is A99-RP2-SE/-TR with its own data sheet (Cisco ASR 9900 Route Processor 2) and its own Table 23 row at 390/400/410 W, and it has no stencil master. The two are easy to conflate because they share an envelope to the millimetre - 46.0 x 428.5 x 628.9 - and differ by 4.2 kg and 151 W. The weight is what separates them here: 13 lb on the RP sheet against 17.8 lb on the RP2's.
provenance.lamps: install guide - Table 4 for the RSP cards and Table 5 for the RP, transcribed per lamp with Cisco's own sentence kept beside the state tokens. WHICH lamp is where is read off this master's own printed legends and matched by position - the RSP-440 has six lamps in two columns and the ASR-9922-RP has eight in three, and neither was assumed from the other. Where a master draws a lamp with NO legend beside it that lamp is not modelled: the ASR-9922-RP has three such, almost certainly the External and two Internal USB lamps Table 4 describes - but almost certainly is not a source, so they are left out and this sentence is the record of them.
provenance.layout: drawing - the Cisco Visio master, scaled to the datasheet's own overall dimensions. index.json's shape box is the Visio drawing box, not the card - it reads 1.73 x 14.75 in for every control-card master - so the ART is the ruler and the box is not, the same correction the line cards needed. provenance.lifecycle: searched - no end-of-life notice for this part number is in the intake.
provenance.power: install guide - Table 23 of the Overview and Reference Guide, row 'RP Card': 227 W at 25 C, 251 W at 40 C, 259 W at 55 C. max is the highest rated ambient. NOT the 'RP2 Card' row's 390/400/410 - see `identity`. provenance.relief: RELIEF IS DECLARED, AND WHAT MATTERS ABOUT IT IS THAT IT IS A HANDFUL OF NUMBERS AND NOT A HANDFUL PER PART. This face carries: 8 panel lamps at dome 0.3 (one number, carried by 120 Cisco contracts); 4 ejector brackets, their levers and the grip flanges at out 4.2 (one number, carried by 61 Cisco contracts); 2 captive screw heads at cyl 1.6 (one number, carried by 63 Cisco contracts); 2 pushbuttons at cyl 1.2 (one number, carried by 15 Cisco contracts). EVERY MAGNITUDE BELOW IS ESTIMATED, AND THAT IS A DELIBERATE READING OF WHAT RELIEF IS FOR. The owner's ruling: 'the whole 3d part is kind of interpolated anyway... It's just to give it a realistic view instead of just being a flat 2d... All of the 3d stuff is going to be mostly conjecture unless the vendor provides that data.' So a proudness here is an interpolation for a realistic view, NOT a claim about the hardware, and the confidence token on every feature says so rather than leaving it to be inferred. WHY `estimated` AND NOT `borrowed`, SINCE EVERY NUMBER HERE DOES COME FROM ANOTHER PORTRAYAL PART. `borrowed` is defined as another part's MEASURED figure reused for the same class of hardware, and these origins are not measured - they are the library's first guess at that hardware, and the contracts say so themselves: agr-panel-screw's provenance reads 'estimated - it stands proud but was not measured', agr-psu-dc sources its latch's ARRANGEMENT from a photograph and never its proudness, agr-fan describes its handle and grille by appearance only, and common/led-dot's entire provenance is 'size: estimated'. Spelling that chain `borrowed` would convert a guess into an apparent measurement at one remove, a thousand times over. `source` still names the origin, so the coordinating benefit is kept and only the claim that is not true is dropped. READ THE COUNTS ABOVE AS THEY ARE MEANT: a figure carried by sixty-odd contracts is ONE ESTIMATE WRITTEN SIXTY-ODD TIMES, not sixty-odd readings that happened to agree. One caliper on any one Cisco captive screw, any one ejector lever or any one panel lamp corrects every part in the library that shares it, which is the whole reason the numbers are pooled instead of chosen per card. THE SEARCH FOR A REAL FIGURE WAS RUN FIRST AND IS RECORDED SO IT IS NOT REPEATED: all 112 doc.md extracts for 'protrud', 'extends outward', 'stands proud' and 'clearance in front' - the only vendor in the intake that publishes a projection is UfiSpace, on the S9510-28DC; the per-card dimension tables, including Table A-10 of the older Ethernet Line Card Installation Guide which the current revision dropped, all of which carry H, W, D and weight only; and the ASR 9000 Visio stencil, whose 119 masters are FRONT and REAR elevations with no side, top or isometric view, so it holds no depth axis at all and is closed as a source. Figure 48 of the Ethernet Line Card Installation Guide and Figure 1-8 of the ISM guide DO show this hardware in three dimensions and are perspective drawings with a vanishing point, so they settle the ARRANGEMENT - bracket off the plate, lever along it, domed screw head proud of both - and nothing about size. STILL REFUSED ON THIS FACE, and these are NOT the same kind of gap: the 1 drawn aperture(s) alarm-out - an optical or connector aperture that conforms to no published standard, so no depth exists to interpolate from; led-matrix - an alphanumeric display whose glass may be flush or recessed and no figure says. The ruling sanctions interpolating a PROUDNESS for a realistic view. It does not sanction inventing an APERTURE, which is a dimension a specification is withholding rather than one nobody has measured.

components.description: Cisco ASR 9922 Router Switch Fabric Card, first generation. One switch fabric plane for an ASR 9922. components.name: asr-9922-sfc110

provenance.chassis: INFERRED FROM THE PART NUMBER, which is the weakest kind of source and is labelled as such. provenance.depth: NOT MODELLED. No document in the intake gives a fabric card's depth, and unlike the line cards there is no datasheet row to take it from. provenance.geometry: drawing - measured off this master and NOT inherited. provenance.one-face: ONE DRAWING, TWO PART NUMBERS, and that is a fact about the hardware rather than a shortcut. The stencil has a single 'A9K Power Module V2' master and there is no second one, because an AC and a DC version 2 module present the same face: on these trays the AC receptacles and the DC lugs are on the TRAY, not on the module, so the module's face is a vent field, a handle and three lamps either way. They are two components rather than two skins of one for the reason the AGR PSUs were: a skin cannot carry a different power figure, and 3000 W and 2100 W is the whole difference between these two.
provenance.power: datasheet - the Cisco ASR 9000 Series Aggregation Services Routers Data Sheet's ordering table, which is where the wattage finally becomes attributable to a PART NUMBER rather than to a power system: 'AC power supply, 3000W' against 'PWR-3KW- AC-V2'. That is power-OUTPUT-w, the supply side of the meter, not a draw. The Overview and Reference Guide corroborates it from the system side - 'four 2100 W DC power modules or 3000 W AC power modules in a single tray, 8400 W (DC) 12,000 W (AC)' - and the two multiply out exactly. This is the figure the generic a9k-power- module-v2 component could not carry, because with one drawing and two ratings there was nothing to attach it to; naming the part numbers is what resolves it.
provenance.relief: RELIEF IS DECLARED, AND WHAT MATTERS ABOUT IT IS THAT IT IS A HANDFUL OF NUMBERS AND NOT A HANDFUL PER PART. provenance.size: NO CISCO DOCUMENT IN THIS INTAKE STATES ANY SPA DIMENSION. THIS SENTENCE IS THE SAME SENTENCE ON ALL 24 SPA COMPONENTS: it is ONE derivation, not 24 measurements, and the next reader should count it once. Searches run before writing it: 'Physical dimensions', 'Physical specifications', 'dimension', 'weight', 'inches' and 'mm' across all 104 PDFs of the intake rendered to text, plus the SIP and SPA Hardware Installation Guide read end to end. What the guide has is Table 6, 'Cisco ASR 9000 SIP-700 Physical Specifications', whose 'Physical dimensions' row reads 'Occupies one line card slot on a Cisco ASR 9000 Series Aggregation Services Router' - a heading that promises coverage its row does not have. The SPA data sheet, data_sheet_c78-688005 'Cisco ASR 9000 Series Shared Port Adapter Support', is an ordering list: it points at a URL for specifications and gives none. WHAT THE NUMBER IS: the SIP-700's own subslot band, measured off Cisco's stencil master by whoever built library/components/cisco/a9k-sip-700 and recorded there as bays 17.29 x 167.87 mm. That is the OPENING this SPA seats in, and this library's convention (the note bay-size-vs-component-size.md under working/notes) is that a bay and its occupant carry the same envelope, so the occupant takes the band. THE HALVING IS A JUDGEMENT AND NOT MINE: the SIP-700's own provenance.bay-split says the divider between the left and right subslots is not drawn on the master and the middle was assumed. AND THE FIGURE DOES NOT AGREE WITH IT ALONG THE LONG AXIS. Scale each faceplate figure so its drawn plate is 167.87 mm and two independent standard apertures come out oversized: the SFP bezel opening reads 16.5 mm against SFF-8432's 14.5, and the ganged RJ-45 pitch on the 8-port T1/E1 SPA reads 17.9 mm against this library's measured 13.99. Scale the same figures by those apertures instead and the plate is 131 to 148 mm long - but the ACROSS axis then reads 16.3 to 16.9 mm against the band's 17.29, agreeing to 3 per cent. So the two axes disagree about which reading is right, and nothing in the intake settles it. The likeliest reconciliation is that the 167.87 band includes the SPA's end brackets and captive jackscrews, which every faceplate figure draws OUTSIDE the plate body, and the plate itself is nearer 145 mm - but that is a reading, not a measurement, and the number carried here is the band.

provenance.size: NO CISCO DOCUMENT IN THIS INTAKE STATES ANY SPA DIMENSION. THIS SENTENCE IS THE SAME SENTENCE ON ALL 24 SPA COMPONENTS: it is ONE derivation, not 24 measurements, and the next reader should count it once. Searches run before writing it: 'Physical dimensions', 'Physical specifications', 'dimension', 'weight', 'inches' and 'mm' across all 104 PDFs of the intake rendered to text, plus the SIP and SPA Hardware Installation Guide read end to end. What the guide has is Table 6, 'Cisco ASR 9000 SIP-700 Physical Specifications', whose 'Physical dimensions' row reads 'Occupies one line card slot on a Cisco ASR 9000 Series Aggregation Services Router' - a heading that promises coverage its row does not have. The SPA data sheet, data_sheet_c78-688005 'Cisco ASR 9000 Series Shared Port Adapter Support', is an ordering list: it points at a URL for specifications and gives none. WHAT THE NUMBER IS: the SIP-700's own subslot band, measured off Cisco's stencil master by whoever built library/components/cisco/a9k-sip-700 and recorded there as bays 17.29 x 167.87 mm. That is the OPENING this SPA seats in, and this library's convention (the note bay-size-vs-component-size.md under working/notes) is that a bay and its occupant carry the same envelope, so the occupant takes the band. THE HALVING IS A JUDGEMENT AND NOT MINE: the SIP-700's own provenance.bay-split says the divider between the left and right subslots is not drawn on the master and the middle was assumed. AND THE FIGURE DOES NOT AGREE WITH IT ALONG THE LONG AXIS. Scale each faceplate figure so its drawn plate is 167.87 mm and two independent standard apertures come out oversized: the SFP bezel opening reads 16.5 mm against SFF-8432's 14.5, and the ganged RJ-45 pitch on the 8-port T1/E1 SPA reads 17.9 mm against this library's measured 13.99. Scale the same figures by those apertures instead and the plate is 131 to 148 mm long - but the ACROSS axis then reads 16.3 to 16.9 mm against the band's 17.29, agreeing to 3 per cent. So the two axes disagree about which reading is right, and nothing in the intake settles it. The likeliest reconciliation is that the 167.87 band includes the SPA's end brackets and captive jackscrews, which every faceplate figure draws OUTSIDE the plate body, and the plate itself is nearer 145 mm - but that is a reading, not a measurement, and the number carried here is the band.

provenance.relief: RELIEF IS DECLARED, AND WHAT MATTERS ABOUT IT IS THAT IT IS A HANDFUL OF NUMBERS AND NOT A HANDFUL PER PART. EVERY MAGNITUDE BELOW IS ESTIMATED, AND THAT IS A DELIBERATE READING OF WHAT RELIEF IS FOR. The owner's ruling: 'the whole 3d part is kind of interpolated anyway... So a proudness here is an interpolation for a realistic view, NOT a claim about the hardware, and the confidence token on every feature says so rather than leaving it to be inferred. Spelling that chain `borrowed` would convert a guess into an apparent measurement at one remove, a thousand times over. `source` still names the origin, so the coordinating benefit is kept and only the claim that is not true is dropped. provenance.size: NO CISCO DOCUMENT IN THIS INTAKE STATES ANY SPA DIMENSION. THIS SENTENCE IS THE SAME SENTENCE ON ALL 24 SPA COMPONENTS: it is ONE derivation, not 24 measurements, and the next reader should count it once. Searches run before writing it: 'Physical dimensions', 'Physical specifications', 'dimension', 'weight', 'inches' and 'mm' across all 104 PDFs of the intake rendered to text, plus the SIP and SPA Hardware Installation Guide read end to end. What the guide has is Table 6, 'Cisco ASR 9000 SIP-700 Physical Specifications', whose 'Physical dimensions' row reads 'Occupies one line card slot on a Cisco ASR 9000 Series Aggregation Services Router' - a heading that promises coverage its row does not have. The SPA data sheet, data_sheet_c78-688005 'Cisco ASR 9000 Series Shared Port Adapter Support', is an ordering list: it points at a URL for specifications and gives none. WHAT THE NUMBER IS: the SIP-700's own subslot band, measured off Cisco's stencil master by whoever built library/components/cisco/a9k-sip-700 and recorded there as bays 17.29 x 167.87 mm. That is the OPENING this SPA seats in, and this library's convention (the note bay-size-vs-component-size.md under working/notes) is that a bay and its occupant carry the same envelope, so the occupant takes the band. THE HALVING IS A JUDGEMENT AND NOT MINE: the SIP-700's own provenance.bay-split says the divider between the left and right subslots is not drawn on the master and the middle was assumed. AND THE FIGURE DOES NOT AGREE WITH IT ALONG THE LONG AXIS. Scale each faceplate figure so its drawn plate is 167.87 mm and two independent standard apertures come out oversized: the SFP bezel opening reads 16.5 mm against SFF-8432's 14.5, and the ganged RJ-45 pitch on the 8-port T1/E1 SPA reads 17.9 mm against this library's measured 13.99. Scale the same figures by those apertures instead and the plate is 131 to 148 mm long - but the ACROSS axis then reads 16.3 to 16.9 mm against the band's 17.29, agreeing to 3 per cent. So the two axes disagree about which reading is right, and nothing in the intake settles it. The likeliest reconciliation is that the 167.87 band includes the SPA's end brackets and captive jackscrews, which every faceplate figure draws OUTSIDE the plate body, and the plate itself is nearer 145 mm - but that is a reading, not a measurement, and the number carried here is the band.

provenance.size: NO CISCO DOCUMENT IN THIS INTAKE STATES ANY SPA DIMENSION. THIS SENTENCE IS THE SAME SENTENCE ON ALL 24 SPA COMPONENTS: it is ONE derivation, not 24 measurements, and the next reader should count it once. Searches run before writing it: 'Physical dimensions', 'Physical specifications', 'dimension', 'weight', 'inches' and 'mm' across all 104 PDFs of the intake rendered to text, plus the SIP and SPA Hardware Installation Guide read end to end. What the guide has is Table 6, 'Cisco ASR 9000 SIP-700 Physical Specifications', whose 'Physical dimensions' row reads 'Occupies one line card slot on a Cisco ASR 9000 Series Aggregation Services Router' - a heading that promises coverage its row does not have. The SPA data sheet, data_sheet_c78-688005 'Cisco ASR 9000 Series Shared Port Adapter Support', is an ordering list: it points at a URL for specifications and gives none. WHAT THE NUMBER IS: the SIP-700's own subslot band, measured off Cisco's stencil master by whoever built library/components/cisco/a9k-sip-700 and recorded there as bays 17.29 x 167.87 mm. Scale each faceplate figure so its drawn plate is 167.87 mm and two independent standard apertures come out oversized: the SFP bezel opening reads 16.5 mm against SFF-8432's 14.5, and the ganged RJ-45 pitch on the 8-port T1/E1 SPA reads 17.9 mm against this library's measured 13.99. The likeliest reconciliation is that the 167.87 band includes the SPA's end brackets and captive jackscrews, which every faceplate figure draws OUTSIDE the plate body, and the plate itself is nearer 145 mm - but that is a reading, not a measurement, and the number carried here is the band.

provenance.power: NOT STATED. No document in this intake gives a power figure for any SPA: not the SIP and SPA Hardware Installation Guide, which has no power table at all; not data_sheet_c78-688005, the SPA data sheet, which is an ordering list; and not Table 35 of the Ethernet Line Card Installation Guide, whose rows are line cards and carriers. So no power-draw key is written and lint L27 stands - that warning is the record. AND THE SCOPE QUESTION IS OPEN AT THE OTHER END TOO: the SIP-700 states 375 W maximum without saying whether the measurement was taken with SPAs seated or bare, so a budget cannot be closed from this end either. provenance.relief: RELIEF IS DECLARED, AND WHAT MATTERS ABOUT IT IS THAT IT IS A HANDFUL OF NUMBERS AND NOT A HANDFUL PER PART. This face carries: 9 panel lamps at dome 0.3 (one number, carried by 120 Cisco contracts). EVERY MAGNITUDE BELOW IS ESTIMATED, AND THAT IS A DELIBERATE READING OF WHAT RELIEF IS FOR. The owner's ruling: 'the whole 3d part is kind of interpolated anyway... It's just to give it a realistic view instead of just being a flat 2d... All of the 3d stuff is going to be mostly conjecture unless the vendor provides that data.' So a proudness here is an interpolation for a realistic view, NOT a claim about the hardware, and the confidence token on every feature says so rather than leaving it to be inferred. WHY `estimated` AND NOT `borrowed`, SINCE EVERY NUMBER HERE DOES COME FROM ANOTHER PORTRAYAL PART. `borrowed` is defined as another part's MEASURED figure reused for the same class of hardware, and these origins are not measured - they are the library's first guess at that hardware, and the contracts say so themselves: agr-panel-screw's provenance reads 'estimated - it stands proud but was not measured', agr-psu-dc sources its latch's ARRANGEMENT from a photograph and never its proudness, agr-fan describes its handle and grille by appearance only, and common/led-dot's entire provenance is 'size: estimated'. One caliper on any one Cisco captive screw, any one ejector lever or any one panel lamp corrects every part in the library that shares it, which is the whole reason the numbers are pooled instead of chosen per card. provenance.relief: RELIEF IS DECLARED, AND WHAT MATTERS ABOUT IT IS THAT IT IS A HANDFUL OF NUMBERS AND NOT A HANDFUL PER PART. WHY `estimated` AND NOT `borrowed`, SINCE EVERY NUMBER HERE DOES COME FROM ANOTHER PORTRAYAL PART. `borrowed` is defined as another part's MEASURED figure reused for the same class of hardware, and these origins are not measured - they are the library's first guess at that hardware, and the contracts say so themselves: agr-panel-screw's provenance reads 'estimated - it stands proud but was not measured', agr-psu-dc sources its latch's ARRANGEMENT from a photograph and never its proudness, agr-fan describes its handle and grille by appearance only, and common/led-dot's entire provenance is 'size: estimated'. provenance.size: NO CISCO DOCUMENT IN THIS INTAKE STATES ANY SPA DIMENSION. THIS SENTENCE IS THE SAME SENTENCE ON ALL 24 SPA COMPONENTS: it is ONE derivation, not 24 measurements, and the next reader should count it once. Searches run before writing it: 'Physical dimensions', 'Physical specifications', 'dimension', 'weight', 'inches' and 'mm' across all 104 PDFs of the intake rendered to text, plus the SIP and SPA Hardware Installation Guide read end to end. What the guide has is Table 6, 'Cisco ASR 9000 SIP-700 Physical Specifications', whose 'Physical dimensions' row reads 'Occupies one line card slot on a Cisco ASR 9000 Series Aggregation Services Router' - a heading that promises coverage its row does not have. The SPA data sheet, data_sheet_c78-688005 'Cisco ASR 9000 Series Shared Port Adapter Support', is an ordering list: it points at a URL for specifications and gives none. WHAT THE NUMBER IS: the SIP-700's own subslot band, measured off Cisco's stencil master by whoever built library/components/cisco/a9k-sip-700 and recorded there as bays 17.29 x 167.87 mm. That is the OPENING this SPA seats in, and this library's convention (the note bay-size-vs-component-size.md under working/notes) is that a bay and its occupant carry the same envelope, so the occupant takes the band. THE HALVING IS A JUDGEMENT AND NOT MINE: the SIP-700's own provenance.bay-split says the divider between the left and right subslots is not drawn on the master and the middle was assumed. AND THE FIGURE DOES NOT AGREE WITH IT ALONG THE LONG AXIS. Scale the same figures by those apertures instead and the plate is 131 to 148 mm long - but the ACROSS axis then reads 16.3 to 16.9 mm against the band's 17.29, agreeing to 3 per cent. So the two axes disagree about which reading is right, and nothing in the intake settles it. The likeliest reconciliation is that the 167.87 band includes the SPA's end brackets and captive jackscrews, which every faceplate figure draws OUTSIDE the plate body, and the plate itself is nearer 145 mm - but that is a reading, not a measurement, and the number carried here is the band.

provenance.figure: install guide - THIS PART HAS NO FACEPLATE FIGURE OF ITS OWN. The guide draws Figure 23 at the shared section's figure and captions it for the sibling SPA-8XCHT1/E1; the layout here is that drawing with the extra ports removed, which is a REDUCTION and not a reading of this part. THIS SENTENCE IS SHARED BY ALL 24 SPA COMPONENTS and describes the drawings as a class. The faceplate figures are RASTERS embedded in the PDF at about 570 px across, which is roughly 2.7 px/mm at the plate scale used here, so no position below is better than about +/- 0.4 mm and none of them is stated more precisely than the millimetre. GATE 1, on the axis it can be run on: the drawn plate's thickness-to-length ratio is 0.107 against the 0.103 the SIP-700's subslot band implies, agreeing to 4 per cent, and a single-height plate and a double-height plate differ by the factor of two the guide's vocabulary requires - so the figures are orthographic and their FRACTIONS carry geometry. They do not carry absolute scale: see provenance.size. Every position on this component is therefore a fraction of the drawn plate mapped onto the band, and every standard aperture is placed at its measured CENTRE at the size the registry gives it rather than at the size the figure draws it.
provenance.form-factor: install guide - THIS PARAGRAPH IS SHARED BY ALL 24 SPA COMPONENTS. The guide uses TWO AXIS VOCABULARIES for one form factor and never reconciles them. Table 7 uses the opposite naming for the same shape: 'Double height single width SPA in Subslot 0, Bay 3', against a figure in which that SPA is the one spanning both levels across the card. Table 10, the supported-SPA list, is in TABLE 7's vocabulary - it calls SPA-2XCHOC12/DS0 double- height, and Figure 6 draws that part's plate at twice the thickness and the same length as a single. So: `double-height` in Table 10 and `double-width` in the SIP-700 prose are the SAME PHYSICAL THING, a plate about 34.58 mm across and the same length as a single, filling two subslots SIDE BY SIDE. The attrs key here is written in the SIP-700 chapter's vocabulary, because that is the chapter the seating geometry comes from, and the drawing is what settles the shape. FOR THIS PART the sources agree on single-height: Table 10's row reads 'single-height' and the faceplate figure draws a single-height plate.
provenance.leds: install guide - Table 23, which the guide does not split between the two variants. The state vocabularies are transcribed from this part's own LED table, named in each element's description, and NOT from a sibling's - the SPA sections in this guide word the same lamp differently often enough that borrowing one would be a false citation.
provenance.lifecycle: searched - no end-of-life notice for SPA-8XCHT1/E1-V2 is in this intake. Table 10 gives this part a minimum IOS XR release of 5.1.1 and a minimum hardware revision of 1.0, which is a support floor and not a lifecycle statement.
provenance.ports: install guide - Table 10 gives this its own row - '8-Port Channelized T1/E1 SPA ... 8 T1/E1 ... single-height', minimum IOS XR 5.1.1 against the original's 4.1.0 - and the March 2014 change log records it as an addition. The guide has ONE section, ONE LED table and ONE faceplate figure for '8-Port Channelized T1/E1 SPA', and never says whether the V2's faceplate differs.. as the original: 'The E1 interface on the 8-Port Channelized T1/E1 SPA uses RJ-48c receptacles for E1 (120-Ohm) cables with RJ-45 connectors.'
provenance.power: NOT STATED. No document in this intake gives a power figure for any SPA: not the SIP and SPA Hardware Installation Guide, which has no power table at all; not data_sheet_c78-688005, the SPA data sheet, which is an ordering list; and not Table 35 of the Ethernet Line Card Installation Guide, whose rows are line cards and carriers. So no power-draw key is written and lint L27 stands - that warning is the record. AND THE SCOPE QUESTION IS OPEN AT THE OTHER END TOO: the SIP-700 states 375 W maximum without saying whether the measurement was taken with SPAs seated or bare, so a budget cannot be closed from this end either. See a9k-sip-700's provenance.power.
provenance.relief: RELIEF IS DECLARED, AND WHAT MATTERS ABOUT IT IS THAT IT IS A HANDFUL OF NUMBERS AND NOT A HANDFUL PER PART. This face carries: 17 panel lamps at dome 0.3 (one number, carried by 120 Cisco contracts). EVERY MAGNITUDE BELOW IS ESTIMATED, AND THAT IS A DELIBERATE READING OF WHAT RELIEF IS FOR. The owner's ruling: 'the whole 3d part is kind of interpolated anyway... It's just to give it a realistic view instead of just being a flat 2d... All of the 3d stuff is going to be mostly conjecture unless the vendor provides that data.' So a proudness here is an interpolation for a realistic view, NOT a claim about the hardware, and the confidence token on every feature says so rather than leaving it to be inferred. WHY `estimated` AND NOT `borrowed`, SINCE EVERY NUMBER HERE DOES COME FROM ANOTHER PORTRAYAL PART. `borrowed` is defined as another part's MEASURED figure reused for the same class of hardware, and these origins are not measured - they are the library's first guess at that hardware, and the contracts say so themselves: agr-panel-screw's provenance reads 'estimated - it stands proud but was not measured', agr-psu-dc sources its latch's ARRANGEMENT from a photograph and never its proudness, agr-fan describes its handle and grille by appearance only, and common/led-dot's entire provenance is 'size: estimated'. Spelling that chain `borrowed` would convert a guess into an apparent measurement at one remove, a thousand times over. `source` still names the origin, so the coordinating benefit is kept and only the claim that is not true is dropped. READ THE COUNTS ABOVE AS THEY ARE MEANT: a figure carried by sixty-odd contracts is ONE ESTIMATE WRITTEN SIXTY-ODD TIMES, not sixty-odd readings that happened to agree. One caliper on any one Cisco captive screw, any one ejector lever or any one panel lamp corrects every part in the library that shares it, which is the whole reason the numbers are pooled instead of chosen per card. THE SEARCH FOR A REAL FIGURE WAS RUN FIRST AND IS RECORDED SO IT IS NOT REPEATED: all 112 doc.md extracts for 'protrud', 'extends outward', 'stands proud' and 'clearance in front' - the only vendor in the intake that publishes a projection is UfiSpace, on the S9510-28DC; the per-card dimension tables, including Table A-10 of the older Ethernet Line Card Installation Guide which the current revision dropped, all of which carry H, W, D and weight only; and the ASR 9000 Visio stencil, whose 119 masters are FRONT and REAR elevations with no side, top or isometric view, so it holds no depth axis at all and is closed as a source. Figure 48 of the Ethernet Line Card Installation Guide and Figure 1-8 of the ISM guide DO show this hardware in three dimensions and are perspective drawings with a vanishing point, so they settle the ARRANGEMENT - bracket off the plate, lever along it, domed screw head proud of both - and nothing about size.
provenance.size: NO CISCO DOCUMENT IN THIS INTAKE STATES ANY SPA DIMENSION. THIS SENTENCE IS THE SAME SENTENCE ON ALL 24 SPA COMPONENTS: it is ONE derivation, not 24 measurements, and the next reader should count it once. Searches run before writing it: 'Physical dimensions', 'Physical specifications', 'dimension', 'weight', 'inches' and 'mm' across all 104 PDFs of the intake rendered to text, plus the SIP and SPA Hardware Installation Guide read end to end. What the guide has is Table 6, 'Cisco ASR 9000 SIP-700 Physical Specifications', whose 'Physical dimensions' row reads 'Occupies one line card slot on a Cisco ASR 9000 Series Aggregation Services Router' - a heading that promises coverage its row does not have. The SPA data sheet, data_sheet_c78-688005 'Cisco ASR 9000 Series Shared Port Adapter Support', is an ordering list: it points at a URL for specifications and gives none. WHAT THE NUMBER IS: the SIP-700's own subslot band, measured off Cisco's stencil master by whoever built library/components/cisco/a9k-sip-700 and recorded there as bays 17.29 x 167.87 mm. That is the OPENING this SPA seats in, and this library's convention (the note bay-size-vs-component-size.md under working/notes) is that a bay and its occupant carry the same envelope, so the occupant takes the band. THE HALVING IS A JUDGEMENT AND NOT MINE: the SIP-700's own provenance.bay-split says the divider between the left and right subslots is not drawn on the master and the middle was assumed. AND THE FIGURE DOES NOT AGREE WITH IT ALONG THE LONG AXIS. Scale each faceplate figure so its drawn plate is 167.87 mm and two independent standard apertures come out oversized: the SFP bezel opening reads 16.5 mm against SFF-8432's 14.5, and the ganged RJ-45 pitch on the 8-port T1/E1 SPA reads 17.9 mm against this library's measured 13.99. Scale the same figures by those apertures instead and the plate is 131 to 148 mm long - but the ACROSS axis then reads 16.3 to 16.9 mm against the band's 17.29, agreeing to 3 per cent. So the two axes disagree about which reading is right, and nothing in the intake settles it. The likeliest reconciliation is that the 167.87 band includes the SPA's end brackets and captive jackscrews, which every faceplate figure draws OUTSIDE the plate body, and the plate itself is nearer 145 mm - but that is a reading, not a measurement, and the number carried here is the band.

provenance.size: NO CISCO DOCUMENT IN THIS INTAKE STATES ANY SPA DIMENSION. THIS SENTENCE IS THE SAME SENTENCE ON ALL 24 SPA COMPONENTS: it is ONE derivation, not 24 measurements, and the next reader should count it once. Searches run before writing it: 'Physical dimensions', 'Physical specifications', 'dimension', 'weight', 'inches' and 'mm' across all 104 PDFs of the intake rendered to text, plus the SIP and SPA Hardware Installation Guide read end to end. What the guide has is Table 6, 'Cisco ASR 9000 SIP-700 Physical Specifications', whose 'Physical dimensions' row reads 'Occupies one line card slot on a Cisco ASR 9000 Series Aggregation Services Router' - a heading that promises coverage its row does not have. The SPA data sheet, data_sheet_c78-688005 'Cisco ASR 9000 Series Shared Port Adapter Support', is an ordering list: it points at a URL for specifications and gives none. WHAT THE NUMBER IS: the SIP-700's own subslot band, measured off Cisco's stencil master by whoever built library/components/cisco/a9k-sip-700 and recorded there as bays 17.29 x 167.87 mm. That is the OPENING this SPA seats in, and this library's convention (the note bay-size-vs-component-size.md under working/notes) is that a bay and its occupant carry the same envelope, so the occupant takes the band. THE HALVING IS A JUDGEMENT AND NOT MINE: the SIP-700's own provenance.bay-split says the divider between the left and right subslots is not drawn on the master and the middle was assumed. AND THE FIGURE DOES NOT AGREE WITH IT ALONG THE LONG AXIS. Scale each faceplate figure so its drawn plate is 167.87 mm and two independent standard apertures come out oversized: the SFP bezel opening reads 16.5 mm against SFF-8432's 14.5, and the ganged RJ-45 pitch on the 8-port T1/E1 SPA reads 17.9 mm against this library's measured 13.99. Scale the same figures by those apertures instead and the plate is 131 to 148 mm long - but the ACROSS axis then reads 16.3 to 16.9 mm against the band's 17.29, agreeing to 3 per cent. So the two axes disagree about which reading is right, and nothing in the intake settles it. The likeliest reconciliation is that the 167.87 band includes the SPA's end brackets and captive jackscrews, which every faceplate figure draws OUTSIDE the plate body, and the plate itself is nearer 145 mm - but that is a reading, not a measurement, and the number carried here is the band.

provenance.figure: install guide - Figure 18, '1-Port OC-192/STM-64 POS/RPR SPA Faceplate'. THIS SENTENCE IS SHARED BY ALL 24 SPA COMPONENTS and describes the drawings as a class. The faceplate figures are RASTERS embedded in the PDF at about 570 px across, which is roughly 2.7 px/mm at the plate scale used here, so no position below is better than about +/- 0.4 mm and none of them is stated more precisely than the millimetre. GATE 1, on the axis it can be run on: the drawn plate's thickness-to-length ratio is 0.107 against the 0.103 the SIP-700's subslot band implies, agreeing to 4 per cent, and a single-height plate and a double-height plate differ by the factor of two the guide's vocabulary requires - so the figures are orthographic and their FRACTIONS carry geometry. They do not carry absolute scale: see provenance.size. Every position on this component is therefore a fraction of the drawn plate mapped onto the band, and every standard aperture is placed at its measured CENTRE at the size the registry gives it rather than at the size the figure draws it.
provenance.form-factor: install guide - THIS PARAGRAPH IS SHARED BY ALL 24 SPA COMPONENTS. The guide uses TWO AXIS VOCABULARIES for one form factor and never reconciles them. The SIP-700 chapter says width for the axis across the card and height for the axis along it - 'The Cisco ASR 9000 SIP-700 supports a maximum of 2 single-width, double-height SPAs, 4 single- width, single-height SPAs, 2 double-width, single-height SPAs' - and Figure 2's caption, 'the Cisco ASR 9000 SIP-700 faceplate with 2 double-width, single-height SPAs', is drawn as two panels each spanning the full 34.58 mm across the card. Table 7 uses the opposite naming for the same shape: 'Double height single width SPA in Subslot 0, Bay 3', against a figure in which that SPA is the one spanning both levels across the card. Table 10, the supported-SPA list, is in TABLE 7's vocabulary - it calls SPA-2XCHOC12/DS0 double- height, and Figure 6 draws that part's plate at twice the thickness and the same length as a single. So: `double-height` in Table 10 and `double-width` in the SIP-700 prose are the SAME PHYSICAL THING, a plate about 34.58 mm across and the same length as a single, filling two subslots SIDE BY SIDE. The attrs key here is written in the SIP-700 chapter's vocabulary, because that is the chapter the seating geometry comes from, and the drawing is what settles the shape. provenance.leds: install guide - Table 17 gives six LEDs and the guide's own callout list names them in this order. provenance.barrel: drawing - the same sheet's side elevation, scaled against its own 2.5 mm maximum panel thickness (36 px/mm at 600 dpi). The 6.5 dia flange and the mating interface together stand about 2.0 mm proud of the panel front, which is why an MCX jack reads as a flush disc rather than a threaded stalk the way sma does
provenance.flat: the flat is drawn at the BOTTOM of the aperture. Nothing in the Radiall sheet fixes its clocking - a D-hole is punched to whatever orientation the panel drawing calls for - so a card that shows a different clocking should place this part with `rotate:` rather than have the flat re-cut here
provenance.size: standard - registry key `mcx`, from the MOUNTING HOLE inset of the Radiall R113.553.000 technical data sheet (MCX bulkhead jack receptacle, front mount, cylindrical contact; issue 9841B04). Bore dia 5.00/4.90, across the flat 4.55/4.45; w and h are the midpoints. Radiall originated MCX, so this is the series' own panel drawing rather than a derived figure. Corroborated by L-com LCCN3038, sold as fitting a ".177 inch D hole"
provenance.variant-is-front-mount-and-at-least-one-: THE 2.0 IS TRUE OF THIS VARIANT AND IS NOT TRUE OF EVERY MCX. It is read off a FRONT-MOUNT bulkhead jack, whose flange sits on the front of the panel - the sheet is named in `barrel` above and the registry entry says 'bulkhead front-mount panel hole' in as many words. This part is not wrong; it is specific, and the specificity was not stated where a reader would meet it. THE CASA CARDS THAT COMPOSE IT USE A VARIANT THAT DOES NOT PROTRUDE. The owner, looking at the hardware: the MCX connectors on the 6+12 I/O cards are RECESSED INTO the faceplate and do not stick out, where the F fittings on the US and DS I/O cards do. Figure 1-12 of the C40G guide shows both in one image - every F port a hex nut with concentric rings and a shadow, every MCX port on the neighbouring UPS IO 32 a flat dark circle with no body at all. So all five users of this part - casa/io-6p12, io-6p12-sw, io-6p12-io2, io-6p12-sw-io2 and ups-32x4 - draw about 774 barrels standing 2.0 proud that the hardware does not stand. NOTHING IS CHANGED HERE, DELIBERATELY. Flattening this part would make it wrong about the jack it documents and would silently re-point every future user at a shape nobody measured. What is missing is the Casa variant: a part number, or a Casa mechanical drawing, or one oblique photograph with a rule. Until then the mismatch is recorded on the Casa contracts where it applies rather than corrected here, and the direction is known - the error is PROUD-WHEN-IT-SHOULD-NOT-BE, not an unknown sign. Portrayal also has no way to express the recess itself: `sink` is the right word and is in the schema, but the extractor reads it only inside a node already carrying a depth, and `relief.cavity` on a module would make the whole card a cavity. That mechanism is not being built ahead of a number to put in it.

features.source: std/mcx@1's own barrel key - the Radiall R113.553.000 side elevation (issue 9841B04) scaled against its own 2.5 mm maximum panel thickness at 36 px/mm: flange plus mating interface stand about 2.0 proud. TRUE OF THIS FRONT-MOUNT VARIANT ONLY, as this contract's variant-is-front-mount key warns - a rear-mount MCX does not read as a flush disc.

UfiSpace S9510-28DC HIG, Space Clearance: 'the handle for the power supplies will extend outwards by 1.06 inches (2.7cm)'. 27 mm. CORRECTED FROM 25, which was the FAN handle's figure from the first half of the same sentence. THE FILE ALREADY HELD THE RIGHT NUMBER: this contract's own size key reads 'body 211mm, handle to 27mm proud'. That is not a second source corroborating this one - it is the same HIG read by whoever sized the part - but it does mean the contract stated 27 in one place and rendered 25 in another.
ufispace/psu-401-dc@1 - unsourced. Its size key reaches past the face to give 'body 211mm, handle to 27mm proud' and stops there; the terminal block's 8 mm is not in the HIG.
ufispace/psu-401-dc@1 - unsourced. The HIG's PSU FRU LED table gives the lamp's states and nothing about its lens. Same 0.4 as the fan and the AC PSU: one estimate written three times.
